title: feat(cloudflare): run submissions on Agents SDK Tasks
body:
> **Draft.** Depends on the Agents SDK release that carries [cloudflare/agents#2274](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/2274) (`step.signal`, `run({ deadline })`, `onError(error, run)`). The lockfile resolves `agents@0.23.0`, which does not yet have those; against it the Task handlers throw on `step.signal`. Bump the range once the release lands and this is ready for review.

## What

Flue's Cloudflare target already extends the Agents SDK `Agent` class; this replatforms its execution layer onto the SDK's `Tasks` capability and deletes the hand-rolled supervision: the zero-delay drain plus 30s heartbeat on `schedule()`, the in-isolate supervisor chain, detached `runFiber` attempt fibers with `onFiberRecovered`, deadline enforcement over live fibers with a 60s force-settle grace, and the `__flueWakeAgentSubmissions` schedule target.

Two Task definitions are declared on the generated class via `taskDefinitions` (resolved by the SDK on every wake, so replay is correct by construction):

- **`flue:drive@v1`** — one bounded reconcile pass: materialize unready rows, finalize pending settlements, recover interrupted running rows, claim runnable heads, start an attempt run per claim, complete. One run id per object; every former "arm the drain" boundary (admission, abort, `onStart`, attempt settlement, Task failures) ensures it and joins a live one for free.
- **`flue:attempt@v1`** — one submission processed to settlement in the handler body. The flue abort controller is linked to `step.signal`; the submission's durability timeout is the run's `deadline`. The SDK owns the claim backstop that survives eviction, replays the run on a fresh isolate after an interruption (the body reconciles from stream evidence first, then processes the replacement attempt), and settles over a signal-deaf attempt at the deadline, fencing its later writes; the next drive settles the submission through the existing timeout classification.

Unchanged: the submission ledger (now the inbox), the canonical stream, admission and dispatch paths, `processSubmission`, `reconcileInterruptedSubmission`, the extension mechanism, and the `alarm()` context wrapper for extension-authored schedule callbacks.

Behavior change worth knowing: abort of an attempt that ignores its signal now settles at the submission timeout rather than after a fixed 60s grace. Stale `__flueWakeAgentSubmissions` schedule rows from earlier deploys log `callback not found` once and complete.

`@flue/runtime` still never imports `agents`: the Tasks surface is typed structurally, as before.

## Verification

`pnpm check:types` and `biome lint` are green (knip's unused-export findings are pre-existing on `main`). Against a local build of the agents PR branch, `examples/cloudflare` under `vite dev` with the Workers AI binding:

- single prompt settles `completed`;
- two prompts back to back: the second joins the running response at a turn boundary, both settle `completed`;
- `POST /abort` mid-response settles `aborted`;
- killing the dev server mid-response and restarting: the SDK replays the attempt run (attempt 2), flue claims a replacement attempt, the partial is closed out, the response completes and settles, and the non-retained Task rows are gone from `cf_agents_task_runs`.

title: fix(runtime): use newline separators for Cloudflare sandbox readdir
body:
`cfSandboxToSandbox().readdir` ran `find … -printf '%f\0'` and split stdout on NUL. When NUL bytes do not survive the exec hop, every listing collapses into one concatenated entry, which is what the issue reports from production.

Switch to newline separators. `find` still includes dotfiles; the only trade-off is that a filename containing a newline now splits wrongly, versus every multi-entry listing being wrong today.

Closes #644

Validation:

- Repro wraps a mock sandbox whose `exec` runs the real command through `bash -c` and strips NUL from stdout (with a control pass that keeps NUL), over a fixture directory with dotfiles. Run against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Main with NUL stripped: 1 entry, `delivery-reportskills-a.agents.envconventional-commitsAGENTS.md`. Main with NUL kept: 6 correct entries.
- Branch: 6 correct entries in both passes, dotfiles included.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

Where NUL is lost: not in `@cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.4`'s client. Non-streaming `exec()` is a JSON POST and JSON escapes NUL as a unicode escape; the SSE parser splits only on newlines; the only sanitizer is log formatting. The container-side producer is not in the npm tarball, so the loss is most likely in the container's pipe decoding. Newline separators remove the dependency on NUL surviving whichever hop is lossy.

title: fix(runtime): admit undefined object properties in schema-less tool output
body:
A schema-less `useTool` whose `run()` returns different object shapes from different branches (`{ committed, alreadyCommitted }` vs `{ committed, factCount }`) fails to typecheck, and TypeScript reports only the last overload's error: "Property 'output' is missing … but required in type 'ToolDefinition'". Neither the shape mismatch theory on the issue nor that message is the cause. TypeScript unions the two literals by synthesizing `?: undefined` for the missing keys, and `JsonValue`'s index signature rejects `undefined`.

Add `JsonOutput`, `JsonValue` widened so object properties may be `undefined`, and use it for the schema-less `output` arm of `ToolRunEnvelope`. `undefined` properties are dropped by JSON serialization, so nothing changes at runtime, and the type only loosens, so no existing tool breaks.

Closes #617

Validation:

- Fixture typechecked with `tsc` against `packages/runtime/src` of a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Two-branch object return, no schema: main `error TS2769`, branch clean.
- `{ when: new Date() }` and `{ cb: () => 1 }` outputs: still `TS2769` on the branch.
- Schema-declared tool with matching output: clean on both. With wrong shape: `TS2769` on both.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

title: fix(sdk): reset observe() reconnect backoff after a healthy stream lifetime
body:
`observe()` increments `reconnectAttempt` on every `scheduleRetry` and only resets it when a chunk is applied. A quiet conversation whose live stream is closed on a schedule (or times out on the stale watchdog) therefore climbs 1s → 2s → 4s → … → 30s between reconnects even though every stream was healthy, so the first update after a long quiet period can be delayed up to 30s.

Record the stream's first activity in `armWatchdog` (called at open and on every delivered chunk), and before the three stream-lifetime retry paths (stale watchdog, unexpected end, transport error) reset the attempt counter if the stream lived at least `HEALTHY_STREAM_MS` (30s). The `updates()`-throws path and hydrate retries are untouched, so a server that refuses or immediately drops connections still escalates.

Closes #663

Validation:

- Repro uses a fake observation source with real timers, `Date.now` skewed to give a stream a 31s lifetime in ~20ms of wall clock, and measures the wall-clock gap between teardown and the next `history()` call. Run against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Healthy 31s stream closed by server ×4: main `[1s, 2s, 4s, 8s]`, branch `[1s, 1s, 1s, 1s]`. Same for healthy stream then transport error, and healthy stream then watchdog stall (timer delays divided by 20 so the 90s watchdog fires in 4.5s).
- Immediate drop with 0s lifetime, `updates()` throwing, and stall with no healthy lifetime: `[1s, 2s, 4s, 8s]` on both, escalation preserved.
- `pnpm check:types` green on `@flue/sdk`.

Note: "healthy" is measured from stream open (the first `armWatchdog` call), not from the first delivered chunk, matching the `openedAt` approach proposed on the issue.

title: fix(runtime): flush the first canonical delta after a quiet interval immediately
body:
`ConversationRecordWriter.enqueue` always armed a trailing 1s timer, so the first delta of every text block reached observers ~1s after `message_started`. The delay exists to coalesce mid-block deltas into fewer durable writes, but holding the very first delta buys nothing.

Track when the last flush started. When an append arrives and no flush has started within the coalescing window, flush on the next microtask instead of arming the timer; appends inside the window still coalesce on the trailing timer as before. The flush is scheduled rather than called inline so `pendingFlush` remains the promise handed back to the caller, and the existing `flushing` guard keeps it re-entrant.

This addresses the leading-edge half of the issue. Making the window configurable via `durability.streamFlushMs` is left for a follow-up: durability is resolved per session but the writer is created per instance in the coordinators, so that needs its own plumbing decision.

Closes #659

Validation:

- Repro unit-drives `ConversationRecordWriter` against `InMemoryConversationStreamStore`, replaying the session's streaming call sequence (`append(message_started)`, `append(text_started)`, `enqueue(delta) × N`, `flush()`), against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Main: first-delta latency 1001ms on both messages.
- Branch: 0ms on both. Deltas 1–5 still coalesce into a single later batch (~1044ms). Every `enqueue()` promise resolves with the offset of the batch that carried its record. No record is appended twice; 9 deltas produce 4 batches.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

Note: the quiet interval is measured from the last flush start, not the last enqueue. A block whose first delta arrives under 1s after the previous block's flush still waits the trailing timer, and per-record latency stays bounded at the window as on main.

title: fix(runtime): populate ModelRequestInfo.contextCompacted on agent turns
body:
`ModelRequestInfo.contextCompacted` is declared, consumed by both telemetry adapters, and documented as never populated. Nothing in `Session` ever set it.

`rebuildCanonicalContext()` is the single place the live context is reseeded from canonical records (on hydration and after every successful compaction), so it now records whether the conversation has a compaction. `emitTurnRequest` spreads `contextCompacted: true` only for `purpose === 'agent'`, so compaction and compaction-prefix turns never carry it and `false` is never emitted. The events reference doc drops its "not populated" caveat.

Closes #623

Validation:

- Repro drives two compactions on one conversation with pi-ai's `fauxProvider` and inspects the raw property on every `turn_request`, distinguishing absent from `false`. Run against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Main: all 11 turn requests have the property absent.
- Branch: the 3 agent turns before the first compaction are absent; the 6 agent turns after are `true`; both `compaction`-purpose turns are absent, including the second one, which runs while the conversation is already a compacted view. `false` never appears.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

title: fix(runtime): run threshold compaction after terminate-settled runs
body:
`runModelTurnWithRecovery` takes the trailing message as `assistant` for overflow/retry classification and reuses the same binding to gate `checkCompaction`. A run that settles through a tool returning `terminate: true` leaves a toolResult as the leaf, so `assistant` is `undefined` and the threshold check is skipped entirely. A conversation can then grow past the compaction threshold indefinitely as long as every run ends via a terminating tool.

Keep `assistant` as-is for overflow/retry, and for the threshold check fall back to the last assistant message in the live context. `checkCompaction` still early-returns on `aborted`/`error`, and the `findLast` only runs under `turnCompleted`, so it cannot pick up a stale assistant on the resume path. Moving the `rebuildCanonicalContext` condition to optional chaining is behaviour-preserving.

Closes #612

Validation:

- Repro on the real Node runtime with pi-ai's `fauxProvider`: two conversations are grown identically past a 2500-token threshold with compaction disabled, then compaction is enabled for one final dispatch. They differ only in how that run settles (plain assistant vs. a `terminate: true` tool). Run against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Main: control compacts (`compactionStarts: 1`); terminate-settled subject does not (`compactionStarts: 0`, no threshold log).
- Branch: subject logs `Threshold reached — 4000 tokens used, window 8000, reserve 5500` and completes one compaction. Both conversations accept a further dispatch afterwards.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

title: fix(runtime): stamp join ids on Cloudflare tracing child spans
body:
The Cloudflare tracing adapter stamped `flue.submission.id` and `flue.instance.id` on agent operation spans and `flue.task.id` on task spans, but no `flue.operation.id` anywhere and no `flue.turn.id` on model or tool spans. When durable work resumes in a later invocation and the owning span was never exported, child spans could not be joined back to their operation. `@flue/opentelemetry` already projects these ids through `identifiers()`.

Add `operationId` and `turnId` to `FLUE_ATTR` and stamp, exactly as the issue lists: `flue.operation.id` on agent operations; `flue.submission.id` and `flue.operation.id` on tasks; submission, operation and turn ids on model and model-tool spans; submission and operation ids on caller-shell spans. `writeAttributes` skips `undefined`, so nothing is emitted when an event lacks a value. No new spans, no renames, no reparenting, no `eventIndex` or harness/session identifiers.

Closes #624

Validation:

- Repro stubs `cloudflare:workers` so the adapter loads under Node with a recording span sink, then feeds `createCloudflareTracing()` the sequence operation_start(prompt) → turn_request → tool_start(model) → task_start → caller-origin bash tool_start under its own shell operation, against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- Main: the five spans carry none of the join ids (task has only `flue.task.id`).
- Branch: invoke_agent gains `flue.operation.id`; chat and execute_tool gain submission/operation/turn ids; the task span gains submission and operation ids without a turn id; the shell span gains submission and operation ids.
- Span names, parents and end state are identical between the two runs. No `flue.event.index`, `flue.harness.name` or `flue.session.name` appear.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

title: fix(runtime): preserve catalog compat for Cloudflare Anthropic gateway models
body:
`toAnthropicGatewayModel` built a fresh `compat` object with only the four binding overrides, and `gatewayCatalogModels` set `compat: undefined` before that, so pi-ai's gateway catalog flags never reached the serializer. For Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8, Sonnet 4.6 and Fable 5 the catalog carries `forceAdaptiveThinking: true` (and for Opus 4.7+ `supportsTemperature: false`), so every reasoning request through the Cloudflare binding sent `thinking: { type: 'enabled', budget_tokens }` and the API rejected it with a 400.

Spread `model.compat` before the binding overrides and stop nulling the catalog compat. The four overrides stay last and still win.

Closes #616

Validation:

- Repro drives `cloudflareBindingProvider().stream(...)` against a fake `env.AI` that records the payload and returns a minimal Anthropic-messages SSE stream, run against a clean `main` worktree (21c6240d) and this branch.
- `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` and `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` with reasoning: main sends `{"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":1024,"display":"summarized"}`; branch sends `{"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}`.
- `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` with `temperature: 0.7`: main forwards the temperature; branch omits it.
- Control `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` (no catalog flag): payload identical on both.
- Overrides still win: wire compat on the branch shows all four binding flags `false` despite the catalog's `sendSessionAffinityHeaders: true`; no `cache_control` or `eager_input_streaming` on tools; the `x-session-affinity` header is unchanged (it comes from `buildExtraHeaders`, not pi-ai).
- No other gateway compat flags change a payload: `supportsStrictTools`/`supportsToolReferences` are not in the catalog for any Anthropic model, and the only other entry (`supportsOpenAIGrammarTools` on `openai/*` Responses models) leaves the Responses payload byte-identical because flue builds that payload itself.
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check:types` green (109/109).

Not addressed here: the binding path still never sends `output_config.effort`, because flue registers its own `streamSimple` and pi-ai's `mapThinkingLevelToEffort` is bypassed. Adaptive without an effort is accepted by the API, so the 400 is gone, but `thinkingLevel` is still collapsed to on/off on this path.

title: feat: add Azure Sandboxes blueprint
body:
Add an Azure Container Apps Sandboxes blueprint so Node-hosted Flue applications can attach an existing Azure sandbox with `flue add sandbox azure` and `useSandbox(azure(client, sandboxId, { cwd }))`.

The generated adapter implements the existing `SandboxDriver` contract using `@azure/containerapps-sandbox@1.0.0-beta.1`. Applications retain ownership of provisioning, authentication, identity mapping, resume, retention, and cleanup. This adds documentation, navigation/catalog discovery, and executable checks of the TypeScript embedded in the blueprint; no runtime API or dependency changes are required.

Provider-specific behavior:
- Binary reads use base64 over shell execution because the preview SDK's file-read response handling can corrupt non-UTF-8 bytes.
- Command environments use quoted `env` arguments; deadlines use GNU `timeout` with a one-second TERM-to-KILL grace period. The sandbox image must provide the documented Linux utilities.
- File operations preserve metadata and recursive semantics; unsupported force deletion is rejected before mutation.
- Failed calls distinguish missing paths from unavailable sandboxes. Flue owns caller-facing cancellation. There is no background death polling, and cancellation may leave the remote command running.

Validation:
- `ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 pnpm check:types` — passed (109 tasks).
- `ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 pnpm build` — passed (59 tasks).
- Extracted adapter and agent example typechecked against the published Azure SDK and workspace runtime types.
- `node --test packages/cli/test/azure-sandbox.test.mjs` — 9 passed; GNU-timeout execution test skipped on macOS without coreutils.
- Blueprint index generation, CLI listing, docs build, and blueprint-serving website build passed; built Azure Markdown matched the source body.
- Formatting, scoped Biome checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

Draft pending a real Azure smoke test (filesystem operations, restart/reconnection, sandbox loss, and explicit cleanup) and execution of the GNU-timeout test on Linux. Workers compatibility and large-artifact transfers are not claimed.

Azure reference: https://sandboxes.azure.com/docs/sandboxes/quickstart/setup-typescript-sdk

This PR is submitted with awareness of the repository's contribution policy: external PRs may be automatically closed and converted to a feature-request discussion. The proposal is to let Azure users give Flue agents a provider-managed Linux workspace through the existing sandbox interface.

title: GenAI message fallbacks can emit invalid JSON or invalid message-array elements
Aborting during a partial tool batch causes record refusal and failure-assistant loop
body:
> _Originally reported by @zvsdev in [#672](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/672)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

When an abort occurs during the first of two sequential tool calls in a batch, the session produces only one result for two calls. The turn writer rejects this incomplete commit as a record refusal. Pi's failure assistant then starts while the batch is still open, which triggers a second record refusal. This leaves the session in a broken state where it cannot recover cleanly.

The error surfaces as:

```text
AssertionError: An abort must not emit a conversation record refusal.: expected [ …(1) ] to have a length of +0 but got 1
```

Affected file: `packages/runtime/src/session.ts`

### Expected Behavior

When an abort interrupts a partial tool batch, the incomplete batch should be filled with unknown-interruption results using the existing repair helpers and committed in full before the abort error is thrown. The session should then be able to resume cleanly on restart without triggering record refusals from Pi's failure assistant.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!-- Either starting from one of the examples in `examples/`, or from a basic hello world. -->

1. Set up an agent with two sequential tool calls in a single batch.
2. Abort the session (via the public `abort` API) while the first tool call is still executing.
3. Observe that the turn writer rejects the incomplete commit and Pi's failure assistant emits a record refusal.

---

Original implementation from [#672](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/672) by @zvsdev

title: Abandoned assistant messages from earlier submissions block new input
body:
> _Originally reported by @zvsdev in [#675](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/675)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

When an earlier submission leaves an open assistant message behind a later conversation tail, and the dispatch row for that submission is settled but its stream settlement is unavailable, the next input into the conversation fails. The conversation writer does not clear these verified abandoned messages before processing new input, causing subsequent prompts to error out even though the earlier dispatch has already been resolved.

This affects all persistence adapters (SQLite, libSQL/Postgres/MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis) and occurs in the default conversation within the runtime's conversation writer (`packages/runtime/src/conversation-writer.ts`).

### Expected Behavior

When a previous submission has left an abandoned assistant message in the conversation and its dispatch is already settled, new input should succeed. The runtime should detect and clear verified abandoned messages before processing the next input, preserving completed entries, raw history, tool results, and the active conversation tail.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!-- Either starting from one of the examples in `examples/`, or from a basic hello world. -->

1. Submit input to an agent session so that the submission begins producing an assistant message.
2. Allow the dispatch row for that submission to settle, but arrange for its stream settlement to become unavailable (e.g., an interrupted or crashed streaming response), leaving an open assistant message behind the conversation tail.
3. Submit new input to the same agent session and observe that the input fails.

---

Original implementation from [#675](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/675) by @zvsdev

title: Queued note acknowledgments can be lost when start hooks buffer signals before stream commit
body:
> _Originally reported by @zvsdev in [#676](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/676)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

Start hooks buffer signals before the stream commits. When a consumer deletes a queued note after `append()` returns, that note can be silently lost if another hook in the batch or the batch itself fails. The deletion happens outside the transaction boundary, so there is no rollback — the note is removed from the local queue but never committed to the stream.

This affects the local SQLite store in `packages/runtime`. The memory and async SQL stores are not impacted because they do not support acknowledgments.

### Expected Behavior

Queued note deletions should be atomic with the rest of the start-hook batch. If any hook or the batch commit fails, the deletion should roll back so the note remains in the queue and is not lost. Acknowledgments (row deletions) should occur inside the same transaction that stores signals, state writes, and the start marker.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!-- Either starting from one of the examples in `examples/`, or from a basic hello world. -->

1. Set up an agent with a start hook that calls `append(message)` to consume a note from a local SQLite queue, then deletes the corresponding queue row after `append()` returns.
2. Arrange for a subsequent hook in the same batch to fail (or for the batch commit itself to fail).
3. Observe that the queue row has been deleted but the appended message was never committed to the stream — the note is lost.

---

Original implementation from [#676](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/676) by @zvsdev

title: feat(runtime): expose safe failed recovery decisions (RUN-7644)
body:
Recovery can select budget or timeout failure, or catch a reconciliation error, without a distinct safe observer event. This adds `submission_recovery_decision` before terminal work and in the existing reconciliation catches, including the inner terminal-record catch. The event reports a choice or caught failure; the existing settlement record confirms the terminal result.

**Dependency: #674 at `14189f8c492dbb11c8ccde80070e76c2458f2747`.** This branch descends directly from its published branch, `zvs/run-7631-expose-committed-flue-submission-attempt-changes`. That commit stays unchanged. GitHub targets upstream `main`; the [RUN-7644-only diff](https://github.com/zvsdev/flue/compare/14189f8c492dbb11c8ccde80070e76c2458f2747...ead79d08fd22eceb5fceb52b8cda319d80101621) contains four production files, two sibling test files, and the events reference.

- Keep completion before abort, budget, and timeout. Keep attempt changes, queries, retries, execution, and settlement unchanged.
- Reuse the existing inspection snapshot. Missing submission fields and positions stay unknown.
- Copy safe name and Boolean platform flags from one cause entry, with at most four entries examined. Contain property failures, cycles, and subscriber failures. Copy no message, stack, body, request, or `errorInfo` detail.
- Preserve the separate PR675 cleanup hunk and RUN-7643 acknowledgment work.

Validation:

- All 64 runtime tests pass: 45 new regressions plus the 19 dependency regressions. Tests use both real coordinators and SQL stores. A real Session test compares retained transcripts, pending tool results, attempt counts, and settlement with reporting on and off, with no extra stream read.
- `pnpm check:types` passes all 109 workspace build/type tasks. The final runtime type check also passes.
- Biome passes all six changed TypeScript files. Prettier passes the new tests, public types, and event reference. Existing formatting outside the change stays intact. `git diff --check` passes.
- GitHub reports no required checks, status checks, automated reviews, or open review threads. The undrafted PR is CLEAN/MERGEABLE.
- `pnpm check` stops at the existing Knip listings: 48 unused development dependencies, 29 unused exports, and two unused exported types. These match the upstream-main limit recorded for #674.
- `pnpm test` stops at packages with no test files; this run first reports `@flue/redis`. The direct runtime suite passes. The repository-wide checks are not green, and this PR claims no waiver.

The complete fixer staff review covers correctness, design, privacy, tests, checks, and reader compatibility. It strengthens the raw-field access assertion, adds failed-settlement coverage, and removes unrelated formatting. No blocker, major, minor, or nit remains. Live delivery can still be lost during process failure; no stored delivery guarantee is added.

[RUN-7644](https://linear.app/runner-app/issue/RUN-7644/expose-safe-flue-failed-recovery-decisions), under RUN-5631. A future upstream release supplies diagnostic events only. It does not repair resets. Package publication and Runner adoption remain separate; this PR has no Runner deployment effect.

title: fix(runtime): commit local note acknowledgments with start signals
body:
Start hooks currently buffer signals before the stream commits. A consumer that deletes a queued note after `append()` returns can lose that note when another hook or the batch fails.

Add `append(message, { acknowledge: { table, key } })` to `AgentStartContext`. It validates and copies the row key while staging. The local SQLite store deletes that row in the transaction that stores the signals, state writes, and start marker. A failed deletion rolls back the batch. A committed producer-batch replay skips deletion, so a later row with the same key remains queued.

The optional store method makes support explicit. The memory and async SQL stores refuse acknowledgments. Calls without acknowledgments keep their existing path. Each key must select exactly one application row in the same SQLite database. No stored format, coordinator, submission policy, package version, or Runner consumer changes.

Validation:

- 27 maintained regressions pass through Node SQLite, the runtime, and a local fake model provider. They cover hook and batch failure, partial deletion rollback, staging and declaration order, key mutation, database reopen, lost commit response, key reuse, joined delivery, producer and submission checks, unsupported stores, and ordinary appends.
- `pnpm build` passes all 59 tasks. `pnpm check:types` passes all 109 tasks, including fresh dependency builds after the review fixes.
- Scoped Biome lint passes with five existing warnings in unchanged Session code. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm check` stops on existing Knip findings: 48 unused development dependencies, 29 unused exports, and two unused exported types. `pnpm test` stops on existing packages without test files, first `@flue/whatsapp`. The focused runtime suite passes.

The complete staff review in the implementing session is finished. The review fixed row-key parsing that could omit `constructor`, `prototype`, or `__proto__`, qualified SQL columns, and corrected type and style details. No findings remain. Cloudflare uses the same SQLite store; these regressions do not execute workerd. This repository has no current PR test workflow.

Related work: RUN-7643. PR #675 shares the writer and store methods. Later integration must keep its cleanup validation after the producer check and before the committed-batch lookup. Keep acknowledgment execution after that lookup, preserve its cleanup-versus-submission check, and retain `abandonedMessage` forwarding. PR #674 and the RUN-7644 diagnostics changes do not share these hunks.

title: fix(runtime): clear verified abandoned messages before new input
body:
An earlier submission can leave an open assistant message behind a later conversation tail. If its dispatch row is settled but its stream settlement is unavailable, the next input still fails.

Before processing input, the writer now drains pending writes and clears only verified messages in the default conversation. A dedicated record identifies the conversation, submission, and message. It records cleanup now without inventing an old outcome or attempt.

The append transaction checks the earlier unjoined dispatch, its sequence and settlement time, the current attempt, and the agent/session match. It keeps ordinary attempt checks and producer checks. It rejects mixed batches and changed targets. The reducer preserves completed entries, raw history, tool results, and the active tail. No tool runs, and the old submission row stays unchanged.

SQLite, libSQL/Postgres/MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis implement the checks. Old custom adapters and the transient memory store refuse cleanup without the transaction capability.

**Reader compatibility:** The new record uses version 2; fold checkpoints use version 3. New readers replay old records. Old readers reject cleanup records. Stop old raw-record readers before starting this version against shared storage. The existing client reset chunk carries the corrected snapshot. No database reset or format-stamp change occurs.

Validation:

- Full repository build and type checks: 110/110 tasks pass.
- Runtime/SQLite: 41 tests pass. libSQL, private Redis 8, and private MongoDB 8 replica set: 32 tests pass each.
- Tests cover two attempts, fresh reads, retry, input ordering, append failure, stale attempts, foreign sessions, and retained history/tool results.
- Changed TypeScript files pass lint; one warning remains in an unchanged reducer line.
- `pnpm check` reaches existing Knip listings: 46 unused dependencies, 28 exports, and 2 types. The full check is not green.
- Native Postgres/MySQL servers and Cloudflare execution are not tested here. Their builds and type checks pass.
- One complete session staff review is done; all change findings are fixed.

Tracking: RUN-7628. This PR has separate changes from PR672 and the RUN-7631 attempt-change events. Package publication and Runner adoption are separate work.

title: feat(runtime): observe committed submission attempt changes
body:
Observers cannot see the committed submission attempt until execution starts. This adds `submission_attempt_changed` to `observe()` immediately after a guarded claim or replacement returns, before execution starts.

- Cloudflare and Node use the existing contained coordinator emitter.
- Current IDs, count, kind, and budget come from the returned row. The prior snapshot stays unknown when a queued selection is stale.
- Rejected stale changes emit nothing. The existing recovery inspection supplies the stream offset without another query. Its pending-tool count stays unknown.
- Observer failures do not change execution. A process can stop between the store commit and event delivery; no replay or outbox is added.

Validation: 19 runtime regressions pass with real SQL claims and replacements on both coordinators. They cover stale selections, duplicate wakes, prior/current IDs, observer failures, and ordering before execution. The Session regression checks the existing offset without another stream read. All 59 workspace build tasks and all 109 type-check/build tasks pass. The changed files pass Biome with five existing warnings outside the changed lines.

The full `pnpm check` stops at Knip: 48 unused dependency listings, 29 unused exports, and two unused exported types. Upstream main `1ae1c85d` reproduces the same listings. The full `pnpm test` stops at `@flue/twilio` because that package has no test files; other existing packages report the same limit. The runtime suite passes when run directly.

GitHub reports no required checks, status checks, or automated reviews. Upstream main has no PR CI workflow. The repository-wide checks are not green; these limits remain explicit.

The full fixer staff review covers correctness, design, privacy, tests, repository checks, and reader compatibility. No blocker, major, minor, or nit remains in this change. The review fixes the test lease, write permission, type, and observer assertion gaps. It also removes unrelated formatting changes. The live delivery gap remains.

RUN-7631. This adds a live event, with no durable record or storage format change. The SQL guards, attempt budgets, scheduling, execution, recovery, and settlement stay as they are. Package publication and Runner adoption are separate work. This PR has no Runner deployment effect.

title: fix(runtime): complete aborted partial tool batches
body:
An abort during the first of two sequential tools can give Flue one result for two calls. The turn writer rejects that incomplete commit. Pi then starts its failure assistant while the batch is still open, which causes another record refusal.

The awaited `turn_end` subscriber now uses Pi's public abort signal. For the current submission's incomplete batch at the active leaf, it preserves stored outcomes and uses the existing repair helpers to add unknown interruption results. It commits the complete batch before publishing results and throwing the abort error. It also drops pending state writes and clears render and join tracking for that attempt.

Terminal cleanup reads committed repair IDs so a fresh Session keeps the interrupted tool IDs. The change preserves child references, repeated cleanup, and storage error propagation. It adds no package dependency or record type.

Validation uses public `start` / `init` / `dispatch` / `abort` / `read`, a faux provider, local SQLite, and the real conversation writer. Twelve tests cover normal, one-tool, pre-start, queued, interrupted-state, restart, repeated-cleanup, storage-failure, other-submission, and malformed-list cases.

The regression fails on the base and when the fix is removed:

```text
AssertionError: An abort must not emit a conversation record refusal.: expected [ …(1) ] to have a length of +0 but got 1
```

All 12 tests, runtime types, runtime build, affected-file lint, and formatting pass. Eight code mutations fail at the intended checks. Biome reports five existing optional-chain warnings. Runtime-filtered Knip fails with the same missing example dependencies and unused declarations on the base and this change.

Commands:

```sh
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime test --maxWorkers=1
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime check:types
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime build
pnpm exec biome lint packages/runtime/src/session.ts packages/runtime/src/session-abort.test.ts packages/runtime/src/session-terminal.test.ts packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts
pnpm exec prettier --check packages/runtime/src/session.ts packages/runtime/src/session-abort.test.ts packages/runtime/src/session-terminal.test.ts packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts
pnpm exec knip --workspace packages/runtime
```

The source and tests receive a staff self-review. This is not an independent maintainer review. No live provider call or package publication occurs. A skipped call remains an unknown external outcome. The change does not repair old stored sessions or change the coordinator's broader storage retry policy.

Tracking: [RUN-7611](https://linear.app/runner-app/issue/RUN-7611/complete-aborted-flue-tool-batches-before-failure-messages).

title: Dynamic model template synthesizes a zero-cost, zero-context model, so budgeting and accounting silently read 0
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

`Symbol.for('flue.dynamicModelTemplate')` lets a provider resolve ids no catalog knows. The synthesized value is `zeroMetadataModel(...)`: `cost` of 0, and no context window or reasoning metadata ("Zero-metadata Model literal for ids no catalog knows").

### Impact

Anything downstream that reads model metadata now reads plausible-looking zeros: per-turn cost lands at $0, and context budgeting has no window to budget against. Nothing warns. A host that adopts the escape hatch to unblock one model id can lose cost accounting for that model without noticing — we avoid the symbol entirely for this reason and synthesize `Model` literals ourselves.

### Proposal

Mark the synthesized model so consumers can tell it apart — a flag on the value, or a one-time warning when the template is used — and, if possible, leave `cost` undefined rather than 0 so "unknown" is distinguishable from "free".

title: Skill `allowedTools` is advisory: not enforced at runtime, and not documented as such
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

A skill can declare `allowedTools`, and nothing enforces it. The value is carried in the skill frontmatter type and surfaced to the model, but the runtime never restricts which tools the model may call while that skill is active.

### Why it matters

`allowedTools` reads like a capability restriction. We designed around it initially, assuming a skill marked as code-only could not reach other tools, and only found out by testing that the model can call anything the render declares. Our real guard is our own approval gate, so nothing was exposed — but a reader of the field name would reasonably conclude the opposite, and a host that trusts it has a hole it cannot see.

### Proposal

Either enforce it (filter the active tool set while the skill is open), or document it plainly as a hint to the model, in the field's own doc comment as well as the skills guide. We would prefer enforcement, but the documentation fix is the part that prevents a wrong assumption.

title: Projected parts drop chunk timestamps, so a UI cannot show how long reasoning took
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

#438 put server-authored `timestamp` on conversation stream chunks, but the parts projected by `@flue/sdk` / `@flue/react` do not carry it. A reasoning part is `{ type: 'reasoning', text, state }` — no time of any kind.

### Impact

Our chat shows elapsed time on tool rows but cannot on thinking rows, so a long reasoning block is just an animated shimmer with no indication of whether it has been 5 seconds or 4 minutes. The client can stamp `Date.now()` when it first sees a part, but that is the client's clock and it is wrong after a reload — a replayed history renders every part as if it happened now.

### Proposal

Project the chunk's `timestamp` onto the part (first-seen and completed would both be useful), or expose the raw chunk timestamps alongside the projection so a consumer can derive durations that survive a reload.

title: No model fallback within a submission: retries always go back to the same model
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

`useModel(model, { thinkingLevel })` takes exactly one model id, and a transient provider failure is retried against that same model. There is no candidate list and no hook to pick a different model for the next attempt.

### Impact

When one upstream model is degraded — not erroring cleanly, just slow or repeatedly failing — the submission burns its attempt budget on it and fails, even though an equivalent model would have answered. We implemented switching inside our own provider, which means our fallback logic lives below flue and is invisible to flue's own retry accounting and telemetry.

### Proposal

Either accept an ordered candidate list in `useModel`, or expose a hook that runs before a re-attempt and may return a different model id. Attribution would need to follow (the response metadata should say which model actually answered).

title: Attachments are image-only, so a PDF cannot be delivered to a model that accepts PDFs
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

`DeliveredAttachment = PromptImage & { filename?: string }`, and the type's own comment says: "Today the only supported attachment is an image." Models we run (for example `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` through a registered provider) accept PDF input, but there is no delivery shape that carries one.

### What we do instead

Files go to our own object storage, and the model reaches them through our tools. That works for a document pipeline, but it means a user who drops a PDF into a chat cannot simply have the model read it the way an image is read — we have to extract text first, and the extraction is lossy for scanned documents.

Note the second half of the wall: on the Cloudflare target `attachmentStore` is not injectable, so a host cannot swap in its own store to sidestep this.

### Proposal

Widen `DeliveredAttachment` to a file kind (`{ type: 'file', data, mimeType, filename }`) and pass it through to providers that declare support, leaving the existing image path untouched.

title: Delegated (task) child conversations have no public read surface
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

A `task` delegation creates a child conversation that is durably linked to the parent's tool call, but there is no supported way to read it. `AgentInstanceHandle` offers `dispatch` / `read` / `abort`; the child's conversation id is minted inside the execution store; the HTTP surface does not expose children. The only paths left are the store adapter (a Cloudflare-target internal) and raw SQL inside the generated DO class, whose canonical record shape is explicitly not a public contract.

### Why we want it

We show users what a delegated run actually did. Today we rebuild that from `observe()` events into our own ledger, which means the shape of our audit log depends on an event stream that can change, and nested delegation (flue allows depth 4) only ever yields one level — deeper children accumulate as unlinked rows.

### Proposal

A read-only handle for children of a submission or tool call: enough to list child conversation ids with their parent tool call, and to read a child's settled messages through the same public API used for a normal conversation. Write access is not needed.

title: Conversation stream carries no tool-input deltas: `toolcall_delta` is observable but never reaches SSE clients
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

`observe()` gained `toolcall_delta` in #450, but the conversation stream that browsers consume still has no equivalent. `ConversationStreamChunk` carries `message-delta` (text / reasoning) and `tool-input`, and `@flue/sdk`'s `appendToolInput` creates the part directly with `state: 'input-available'` — `'input-streaming'` does not exist in `FlueConversationPart`.

### Impact

When a model writes a long tool argument — for us, a document-generating script of a few thousand characters — the browser receives **nothing** for minutes. The last reasoning part stays `state: 'streaming'`, so the UI keeps claiming "thinking" long after thinking stopped. We measured 3–4 minutes of this on ordinary document-creation requests. The only client-side mitigation is to notice that reasoning has not grown for N seconds and reword the label, which is a guess about what is happening.

### Proposal

Surface the deltas that `observe()` already sees on the conversation stream: a `tool-input-delta` chunk, and an `input-streaming` state on the projected tool part so `@flue/react` consumers can render progress. Emitting only a byte/char count would already be enough to keep a UI honest.

title: Compaction: nothing tells the host it ran, and `CompactionConfig` cannot preserve host-owned state
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

Threshold compaction summarizes `messages` only, and the host cannot participate in it.

`CompactionConfig` exposes exactly three fields — `reserveTokens`, `keepRecentTokens`, `model`. There is no hook that fires when compaction runs, and no way to include host-owned state in what survives.

### What breaks for us

Our agent keeps a task plan in `usePersistentState()` and re-injects the unfinished items as a signal from `useAgentStart()`, which runs per delivery. That covers compaction between deliveries. It does **not** cover compaction that runs **in the middle of one long response** (for us: a delegation that fans out several `task` calls). `usePersistentState` is not a message, so the summary never carries it, and `useAgentStart` does not run again until the next delivery. The result is a response that continues with the plan gone from the model's context while the UI still shows it. Nothing errors.

`useAgentFinish` does not help — it runs at a would-stop, which is after the damage.

### Proposal

Any one of these would close it:

- A hook that fires when compaction is about to run / has run, so the host can re-append what must survive.
- Let the host contribute text to the summary (or mark a persistent-state slice as summary-preserved).
- `ModelRequestInfo.contextCompacted` being populated would at least let the host detect it after the fact — see #623.

Related: #612 (threshold compaction skipped when a run settles on a `terminate: true` tool result), #623.

title: observe(): reconnect backoff grows to its cap on a quiet conversation whose live stream is closed on a schedule
Cloudflare binding provider forces Anthropic prompt caching off, but env.AI.run() forwards cache_control
MCP connections: expose tool `annotations` (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint / ...)
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked).

### Summary

The MCP adapter drops tool `annotations`. In 2.0.4 the only read of the field is `tool.title ?? tool.annotations?.title` inside `createToolDescription`. No public type carries `annotations`, so `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint` never reach application code.

### Use case

We gate MCP tool calls on human approval, and whether a call needs approval depends on those hints. For example, read-only tools run directly while destructive ones require confirmation. The hints are unreachable through `createMcpConnection()` / `useMcpConnection()`, so we maintain our own MCP client instead of using flue's. That also means we cannot pick up improvements to flue's MCP integration.

### Proposal

Either of these:

- Carry `annotations` through to the generated tool definition, or expose it on a public per-tool metadata field, or
- Add a per-tool customization hook on the connection, for example `mapTool(mcpTool) => ToolDefinition | undefined`, so an application can wrap or filter tools and attach its own approval policy from the original `tools/list` entry.

title: Cloudflare target: allow a `locationHint` for agent Durable Objects
body:
**Version:** `@flue/vite` / `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked). Cloudflare target.

### Summary

Agent Durable Objects are always created without options, so an application cannot place them:

- `@flue/vite` generates `fetchAgent`, which calls `getAgentByName(binding, instanceId)` with no options object.
- `@flue/runtime`'s `routeToAgent` calls `rt.routeAgentRequest(request, env, { agentName, instanceId })`, again with no `locationHint`.

The lower layer already supports it: `partyserver`'s routing reads `options.locationHint`.

### Why it matters

A DO is created near the colo of **the first request that touches it**, and it stays there permanently. Our other per-tenant DOs use `locationHint: "apac"`. The agent DO that holds the conversation's execution state is the only one we cannot place, and that makes our data-residency statement asymmetric. A conversation whose first request arrives from a webhook, a CLI, or an MCP client abroad gets pinned far from its users, and the pinning is invisible.

### Proposal

Some per-agent or per-request hook, for example:

```ts
// agent module
export const placement = { locationHint: "apac" };
// or a resolver on the mount / router
createAgentRouter(agent, { locationHint: (req, instanceId) => "apac" });
```

The resolved value would then be threaded into both `getAgentByName` and `routeAgentRequest`. A `jurisdiction` option would fit in the same place.

title: Configurable `CANONICAL_FLUSH_DELAY_MS`, or flush the first delta immediately (first text is always ~1s late)
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked); measured on 2.0.3. Cloudflare target.

### Summary

`ConversationRecordWriter` coalesces streamed deltas for `CANONICAL_FLUSH_DELAY_MS = 1e3` before appending them to the durable stream. The constant is module-level, not exported, and not part of `FlueConfig`. The source comment already names the trade-off ("Lower = smoother live streaming … at the cost of more durable writes"), but applications cannot choose where they sit on it.

### Observed

We measured on the Cloudflare target with a real model through `@flue/sdk`:

- A 2,351-character answer arrived as 1,715 deltas packed into **15 SSE frames**.
- Frame intervals were fixed at **1,014–1,025 ms**, with 94–232 deltas per frame.
- The median delta was 1 character, so the model streams per token and the batching happens entirely in the writer.
- **`message-started` → first delta batch: 1,010 ms.** Every response's first visible text is delayed by about 1 s, and client-side smoothing cannot recover that.

### Proposal

Either of these would solve it for us:

- **Leading-edge flush:** flush the first delta of a block immediately, then coalesce the rest at the current cadence. Time-to-first-text improves and the write count barely changes.
- **Make the delay configurable,** for example `durability.streamFlushMs` or a `FlueConfig` field, so that latency-sensitive chat UIs can trade writes for smoothness.

title: Durable conversation stream grows without bound: per-token deltas in `flue_conversation_stream_batches` are never compacted or deleted
body:
**Version:** `@flue/runtime` 2.0.4 (source checked); observed in production-like use on 2.0.3. Cloudflare target.

### Describe the Bug

On the Cloudflare target, `flue_conversation_stream_batches` is append-only for the lifetime of an agent instance. In `@flue/runtime@2.0.4` the whole `dist/` contains exactly three `DELETE FROM` statements, and none of them targets this table (or `flue_agent_submissions`):

- `DELETE FROM flue_conversation_fold_checkpoints` (replacing a checkpoint)
- `DELETE FROM flue_conversation_fold_checkpoint_chunks` (replacing a checkpoint)
- `DELETE FROM flue_submission_chunks WHERE submission_id = ?` (`replace()` of the same submission)

Most of what is kept is streaming deltas. Measured across our local agent DOs (SQLite `dbstat`):

| What | Share of stored bytes |
| --- | --- |
| `flue_conversation_stream_batches` | 79.7% |
| + `flue_conversation_fold_checkpoints` | 93% combined |
| `assistant_reasoning_delta` records | 43.1% |
| `assistant_text_delta` records | 36.7% |

That puts roughly **64% of all stored bytes in per-token delta records**. Once the message settles, the same content also exists in the completed record (`assistant_text_completed` etc.).

### Why the host application cannot prune it

`seedReducedConversationState` treats the fold checkpoint as a disposable cache, not as a seal. It silently re-folds from the origin when any of these hold:

1. There is no checkpoint.
2. `formatVersion !== 2`.
3. The checkpoint is ahead of the `atOrBefore` offset.
4. The incarnation differs.
5. The checkpoint is ahead of the stream head.
6. The decoded state's offset disagrees with its recorded offset.
7. The checkpoint read throws.

`writeFoldCheckpoint` also only warns on failure, so an instance can end up with no checkpoint at all. If the host deletes batches at or below a checkpoint offset, every one of these fallbacks turns into **silent history loss**. There is no safe way for an application to reclaim the space.

### Impact

- A Durable Object is capped at 10 GB. Long-lived agents, and especially shared conversations with one instance and many writers, grow monotonically.
- Our workaround is to discard the instance's storage past 250 MB and re-seed it with a plain-text handoff message. That loses structured history and persistent state.

### Expected Behavior

One of these, or anything with the same effect:

- Compact the deltas of a **settled** submission once its completed records are durable, or
- Make the fold checkpoint a seal, and provide a supported retention / compaction API that deletes records at or below it, or
- A config option to not persist deltas at all, for applications that only need completed messages after settlement.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the Cloudflare target, any agent with a reasoning model, and `wrangler dev` / `vite dev`.
2. Run 20–30 turns with long responses in one conversation.
3. Open the agent DO's SQLite file under `.wrangler/state/v3/do/<...>/*.sqlite` and run:
   `SELECT name, SUM(pgsize) FROM dbstat GROUP BY name ORDER BY 2 DESC;`
4. `flue_conversation_stream_batches` dominates, and nothing ever shrinks it.

title: @flue/cli@2.0.4 and @flue/vite@2.0.4 published with workspace:* dependency specs — unresolvable for external consumers
body:
### Describe the bug

`@flue/cli@2.0.4` and `@flue/vite@2.0.4` were published with the pnpm workspace protocol left in their `dependencies`, which makes both packages unresolvable from any external registry consumer:

```
$ npm view @flue/cli@2.0.4 dependencies --json
{
  "@flue/runtime": "workspace:*",
  "@flue/vite": "workspace:*"
}

$ npm view @flue/vite@2.0.4 dependencies --json
{
  "@flue/runtime": "workspace:*"
}
```

pnpm errors on install:

```
Failed to resolve dependency: "@flue/runtime@workspace:*" is in the dependencies
but no package named "@flue/runtime" is present in the workspace
```

`@flue/cli@2.0.3` and `@flue/vite@2.0.3` declare exact versions (`"2.0.3"`) and install fine, so this looks like a publish-pipeline regression in 2.0.4 — the tarballs were likely published with a raw `npm publish` instead of `pnpm publish` (pnpm rewrites `workspace:*` specifiers at publish time).

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
npm view @flue/cli@2.0.4 dependencies --json
pnpm add @flue/cli@2.0.4   # or npm install @flue/cli@2.0.4 in a non-flue workspace
```

### Expected behavior

Published tarballs must not reference workspace packages. Publishing via `pnpm publish` (or a post-publish `publishConfig`/workspace-protocol rewrite) would resolve `@flue/runtime` and `@flue/vite` to real semver ranges.

### Versions

- `@flue/cli` 2.0.4 (broken), 2.0.3 (clean)
- `@flue/vite` 2.0.4 (broken), 2.0.3 (clean)
- pnpm 12.3.2 / npm latest

title: Cloudflare quickstart has incorrect vite.config.ts and missing "type": "module" in package.json, causing dev server failure
body:
> _Originally reported by @feliperyan in [#654](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/654)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

The Cloudflare deploy quickstart (`apps/docs/src/content/docs/ecosystem/deploy/cloudflare.md`) contains two errors that cause `npm run dev` to fail when following the guide as written:

1. The `vite.config.ts` example calls `cloudflare()` with no arguments, but `@flue/vite` requires the Cloudflare plugin to receive Flue's Worker config via `cloudflare({ config: flueWorkerConfig() })`. The doc comment claiming the Cloudflare target is auto-detected is incorrect. Without the config argument, a runtime error is thrown indicating the plugin isn't receiving the Worker config.

2. The `package.json` example omits `"type": "module"`. Without it, Vite loads `vite.config.ts` via `require()`, and since `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` is ESM-only, the dev server startup fails with a module resolution error.

*Reported via PR #<!-- number --> by @feliperyan.*

### Expected Behavior

Following the Cloudflare deploy quickstart as written should produce a working project where `npm run dev` starts the dev server successfully without runtime or module resolution errors.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Follow the Cloudflare deploy quickstart at `apps/docs/src/content/docs/ecosystem/deploy/cloudflare.md` exactly as written, including its `vite.config.ts` and `package.json` examples.
2. Run `npm run dev`.
3. Observe that the dev server fails to start — either with a runtime error from `@flue/vite` about the missing Worker config, or with an ESM resolution error from `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` due to the missing `"type": "module"` field.

---

Original implementation from [#654](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/654) by @feliperyan

title: docs: fix Cloudflare quickstart's vite.config.ts and package.json examples
body:
This PR corrects two mistakes in the Cloudflare deploy quickstart (`apps/docs/src/content/docs/ecosystem/deploy/cloudflare.md`) that reproduce a real `npm run dev` failure when following the guide as written.

- `vite.config.ts` example called `cloudflare()` with no arguments. `@flue/vite`'s own runtime error says the Cloudflare plugin isn't receiving Flue's Worker config unless you pass `cloudflare({ config: flueWorkerConfig() })`. The doc comment claiming the cloudflare target is auto-detected is wrong; updated the example and import to match.
- `package.json` example omitted `"type": "module"`. Without it, Vite loads `vite.config.ts` via `require()`, and `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` is ESM-only, so dev server startup fails with a resolution error. Added the field and a short explanatory note.

title: cfSandboxToSandbox().readdir splits on NUL, but Cloudflare sandbox exec strips NUL bytes from stdout
body:
## What happened

`@flue/runtime@2.0.3`'s Cloudflare sandbox adapter, `cfSandboxToSandbox().readdir` in `dist/cloudflare/index.mjs`, lists a directory with:

```js
async readdir(path) {
  const result = await guarded("readdir", sandbox.exec(`find ${shellQuote(path)} -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f\0'`));
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(`readdir failed for ${path}: ${result.stderr}`);
  return result.stdout.split("\0").filter((s) => s.length > 0);
}
```

The Cloudflare `@cloudflare/sandbox` Durable Object's `exec` strips NUL bytes from returned stdout, so a directory listing with more than one entry comes back as a single string with every filename concatenated together — there is nothing left in `stdout` to split on `"\0"`.

## Evidence (production, 2026-09-02, task `01M1FQ8DZ1SRDXWV6SPRA9R41M`)

```
sandbox.exec success find '/workspace/.agents/skills' -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f\0'
sandbox.exec success stat -L -c '%s/%Y/%F' '/workspace/.agents/skills/delivery-reportconventional-commits' && ...
sandbox.exec success find '/workspace' -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f\0'
sandbox.exec success ls /workspace; ... cat /workspace/AGENTS.md.agents 2>/dev/null | head -50
```

`/workspace/.agents/skills` actually contains two directories, `delivery-report` and `conventional-commits` (see `delivery/conventions.ts` in our repo, which writes both). Flue's skill discovery saw one concatenated name `delivery-reportconventional-commits`, the follow-up `stat` on that name failed, and neither skill was ever loaded. Separately, the model itself ended up reading a concatenated top-level listing and guessing at a nonexistent file `AGENTS.md.agents` (really two entries, `AGENTS.md` and `.agents`, joined together).

## Impact

Every agent using `cloudflareSandbox(...)` is affected, and specifically: skill auto-discovery over the Cloudflare sandbox adapter is silently broken whenever a directory being listed has more than one entry whose concatenation doesn't happen to `stat` successfully as one path (and even when it does, the wrong path is read).

## Suggested fix

Use a delimiter that survives the sandbox's `exec` transport — a newline works, since `find -printf '%f\n'` output split on `"\n"` (filtering empty lines) doesn't rely on NUL bytes surviving the round trip. A filename containing a literal newline is an edge case most callers can accept losing to the same degree the existing NUL-based approach already assumed it wouldn't occur in practice.

## Workaround

We've shipped a local wrapper around `cloudflareSandbox(...)` that overrides `readdir` with the newline-based version until a fixed `@flue/runtime` is available and pinned. See rp4rk/factori#364.

title: update boxd sandbox blueprint for @boxd-sh/sdk 0.2
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #62. `@boxd-sh/sdk` 0.2 (0.2.7 at time of writing) replaced the 0.1.x handle-based API the boxd blueprint was written against, so this updates the integration to the latest SDK:

- `blueprints/sandbox--boxd.md` bumped to **version 2**: adapter rewritten against the new API, prose updated (`@boxd-sh/sdk@^0.2.7`, `bxd_` key prefix, `machines.fork` tip), and a cumulative Upgrade Guide entry carrying the complete v1 → v2 unified diff per the `blueprints/README.md` contract. Validated with `generate-blueprint-index.ts`.
- `apps/docs/.../ecosystem/sandboxes/boxd.md` refreshed to match.

## What changed in the SDK

0.2 is a full API rewrite, not an incremental bump:

- Client is `Boxd` (was `Compute`); the stateful `Box` handle is gone in favor of a flat `client.machines.*` namespace whose methods take the machine id.
- File transfer moved to `machines.files.download` / `machines.files.upload`.
- Exec takes a params object (`{ command, env, timeout }`); the timeout option was renamed from `timeoutMs` to `timeout` (still milliseconds).
- Statuses renamed (`suspended`, `starting`, `migrating`, …); the terminal set the death detector keys on (`destroyed` / `failed` / `stopped`) is unchanged.
- Unary calls now carry a 60s client deadline, but exec streams still carry none — so the adapter's in-flight death-detector poll is still required and is kept.

## Adapter shape change

`boxd(box, { client })` becomes `boxd(client, machine, options?)`: the `Boxd` client is now a required first argument (every operation routes through it), so the death detector is always active instead of opt-in via `options.client`. The machine can be passed as the `Machine` record or its id. `cwd`, `readyTimeoutMs`, the `/home/boxd` default, and all `SandboxDriver` behavior are unchanged. The Upgrade Guide diff covers existing installs.

## Verification

- Blueprint index generator validates the version-2 contract (frontmatter, marker, cumulative Upgrade Guide with unified diff) and regenerates the index with `boxd` at version 2.
- The verbatim adapter file typechecks cleanly (`tsc --noEmit`) against `@boxd-sh/sdk@0.2.7` and `@flue/runtime`.
- Exercised end to end against a real boxd production VM through Flue's `Sandbox` interface (the same surface a model-invoked tool drives): 23/23 checks — readiness probe on a fresh machine, default cwd `/home/boxd`, shell coverage (compound commands, pipes, redirects, env forwarding with quoting, stderr/exit codes), file APIs including a binary round-trip via `machines.files`, `stat`/`readdir`/`exists`/`mkdir`/`rm`, exec `timeout` enforcement, and the death detector rejecting with `SandboxDiedError` ~5s after the machine was deleted mid-exec.
- Full agent loop verified with `flue run`: an agent using the generated adapter created a machine, the model called its sandbox tool, and all checks passed on the VM.

## Test plan

- [x] `generate-blueprint-index.ts` passes and lists `boxd` at version 2.
- [x] Adapter typechecks against `@boxd-sh/sdk@0.2.7`.
- [x] End-to-end against a real boxd VM (direct `Sandbox` interface + full `flue run` loop).
- [ ] After website rebuild on merge, `https://flueframework.com/cli/blueprints/boxd.md` serves the version-2 body.

title: Add a post-settlement hook for persisting the final agent response
body:
## Context

When embedding a Flue-built agent in an application, the host application may need to persist or otherwise process the agent's final output in its own domain storage after the response has completed.

For example, an application may want to call its own API from `useResponseFinish` to save the final agent response, update domain state, or trigger an application-level integration.

## Problem

`useAgentFinish` is intended for response continuation and may run before the response is actually final. A response can contain multiple model turns when `append()` is used, so it is not a reliable lifecycle point for persisting the final agent output.

However, there does not appear to be a `useResponseFinish` hook (or equivalent host-side completion callback) that runs after the response has settled and exposes the final assistant output. This means application code must currently reconstruct the final response from conversation state or implement an external polling/callback mechanism.

## Proposed capability

Provide a response-completion hook, such as `useResponseFinish`, that:

- runs only after the response is settled;
- exposes the final assistant output/text (including the response's complete output across continuation turns);
- preserves the existing durable/retry semantics;
- optionally exposes response metadata, usage, and tool-call aggregates;
- documents whether external side effects in the hook are at-least-once and how applications should make them idempotent.

A host-side completion API for submitted/dispatched responses could also solve this use case, if that is the preferred architectural boundary.

## Why this matters

Without a first-class completion seam, applications cannot reliably save the final agent output to their own domain model at the point Flue considers the response complete. This is especially important for applications where the agent's response must be persisted alongside domain records or used to trigger downstream processing.

## Implementation offer

I would be happy to implement this if the maintainers are open to it. I can prepare the implementation around the preferred API boundary (a `useResponseFinish` hook or a host-side completion API), including the durable/retry and at-least-once semantics. Please let me know which direction you would prefer before I start.

## Related

- #380 — Support required side-effect completion for `dispatch()`
- #286 — Expose a terminal result/state observation path for dispatched agent runs

Those issues cover required external side effects and observing dispatched runs, respectively. This issue focuses on a post-settlement lifecycle hook or equivalent API for host application persistence of the final agent output.

title: @flue/runtime: normalize Workers AI assistant content null without hiding malformed content
body:
## Package

`@flue/runtime@2.0.3`, Cloudflare Workers AI binding provider.

## Reproduction

Use a binding-backed model with an OpenAI-compatible streaming response whose
first assistant delta is a valid tool-call preamble:

```json
{
  "choices": [
    { "delta": { "role": "assistant", "content": null } }
  ]
}
```

The OpenAI/Workers AI contract permits `content: null` when an assistant turn
has no text (for example, a tool-call-only turn). Responses with other runtime
values, such as an object or array in `delta.content`, are malformed.

## Expected behavior

- Treat `content: null` (and an omitted content field) as no text delta and
  continue processing tool calls.
- Reject other non-string content values with a clear provider error instead of
  silently dropping the malformed response.

## Proposed fix

Normalize the assistant delta at the binding boundary: return an absent text
delta for `null`/`undefined`, accept strings, and throw for all other runtime
types. A focused provider test should cover both the valid null shape and an
invalid non-string shape.

This matters because the provider parses binding responses manually rather than
using the upstream OpenAI stream parser. The current main branch
(`832ad2ee`, published as 2.0.3) ignores `null`, but also silently ignores
malformed non-string values because the TypeScript type is not a runtime guard.

title: @flue/vite: parse JSX markdown importers and delegate external skill registries
body:
## Package `@flue/vite@2.0.3` with Vite 8.x. ## Reproduction 1. Create a `.tsx` module containing a type-only import and JSX, and a static `.md` import: ```tsx import type { Props } from './props'; import instructions from './instructions.md'; export const view =
{instructions}
; ``` 2. Build with the Flue Vite plugin. The markdown transform calls `parserLangForFile('view.tsx')`, but the current implementation returns `js`. The parser then rejects valid TSX syntax. A second independent reproduction occurs when another Vite plugin owns a virtual skill registry. Given an importer ID such as `\\0agents:skills:/workspace/src/skills` that reaches a resolved `/workspace/src/skills/example/SKILL.md`, Flue's markdown resolver throws `Skill import ... reached resolution untransformed` instead of delegating the edge to the plugin that owns the virtual namespace. ## Expected behavior - `.tsx` and `.jsx` files are parsed with the corresponding JSX-aware parser. - A `SKILL.md` import from an explicitly external virtual registry is left for that registry's resolver; Flue should keep rejecting genuinely untransformed Flue imports from ordinary JS/TS importers. ## Proposed fix The smallest fix is to map `.tsx` → `tsx` and `.jsx` → `jsx` in `parserLangForFile`, and return `null` from the markdown resolver only when the importer starts with `\\0agents:skills:`. A focused test can cover both cases without depending on a particular application. The current main branch (`832ad2ee`, published as 2.0.3) still reproduces both failures.
