title: vite dev fails to start on the Cloudflare target: published @flue/runtime chunks break Vite's dep optimizer
body:
`vite dev` usually fails to start on the Cloudflare target once a project has a handful of dependencies — it is a race, so a lucky run occasionally survives. It fails while Vite's dependency optimizer is still discovering them, referencing one of `@flue/runtime`'s own pre-bundled chunks:

```
Error: The file does not exist at ".../node_modules/.vite/deps_<worker>/dispatch-nU3cIlT--CvpinuCR.js"
which is in the optimize deps directory. The dependency might be incompatible with the dep optimizer.
Try adding it to `optimizeDeps.exclude`.
```

The chunk named varies with what the project imports: `providers-*.mjs` in a bare scaffold, `dispatch-*.mjs` and `instrumentation-*.mjs` in a project that uses `dispatch()` and a custom provider.

`vite build`, `wrangler deploy` and `flue run` are all unaffected — this is only the dev server.

## Reproduction

The bare scaffold is not sufficient on its own — see the matrix below — so add a realistic dependency set:

```sh
npx @flue/cli@2.0.3 init probe --target cloudflare
cd probe
npm install @octokit/rest @slack/web-api @earendil-works/pi-ai valibot
npx vite dev
```

Fails identically with npm, bun and pnpm.

## What decides whether it reproduces

Not the package manager, but how many dependencies the optimizer has to discover:

| project | npm / bun | pnpm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare `flue init --target cloudflare` | fails | works |
| the same plus the deps above | fails | fails |

The optimizer discovers the Worker's dependencies in waves at startup (~6 in the project above). Each wave triggers a re-optimize and a reload, each re-optimize re-hashes the shared chunks, and each reload invalidates the previous cache generation while the Worker still holds a reference to it. A bare scaffold finishes discovery in few enough passes to usually survive; a project with a few imports usually does not. pnpm's symlinked layout appears to shift the timing enough to save the small case, which makes it look like a fix until you add dependencies.

Also relevant: `examples/cloudflare` resolves `@flue/runtime` as `workspace:*`, so it never exercises the published package's chunked `dist/` at all.

## Environment

Reproduces across every combination tried, always from a clean `node_modules`, `.vite`, `.wrangler` and `dist`:

| axis | values |
| --- | --- |
| OS | macOS 15 arm64, Linux aarch64 (`node:24-slim` container) |
| Node | 22.22.1, 24.16.0, 24.18.0, 24.19.0 |
| package manager | npm 10, bun 1.4.0, pnpm 11.20.0 |
| vite | 8.0.14 (as scaffolded), 8.2.2 |
| @cloudflare/vite-plugin | 1.39.2 (as scaffolded), 1.53.1 |
| @flue/runtime, @flue/vite, @flue/cli | 2.0.3 |

## What does not fix it

- `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['@flue/runtime', '@earendil-works/pi-ai']`
- `optimizeDeps.include` naming every dependency by package name — fails on an additional chunk instead, because package names alone miss the subpath and lazy entries (see the fix below: an *exhaustive* include list does work)
- `noDiscovery: true` scoped to the Worker environment (`environments.<worker>.optimizeDeps`) — and I now know why: `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` returns `optimizeDeps: { noDiscovery: false, ... }` from its `configEnvironment` hook, and hook-returned config merges over user config, so the option is silently reverted. Verifiable with `resolveConfig`: set `noDiscovery: true` in user config, the resolved Worker environment shows `false`. Forcing it to stick via a later plugin's `configEnvironment` doesn't help either — an unoptimized transitive CJS dependency then throws `exports is not defined` at startup, so the no-optimizer path is dead regardless
- `vite optimize --force` as a pre-warm: it only optimizes the `client` environment (`node_modules/.vite/deps`), never `deps_<worker>`
- downgrading vite and `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` to the scaffolded versions
- switching package manager or Node major

## What does fix it

Pre-declaring the Worker's *entire* dependency graph — subpath exports, `.lazy` entries, and dynamic-import-only targets included — so the optimizer's first pass is final and there is never a re-optimize to invalidate anything:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [flue(), cloudflare({ config: flueWorkerConfig() })],
  environments: {
    <worker_name>: {
      optimizeDeps: {
        include: [
          "@flue/runtime",
          "@flue/runtime/internal",
          "@flue/runtime/routing",
          "@flue/runtime/cloudflare",
          "@flue/runtime/cloudflare/internal",
          "@flue/runtime/cloudflare/workers-ai",
          "@flue/slack",
          "@earendil-works/pi-ai",
          "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-completions.lazy",
          "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/anthropic-messages.lazy",
          "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-completions",
          "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-prompt-cache",
          "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-responses-shared",
          // ...plus the project's own dependencies
        ],
      },
    },
  },
});
```

To derive the list for a given project: start `vite dev` once and collect every specifier from the `dependencies optimized: ...` log lines, then add the bare dynamic-import targets the log can't see up front:

```sh
grep -rhoE 'import\("[^.][^"]*"\)' node_modules/@flue node_modules/@earendil-works
```

(That grep is what surfaces `openai-prompt-cache` and `openai-responses-shared`, which only load on the first model call and would otherwise trigger a mid-session re-optimize.)

Verified stable over repeated cold starts — zero re-optimizes, and a full agent turn through the dev server touches nothing new.

This also points at the real fixes: `flueWorkerConfig()` knows the runtime's own entry points and could ship this include list itself, and `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` silently overriding a user's `noDiscovery` looks like a separate bug worth filing there.

## Workaround (alternative)

Building and serving the Worker directly also works, with the side benefit of running the artifact that actually deploys — at the cost of hot reload:

```sh
vite build
wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json --port 8788 --persist-to .wrangler/state
```

`--persist-to` matters: wrangler otherwise keeps local Durable Object state beside its config under `dist/`, and a rebuild deletes it mid-run. A `vite build --watch` alongside it does not work either — emptying `dist/` while wrangler serves from it kills the Worker with `The directory specified by the "assets.directory" field ... does not exist`.

Happy to test a proper fix against a project with a realistic dependency set, since the bare scaffold does not reproduce it under pnpm.

title: Feature: per-tool execution timeout on ToolDefinition
body:
## Motivation

A host application running agents under a hard submission budget cannot guarantee useful termination unless each tool call is individually bounded. Today `ToolDefinition` has no timeout field, so a single tool whose internals hang — a transport that observes abort signals late or never, an unbounded response-body read, a hung SDK call — can silently consume the entire submission budget while every turn around it is healthy.

We hit this in production: an upstream API returned headers quickly and then streamed its body for ~430s per call. The tool "succeeded" slowly, three calls consumed a 20-minute durability budget, and the submission was aborted at its deadline with zero output. Because the calls succeeded, nothing paged.

## Current workaround

We wrap every tool's `run()` in our own instrumentation seam and race it against a per-tool `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`, settling budget losses as a synthetic error result the model can react to, while caller aborts still propagate. This works, but every Flue host has to rebuild it, and the harness is naturally positioned to own it (it already owns the tool lifecycle, result serialization, and the submission durability timeout).

## Proposal

- Optional `timeoutMs?: number` on `ToolDefinition` (and/or a host-level default in the agent config).
- The harness races `run(context)` against the deadline. On expiry it settles the tool call with a structured timeout result (distinguishable from a thrown tool error), aborts `context.signal`, and lets the conversation continue — mirroring how tool exceptions already become tool results rather than submission failures.
- The submission-level durability timeout remains the outer backstop; the per-tool bound just prevents one call from consuming it.
- Late settlement of the abandoned `run()` promise should be observed (no unhandled rejection) and discarded.

## Alternatives considered

- Relying on tools to bound their own awaits: fails in practice — any single missed await (fetch vs. body read vs. retry sleep) reopens the hole.
- Host-side wrapper (our current approach): works but is per-host reinvention of lifecycle logic the harness already owns.

title: OpenAI/Anthropic SDK "Connection error." not classified retryable, so one network blip permanently fails the submission
body:
### Describe the Bug

`isRetryableModelError()` (`packages/runtime/src/submission-state.ts:439-451` on current `main`, `bf86b87`) is the classifier that routes transient model failures into the in-loop transient retry (`classifyResumeState` → `mode: 'transient_retry'`). Its regex covers `network.?error`, `connection.?(?:reset|refused|lost)`, `socket hang up`, `fetch failed`, timeouts, 5xx, etc. — but it does not match the literal string **"Connection error."**

That exact string is the default message of `APIConnectionError` in both official provider SDKs:

- **openai** (`core/error.ts`): `super(undefined, undefined, message || 'Connection error.', undefined)` — verified in openai `6.26.0`, `core/error.js:80`
- **@anthropic-ai/sdk** (`core/error.ts`): same literal — verified in `0.91.1`, `core/error.js:78`

`APIConnectionError` is what these SDKs throw for *every* connection-layer failure — DNS resolution failure, TLS handshake failure, proxy disconnect, socket aborted before a response — so "Connection error." is arguably the single most common transient error text a production deployment will ever see from these providers. Because the classifier doesn't match it, the assistant error entry is treated as permanent: no transient retry happens and the submission settles as `failed`.

In production we observed a single transient proxy blip permanently fail a submission with `attempt_count = 2` while `maxAttempts` was configured to 10; the durable workflow driving that submission was then failed as a whole. (Durability-level attempts don't help here for the same reason as in #443 — the error is observed and classified, just classified as permanent.)

This is the same class of gap as #443 ("Stream ended without finish_reason" not classified retryable), fixed in 2.0: the provider layer produces a transient connection-layer error, but the retry-classification layer treats it as terminal.

Affected: `@flue/runtime` 2.0.3 (latest) and current `main`.

### Expected Behavior

`stopReason: 'error'` with `errorMessage: 'Connection error.'` (optionally with SDK cause suffixes appended) should be classified retryable, exactly like `connection reset` / `connection refused` / `network error` already are, so the submission retries up to its attempt budget instead of settling `failed` on the first network blip.

### Steps to Reproduce

Deterministic, classifier-level (same shape as the repro in #443):

```ts
import { isRetryableModelError } from './packages/runtime/src/submission-state';

isRetryableModelError({
	role: 'assistant',
	stopReason: 'error',
	errorMessage: 'Connection error.', // openai / @anthropic-ai/sdk APIConnectionError default message
	content: [],
});
// expected: true
// actual:   false
```

End-to-end: run any OpenAI-backed agent behind a proxy and drop the connection mid-request once — the OpenAI SDK throws `APIConnectionError('Connection error.')`, and the submission hard-fails instead of retrying.

### Proposed fix

Minimal, mirroring the existing alternation style — add `connection.?error|` next to the existing connection branch in the `isRetryableModelError` regex:

```diff
-	return /overloaded|rate.?limit|too many requests|429|500|502|503|504|service.?unavailable|server.?error|network.?error|connection.?(?:reset|refused|lost)|socket hang up|fetch failed|timed? out|timeout|terminated|provider finish_reason:\s*error(?![-\w])/i.test(
+	return /overloaded|rate.?limit|too many requests|429|500|502|503|504|service.?unavailable|server.?error|network.?error|connection.?error|connection.?(?:reset|refused|lost)|socket hang up|fetch failed|timed? out|timeout|terminated|provider finish_reason:\s*error(?![-\w])/i.test(
 		message.errorMessage,
 	);
```

Checked against the current pattern: with this change `"Connection error."` classifies retryable, while clearly non-retryable messages (e.g. `"invalid api key"`) still classify non-retryable, and all strings matched by the current regex still match.

We're running this exact one-branch patch in production (via `pnpm patch`) and it resolves the failure mode. Happy to provide anything else that helps — filing this as a fix proposal per CONTRIBUTING.md rather than a PR.

title: Cloudflare tracing omits join IDs from existing child spans
body:
### Describe the Bug

On Cloudflare, durable work can continue in a later invocation. If the owning span is missing, child spans do not carry enough identifiers to join the fragments.

The events already have the IDs. `@flue/opentelemetry` projects them through `identifiers(event)`. The Cloudflare adapter currently:

- puts submission, instance, and conversation on agent operations, but not `flue.operation.id`
- puts task id on task operations, but not submission or operation id
- omits submission, operation, and turn ids from model and model-tool spans
- omits submission and operation ids from caller-shell spans

This is an exporter gap, not a runtime execution bug. The IDs are present on the events; they are just not copied onto those spans.

### Expected Behavior

Keep every existing span name and parent relationship. Add only these optional attributes when the event already has the value:

- agent operation: `flue.operation.id`
- task: `flue.submission.id`, `flue.operation.id`
- model and model-tool: `flue.submission.id`, `flue.operation.id`, `flue.turn.id`
- caller-shell: submission and operation ids when present

Do not add new spans, `eventIndex`, or attempt count. Do not copy the rest of OpenTelemetry's identifier set (`harness`, `session`, `parent_session`, and so on).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Trace an agent prompt that includes a model turn and a tool call with `createCloudflareTracing()`.
2. Compare those span attributes with the same run under `createOpenTelemetryInstrumentation()`.
3. Cloudflare child spans are missing the join IDs above even though the corresponding runtime events carry `submissionId`, `operationId`, and `turnId`.

Relevant code: `packages/runtime/src/cloudflare/tracing/index.ts` (agent / task / model / tool / caller-shell attribute builders) and `packages/runtime/src/cloudflare/tracing/attributes.ts` (no operation or turn ID constants today). OpenTelemetry's projection is `identifiers()` in `packages/opentelemetry/src/index.ts`.

title: ModelRequestInfo.contextCompacted is never populated
body:
### Describe the Bug

`ModelRequestInfo.contextCompacted` is part of the public turn payload. Both trace adapters read it and map it to `gen_ai.conversation.compacted`. `Session.modelRequestInfo()` never sets it, so the attribute never appears.

The events reference already documents this: the field is declared for turns whose context was compacted, and the current runtime does not populate it.

### Expected Behavior

Set `contextCompacted` to `true` when the model request's effective context is a compacted view of earlier history (canonical context includes a compaction summary). Leave it absent otherwise, including on summarization turns (`purpose: 'compaction'` / `'compaction_prefix'`). Never emit `false`.

This should follow the pinned OpenTelemetry meaning: the effective context is a compacted view, not a one-shot "compaction just happened" flag.

Do not change compaction span names or parenting.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Compact a conversation (threshold, overflow, or `session.compact()`).
2. Run another ordinary agent turn on that conversation.
3. Inspect the `turn_request` / `turn` payload and the chat span.
4. `request.contextCompacted` is missing, and neither adapter emits `gen_ai.conversation.compacted`.

The field is declared at `packages/runtime/src/types.ts`, copied into turn events from `Session.modelRequestInfo()` in `packages/runtime/src/session.ts`, consumed by `@flue/opentelemetry` and `createCloudflareTracing()`, and documented as unpopulated in `apps/docs/src/content/docs/reference/events.md`.

title: @flue/opentelemetry README still documents content capture as off by default
body:
### Describe the Bug

`packages/opentelemetry/README.md` says content capture is disabled by default and still documents the pre-v2 `content` options: `enabled`, `externalContent`, `inline`, `maxMessageParts`, `maxToolDefinitions`, `maxAttributeBytes`, and the old truncation marker attributes.

That does not match the rest of the project. After instrumentation is installed, absent `content` means capture is on. `content: false` turns it off. `content: { transform }` redacts or drops values. Content on a span shares one 56 KiB in-band budget. The v2 changelog recorded the default-on change, and the docs site already describes the current contract.

### Expected Behavior

The package README should describe the current `content?: false | { transform }` contract, the same way `createOpenTelemetryInstrumentation()` and `apps/docs/src/content/docs/ecosystem/tooling/opentelemetry.md` do.

This is a documentation fix only. Do not change either adapter's runtime default.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `packages/opentelemetry/README.md` (Content capture).
2. Compare it with:
   - `packages/opentelemetry/src/index.ts` (`content?: ContentOption`, absent means capture on)
   - `packages/runtime/src/telemetry/content.ts` (`contentAttribute()` returns nothing only when policy is `false` or content is undefined)
   - `apps/docs/src/content/docs/guide/observability.md` and `apps/docs/src/content/docs/ecosystem/tooling/opentelemetry.md`
   - the v2 changelog entry that made capture default-on and collapsed the option shape
3. The README still says capture is off and still shows the removed options.

title: Persisted submissions omit final text from terminal telemetry
body:
### Describe the Bug

In Flue v2.0.3, a successful persisted agent submission (`processSubmissionInput`, used by HTTP and `dispatch()` paths) emits a terminal `operation` observation without `agentOutput`. This diverges from a successful freeform `session.prompt()` operation.

Both `@flue/opentelemetry` and Flue's Cloudflare tracing project terminal text `agentOutput` into `gen_ai.output.messages`. Consequently, the persisted parent agent span contains the input but not the final assistant response.

This report is limited to freeform text output. Structured result data and response metadata are not currently projected into `gen_ai.output.messages` for direct prompts, tasks, or persisted submissions.

### Expected Behavior

A successful persisted freeform submission emits terminal text `agentOutput` for its final assistant response through the same live-observation and GenAI projection contract used by a successful freeform `session.prompt()` operation.

This should not redefine the durable submission reply contract (`text`, `data`, and `metadata`) or add structured data or metadata to `gen_ai.output.messages` only for persisted submissions.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `@flue/runtime@2.0.3` and configure Flue OpenTelemetry instrumentation with a span exporter.
2. Run an agent with a deterministic/local OpenAI-compatible model through the persisted HTTP or `dispatch()` submission path.
3. Let the agent complete a normal freeform text response.
4. Inspect the terminal parent `operation` / `invoke_agent` span.
5. Observe that `gen_ai.input.messages` is present but `gen_ai.output.messages` is absent.
6. Run an equivalent freeform `session.prompt()` operation and inspect its terminal parent span. It includes `gen_ai.output.messages` with the final assistant text.

### Additional Evidence

In v2.0.3, the persisted path flushes the response successfully, but returns no result to its enclosing `runOperation('prompt', ...)`. The operation's terminal observation therefore cannot normalize an `agentOutput`. The direct freeform prompt path returns a text result through that same operation boundary.

A local real-Flue reproduction against the affected runtime with a mock OpenAI-compatible streaming model and a file-backed OpenTelemetry span processor confirmed the difference: the unmodified persisted path omitted the parent output; providing the final text at the existing operation boundary populated `gen_ai.output.messages`.



Example implementation: https://github.com/SilasMarvin/flue/pull/2

title: Cloudflare binding provider drops per-model `compat`, breaking Claude 4.6+ models (adaptive thinking) through `env.AI`
body:
### Describe the Bug

Every request to a Claude 4.6+ model through the Cloudflare AI binding fails with:

```
Cloudflare AI binding request failed with 400 Bad Request: {"error":[{"code":7003,
"message":"Model execution failed (User Input Error): \"thinking.type.enabled\" is not
supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\"
to control thinking behavior."}], ...}
```

pi-ai's `cloudflare-ai-gateway` catalog marks these models with `compat.forceAdaptiveThinking: true` (plus `supportsTemperature: false`), and its Anthropic serializer emits `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` only when that flag survives to the model object. `workers-ai-provider.ts` drops the catalog `compat` twice, so the serializer falls back to the legacy `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens}` shape, which Claude 4.6+ models reject.

Drop site 1 — `gatewayCatalogModels` discards `compat` when it re-tags the gateway catalog for the binding. Its comment says "`toAnthropicGatewayModel` replaces it", which is drop site 2 — that replacement loses the per-model flags rather than layering the binding's overrides on top of them:

```ts
// gatewayCatalogModels
compat: undefined,   // loses forceAdaptiveThinking and supportsTemperature

// toAnthropicGatewayModel
compat: {
  supportsCacheControlOnTools: false,
  supportsEagerToolInputStreaming: false,
  supportsLongCacheRetention: false,
  sendSessionAffinityHeaders: false,
}
```

**Fix proposal:** keep the catalog `compat` in `gatewayCatalogModels`, and spread it under the provider's own overrides in `toAnthropicGatewayModel`:

```ts
compat: {
  ...model.compat,
  supportsCacheControlOnTools: false,
  supportsEagerToolInputStreaming: false,
  supportsLongCacheRetention: false,
  sendSessionAffinityHeaders: false,
}
```

We run 2.0.3 in production with exactly this change as a `pnpm patch` and can confirm it fixes the 400: requests go out with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` and complete. It also restores `supportsTemperature: false`, which prevents the equivalent temperature rejection on Opus 4.7+.

### Expected Behavior

`useModel('cloudflare/anthropic/claude-opus-5')` (or any Claude 4.6+ model) through `cloudflareBindingProvider` sends the adaptive thinking shape and the request completes.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start from a basic hello-world agent on Cloudflare Workers with `cloudflareBindingProvider({ binding: env.AI, gateway: { id: '<your-gateway>' } })` and an AI Gateway funded for unified billing.
2. Set the agent's model to `cloudflare/anthropic/claude-opus-5`.
3. Send any message. The turn fails with the 400 above; the AI Gateway log shows the rejected request.

title: useTool run() overload error blames Promise<void> instead of the real branch-shape mismatch
Cloudflare Anthropic provider ignores forceAdaptiveThinking, sends incompatible thinking config
body:
### Describe the Bug

`streamCloudflareAnthropicAi` in `@flue/runtime`'s `dist/cloudflare/workers-ai-provider.mjs` always sets:

```js
thinkingEnabled: Boolean(options?.reasoning)
```

That sends Anthropic's older budget-based `thinking.type.enabled` shape. Some models need Anthropic's newer adaptive-thinking API instead (`thinking.type.adaptive` plus `output_config.effort`), and for those, this fails every time.

`claude-sonnet-5` is one of them. It's registered in `@earendil-works/pi-ai`'s model catalog (`dist/providers/data/anthropic.json`) with `"compat":{"forceAdaptiveThinking":true}`. The other two code paths in the same file, the direct Anthropic API path and `streamCloudflareResponsesAi`/`applyResponsesReasoning`, both check that flag correctly. Only the Cloudflare AI Gateway path for Anthropic models skips it.

Here's what actually comes back, calling `useModel('cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5')` through the Cloudflare `env.AI` binding:

```
Cloudflare AI binding request failed with 400 Bad Request: {"success":false,"result":[],"messages":[],"error":[{"code":7003,"message":"Model execution failed (User Input Error): \"thinking.type.enabled\" is not supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\" to control thinking behavior."}] ...}
```

### Expected Behavior

`streamCloudflareAnthropicAi` should check `compat.forceAdaptiveThinking` the same way the other two paths in this file already do, and send `thinking.type.adaptive` plus `output_config.effort` for models that need it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In a Cloudflare-target Flue app with an `ai` binding in `wrangler.jsonc`, define an agent:
   ```ts
   'use agent';
   import { useModel } from '@flue/runtime';

   export function Extract() {
     useModel('cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5');
     return 'Say hello.';
   }
   ```
2. Dispatch it against a deployed Worker with Workers AI Billing on the AI Gateway set to Unified billing, so a 402 billing error isn't muddying the picture.
3. Watch it 400 with the error above. It never completes.

### Workaround

Turning off thinking entirely dodges the bad payload, at the cost of losing extended thinking for this model:

```ts
useModel('cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5', { thinkingLevel: 'off' });
```

title: Preserve persisted submission output in terminal telemetry
body:
## Summary

Persisted agent submissions currently complete their response stream without returning the final assistant text to `runOperation()`. As a result, the terminal `operation` telemetry observation has no `agentOutput`, so `@flue/opentelemetry` emits an `invoke_agent` parent span without `gen_ai.output.messages`.

Return the final assistant text after `flushResponseOutput()`. The public submission API remains `CallHandle<void>`; its caller intentionally discards the internal operation result. The returned value exists only so the terminal telemetry observation can populate `agentOutput`.

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm --dir packages/runtime check:types`
- `corepack pnpm --dir packages/runtime build`
- Local Flue CLI reproduction with a mock OpenAI-compatible model and a file-backed OTel span processor:
  - before this change, `invoke_agent` had no `gen_ai.output.messages`;
  - after the corresponding local runtime patch, the same persisted submission emitted the final assistant text on the parent span.

title: Overflow recovery dead-ends ("no valid cut point") when the trailing toolResult is ≥ keepRecentTokens — submission fails permanently
body:
### Describe the Bug

With `@flue/runtime` 2.0.0, overflow recovery cannot make progress when the conversation tail is a single toolResult whose estimated size (chars/4) is at or above `keepRecentTokens`.

In `compaction.ts`, `findCutPoint` walks back from the tail accumulating estimated tokens until it has kept `keepRecentTokens`; if the very first (most recent) message already exceeds that budget, no valid cut point is found and the search falls back to index 0. `prepareCompaction` then returns undefined ("Nothing to compact"), the overflow-recovery pass becomes a no-op, and the submission settles `failed` at the provider's context ceiling. Every retry of the same conversation hits the same wall — the failure is permanent, not transient.

Any workload where a single tool call can return a large payload (e.g., `bash` cat of a big file via the sandbox tools, or a bulk download step) can land one oversized toolResult in-conversation and brick recovery for the whole submission.

### Observed vs Expected

**Observed (reproduced live):** A durable agent dispatch accumulated ~1.06M estimated tokens, with the tail being one very large toolResult. The provider rejected the request as context overflow; Flue detected the overflow and entered compaction recovery; `findCutPoint` found no valid cut point; `prepareCompaction` returned undefined; the recovery no-opped and the submission settled `failed`.

**Expected:** Overflow recovery should always be able to shrink the conversation when there is anything before the tail to summarize. Reasonable behaviors when the trailing toolResult alone exceeds `keepRecentTokens`:

- degrade `keepRecentTokens` (keep only the oversized tail message and summarize everything before it), and/or
- truncate or elide the oversized toolResult content itself as a last resort,

rather than declaring "nothing to compact" and failing the submission permanently.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a durable agent with compaction enabled (any `keepRecentTokens`, e.g. the default).
2. Have a tool return a single result whose character length / 4 ≥ `keepRecentTokens` (a `bash` tool reading a large file is enough) as the most recent message, with the total conversation near the model's context window.
3. Continue until the provider rejects with context overflow.
4. Observe: overflow is classified correctly and recovery starts, but `findCutPoint` falls back to index 0, `prepareCompaction` returns undefined, and the submission settles `failed`. Retrying the conversation fails identically.

### Notes

- Related but distinct from #428/#600: here the overflow is detected and recovery does run — it just cannot produce a plan.
- A secondary aggravator: the chars/4 estimate undercounts dense content on Gemini (~0.5 tok/char measured for dense CSV), so real overflow arrives before the estimator expects it.

### Environment

- `@flue/runtime`: 2.0.0 (logic appears unchanged in 2.0.3)
- Provider: Google Vertex (gemini flash / flash-lite), ADC
- Node.js, in-process runtime; durable agent driven by an external dispatcher

title: Threshold compaction never fires when a run settles via a `terminate: true` tool result
body:
### Describe the Bug

With `@flue/runtime` 2.0.0, threshold compaction is only evaluated when a response run settles on a plain assistant message. `checkCompaction` runs after `agentLoop.waitForIdle()` in `session.ts` and is gated on the last message being an assistant message. When a run ends because the model called a tool declared with `terminate: true` (called alone in its batch), the last message in the conversation is a toolResult, so the check is skipped entirely.

For agents whose turns are designed to end with a terminating "completion" tool — a common pattern for durable agents driven by an external dispatcher, where each dispatch ends with the agent submitting a structured outcome — this means threshold compaction never fires at any turn boundary, regardless of how `reserveTokens` / `keepRecentTokens` are configured. The conversation only ever shrinks via overflow recovery (i.e., after the context window has already been blown).

### Observed vs Expected

**Observed:** A durable agent configured with a compaction threshold of ~15k tokens ran a multi-tool dispatch that peaked at ~37.6k estimated tokens and settled via a `terminate: true` tool. Zero compactions occurred. The next dispatch on the same conversation started with the full 37.5k-token context.

Control run confirming the mechanism: sending one plain-text follow-up submission ("reply OK") — which settles on an assistant message — caused threshold compaction to fire exactly as configured (19 → 9 messages; next dispatch's first-turn input dropped from ~37k to ~7.2k tokens).

**Expected:** Threshold compaction should run whenever a response run settles above the threshold, including runs settled by a terminating tool result. The docs state compaction runs "when used tokens exceed contextWindow − reserveTokens" with no caveat about how the run settles; that currently only holds for plain-settled runs.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a durable agent with a tool declared `terminate: true` (the agent's normal way of finishing a dispatch) and a low compaction threshold (e.g., `reserveTokens` sized so the threshold is ~15k on the configured model).
2. Dispatch a task that accumulates well past the threshold (large tool results work) and ends with the model calling the terminating tool.
3. Observe: no `compaction_start` event; the conversation persists uncompacted.
4. Dispatch a plain-text prompt on the same conversation (settles on an assistant message): compaction fires immediately.

### Suggested fix

Run the threshold check on terminate-settled runs too (i.e., evaluate `checkCompaction` after `waitForIdle()` whether the leaf is an assistant message or a terminating toolResult), or document the limitation and expose an application-triggerable compaction path for durable conversations (related: #136).

### Environment

- `@flue/runtime`: 2.0.0 (code paths appear unchanged in 2.0.3)
- Provider: Google Vertex (gemini flash / flash-lite), ADC
- Node.js, in-process runtime

title: Allow configuring the source root so authored modules can live outside src/
body:
### Motivation

`resolveSourceRoot()` fixes the authored-module directory to `.flue/` → `src/` → project root. When a project keeps its frontend in `src/` (the standard Vite convention) and wants to put the agent code in a sibling directory (e.g. `worker/`), there is currently no supported way to re-point the source root:

- `app` / `db` / `cloudflare` entries can be set explicitly, but that only covers entry discovery;
- `agents` accepts a glob, but it resolves **relative to the source root**, so pointing at a sibling directory requires an escape glob like `../worker/**`;
- the dev watcher only rescans agent modules inside the source root (`isWithinDirectory(filePath, sourceRoot)`), so edits to agent files outside `src/` never trigger a rescan — the dev server must be restarted to pick them up.

The result is that a `src/` + sibling source-directory layout is only half-supported and easy to get wrong.

### Expected behavior

A way to override the source root so the whole pipeline — agent scan, entry discovery (`app.ts`, `db.ts`, `cloudflare.ts`) and the dev watcher — targets a configured directory:

```ts
// either as a flue() plugin option
flue({ sourceRoot: 'worker' }) // or any other directory, e.g. 'server/'
// or as a field on FlueConfig
export default defineConfig({ sourceRoot: 'worker' })
```

When unset, current behavior stays exactly as-is (`.flue/` → `src/` → root).

### Alternatives considered

- **Changing the default** to prefer `worker/`: rejected because it would silently change behavior for existing projects that keep authored modules in `src/`.
- **Documenting the `../worker/**` escape glob as the supported path**: it works for scanning but leaves the dev watcher broken for out-of-source agent files.

title: OpenTelemetry spans are silently lost when running an agent via "flue run"
@flue/vite adds DO class to wrangler config but does not export it in the bundle
body:
**Package:** `@flue/vite@2.0.3`
**Related:** `@flue/runtime@2.0.3`, `@cloudflare/vite-plugin@1.52.0`, `wrangler@4.122.0`
**Repo:** https://github.com/withastro/flue

## Environment

- macOS
- Node 22
- pnpm 11.10.0
- `@flue/vite@2.0.3`
- `@flue/runtime@2.0.3`
- `@cloudflare/vite-plugin@1.52.0`
- `wrangler@4.122.0`
- `vite@8.0.14`
- `compatibility_date: "2026-08-13"`

## Summary

The Flue Vite plugin correctly adds a `FlueBrowserAssistantAgent` Durable Object binding and migration entry to the generated `dist/.../wrangler.json`, but does not generate or export the corresponding DO class in the bundled `index.js`. This causes `wrangler deploy` to fail with error code 10070.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/jillesme/talk-to-webpage (which uses `@flue/vite` + `@flue/runtime`)
2. Run `pnpm install && pnpm build`
3. Run `npx wrangler deploy`

## Expected behavior

The Vite build should either:
- Generate and export a `FlueBrowserAssistantAgent` DO class in the bundle entry point, matching the migration/binding it adds to the generated wrangler config
- Or not add the class to the generated wrangler config if it cannot generate the export

## Actual behavior

The generated `dist/voice_imiel_dev/wrangler.json` contains:

```json
{
  "durable_objects": {
    "bindings": [
      { "name": "FLUE_BROWSER_ASSISTANT_AGENT", "class_name": "FlueBrowserAssistantAgent" }
    ]
  },
  "migrations": [
    { "tag": "v1", "new_sqlite_classes": ["FlueBrowserAssistantAgent"] }
  ]
}
```

But the bundled `index.js` only exports:

```js
export { BrowserSession, WebsiteVoiceAgent, worker_entry_default as default };
```

`FlueBrowserAssistantAgent` is not present in the bundle at all:

```
$ grep "FlueBrowserAssistantAgent" dist/voice_imiel_dev/index.js
(no output)
```

The Flue runtime does register the agent function via `__flueBindAgentModule(BrowserAssistant, { identity: "browser-assistant" })` (line 65731), and the naming convention `Flue` + PascalCase(`browser-assistant`) + `Agent` = `FlueBrowserAssistantAgent` is correctly applied to the wrangler config. But the corresponding `class FlueBrowserAssistantAgent extends Server` (or equivalent) is never generated or added to the bundle exports.

Deploy fails with:

```
[ERROR] Cannot apply new-class migration to class 'FlueBrowserAssistantAgent'
that is not exported by script. [code: 10070]
```

Deleting the Worker and redeploying produces the same error (this is not a stale migration issue).


## Workaround (verified)

Manually create and export the DO class in `cloudflare.ts` using the same factory the virtual entry would use:

```ts
// cloudflare.ts
export { default } from './app.ts';
export { BrowserSession } from './browser/browser-session.ts';
export { WebsiteVoiceAgent } from './voice/website-voice-agent.ts';

// Workaround: @flue/vite adds FlueBrowserAssistantAgent to wrangler config
// but doesn't export the class in the bundle.
import { Agent } from 'agents';
import { createFlueAgentClass } from '@flue/runtime/cloudflare/internal';
import { createCloudflareAgentRuntime } from '@flue/runtime/internal';

export const FlueBrowserAssistantAgent = createFlueAgentClass({
  AgentBase: Agent,
  runtime: createCloudflareAgentRuntime(),
  className: 'FlueBrowserAssistantAgent',
  agentName: 'browser-assistant',  // matches the identity in __flueBindAgentModule
  extension: undefined,
});
```

This mirrors exactly what the generated `virtual:flue/worker` entry is supposed to produce. Deploy succeeds with this in place.

title: Silent-overflow recovery fails completed submission by continuing from assistant
body:
### Describe the Bug

With `@flue/runtime` 2.0.3, a durable submission can settle as failed after it has already produced a complete assistant response and threshold compaction succeeds.

The durable submission error is:

```text
Cannot continue from message role: assistant
```

Observed event order:

1. Several model/tool cycles complete successfully.
2. A final assistant message completes with `stopReason: "stop"`.
3. Threshold compaction emits a canonical compaction record parented to that assistant message.
4. A resource snapshot is emitted.
5. 57 ms later, the submission settles as failed with the error above.

There was no tool or model failure. The completed response used about 38.7k total model tokens. This happened twice in adjacent production submissions.

The agent declares `useAgentStart` and `useResponseFinish`, but no `useAgentFinish`, so no finish-hook continuation was expected.

Possible investigation points in v2.0.3:

- [`runModelTurnWithRecovery()` performs threshold compaction and then returns](https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/v2.0.3/packages/runtime/src/session.ts#L4742-L4752).
- [`runWouldStopPhase()` continuation paths call `agentLoop.continue()`](https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/v2.0.3/packages/runtime/src/session.ts#L1587-L1600).
- [`continueRebuilt()` only avoids continuing from an assistant leaf when a `restart` callback was supplied](https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/v2.0.3/packages/runtime/src/session.ts#L4715-L4720).

I do not have the internal stack trace, so the exact continuation entry point remains unconfirmed.

### Expected Behavior

After a successful assistant response and successful threshold compaction, the submission should settle as completed and retain the assistant response. No further model turn should start unless new user/signal/join input exists.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `@flue/runtime` 2.0.3 with durable Postgres submissions and threshold compaction enabled.
2. Run a multi-tool conversation until a successful assistant turn crosses the compaction threshold.
3. Let threshold compaction complete after the assistant's `stop` response.
4. Inspect the durable submission settlement.

Observed result: compaction completes, then the submission fails with `Cannot continue from message role: assistant`.

Environment:

- `@flue/runtime`: 2.0.3
- `@flue/postgres`: 2.0.3
- `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`: 0.83.0
- Node.js: 24.x

title: Docs: document Docker requirement for local Cloudflare Sandbox development
body:
### Describe the Bug

The Cloudflare Sandbox documentation explains the required package, container image, Durable Object binding, migration, and Dockerfile, but it does not state that running the container-backed sandbox locally requires Docker to be installed and the Docker daemon (for example, Docker Desktop) to be running.

This affects the following documentation:

- https://flueframework.com/docs/ecosystem/sandboxes/cloudflare/
- https://flueframework.com/docs/ecosystem/deploy/cloudflare/#connecting-a-remote-sandbox

Without that prerequisite, `vite dev` can fail when it attempts to build or start the local container, and the failure does not clearly lead users back to a missing or stopped Docker installation.

Related: #581 covers the Workers Paid plan requirement for deployed usage and briefly mentions distinguishing local Docker-based development. This issue focuses specifically on documenting the local runtime prerequisite.

### Expected Behavior

The Cloudflare Sandbox setup instructions should explicitly state that local development requires:

- Docker installed.
- The Docker daemon running (for Docker Desktop users, the application must be open).

A short prerequisite callout near the Quickstart or Setup section, repeated or linked from the local development instructions, would make the requirement discoverable before users run `vite dev`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Flue Cloudflare agent with `@cloudflare/sandbox` and a `containers[]` entry as documented.
2. Ensure Docker is not installed or the Docker daemon is stopped.
3. Run `vite dev` and attempt to use the sandbox-backed agent.

title: Packaged skill supporting files are invisible to sandboxes — bundled scripts can't be executed or materialized
body:
### Describe the Bug

 A packaged skill that carries supporting files (scripts, reference documents) cannot be used correctly when the agent has a sandbox. The model can read the files through read / read_skill_resource, but it cannot
 execute them (bash), cannot stat/exists them, and agent code has no API to materialize them into the sandbox. Any skill whose instructions require running a bundled script fails mid-conversation with a confusing
 "No such file or directory" from bash.

 Root cause: overlayPackagedSkills (packages/runtime/src/agent.ts:54-73) wraps only readFile. Everything else — exec, stat, exists, readdir, writeFile, readFileBuffer — passes through to the real sandbox
 filesystem, where /.flue/packaged-skills/<id>/… does not exist. This boundary is documented in apps/docs/src/content/docs/reference/sandbox-api.md ("Packaged-skill overlays"): "Only readFile is overlaid. exec,
 exists, stat, and the other verbs pass straight through, so shell commands cannot see the virtual root."

 Additionally, there is no access path for agent code at all: SkillReference (packages/runtime/src/types.ts:169-177) exposes only id/name/description, getRegisteredPackagedSkills
 (packages/runtime/src/session.ts:584-590) is module-private, and the overlay is session-internal (harness.sandbox and useTool handlers see the adapter's real env). So packaged-skill content is reachable only by
 the model's read tools — a deliberate read-only design that leaves executable content with no working path in any sandboxed session.

 ### Expected Behavior

 A skill whose activation briefing advertises scripts/check.sh should be usable in a sandboxed session: the script should execute, and its internal reads of sibling resources (e.g. reference/policy.md) should
 resolve. At minimum, the docs should state that packaged-skill supporting files are model-read-only and not executable, and recommend workspace skills or useTool for executable content.

 ### Steps to Reproduce

 1. Create a packaged skill with supporting files, and instruct the agent to run the script:
    ```text
src/skills/audit/
├─ SKILL.md            # instructions: "1. Run scripts/check.sh. 2. Read reference/policy.md"
├─ scripts/check.sh    # internally reads sibling reference/policy.md
└─ reference/policy.md
    ```
 2. Mount it in a sandboxed agent:
    ```ts
'use agent';
import { useModel, useSkill, useSandbox } from '@flue/runtime';
import audit from '../skills/audit/SKILL.md';

export function AuditAgent() {
  useModel('anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5');
  useSandbox(local()); // any sandbox-backed agent
  useSkill(audit);
  return 'Activate the `audit` skill before validating an environment.';
}
    ```
 3. Ask the agent to activate the skill and run the audit. The activation briefing correctly lists <skill_resources> with paths like /.flue/packaged-skills/skill:audit:<hash>/scripts/check.sh, then:
   - bash on that path fails with "No such file or directory" (exec sees the real sandbox FS, not the virtual root).
   - stat/exists on the virtual path also fail (not overlaid).
   - Even if the model reads the script text and writes it to a real path, the script's internal read of reference/policy.md still fails (the sandbox process can't see the virtual root either).

 Impact: any packaged skill requiring script execution is unusable with a sandbox; there is no warning at mount/activation time that the advertised paths are non-executable.

 Suggested directions: (1) materialize packaged-skill supporting files into the sandbox on mount/activation so exec and sibling reads work; (2) expose a public API for the packaged-skill file catalog (or carry
 files on SkillReference / harness) so agent code can materialize in useAgentStart; (3) at minimum, document the limitation and the workspace-skill / useTool alternatives.

 Current workarounds: workspace skills (.agents/skills/ — files are real workspace files, exec works); useTool for scripts that must run in the sandbox; defineSkill + useAgentStart materialization (works only when
 the agent authors the skill in code, since SkillDefinition.files is in scope — not for SKILL.md imports).

title: Cloudflare target: scheduled agent fails every run — alarm-driven continuation returns 403 "Request not allowed"
body:
## Scheduled agent fails every run: `dispatch(sub_...) failed: 403 {"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}` during alarm-driven continuation

### Environment

- `@flue/runtime` 2.0.3, `@flue/vite` 2.0.3, `@flue/cli` 2.0.3, `@flue/sdk` 2.0.3
- Cloudflare target, `wrangler` 4.113.0, `compatibility_date: "2026-06-01"`, `nodejs_compat`
- `@cloudflare/sandbox` 0.11.0 (container-backed sandbox attached via `cloudflareSandbox(getSandbox(...))`)
- `agents` (Cloudflare Agents SDK) 0.20.1, resolved purely from `@flue/vite`'s own dependency pin (`^0.20.1`) — not overridden in our project, and already the latest published version

### Symptom

An agent (`SentryTriage`) dispatched every 5 minutes from a Worker `scheduled()` cron handler fails on essentially every run:

```json
{
  "level": "error",
  "message": "[flue:submission-processing] {\"agentName\":\"SentryTriage\",\"instanceId\":\"sentry-triage-scheduled\",\"submissionId\":\"sub_01KZTT3BWX1T0WBSRDT93DDQ5F\",\"operation\":\"process\",\"outcome\":\"failed\"}     at Session.throwIfError (index.js:56398:23)\n    at Session.resumeConversationToCompletion (index.js:56598:10)\n    at async index.js:56683:5\n    at async Session.withCallOverrides (index.js:55704:11)\n    at async index.js:55881:70\n    at async Session.runExclusive (index.js:55932:11)",
  "$workers": { "eventType": "alarm", "entrypoint": "FlueSentryTriageAgent", "executionModel": "durableObject" }
}
```

The underlying `FlueError`, captured via `wrangler tail --format json`:

```
FlueError: dispatch(sub_01KZTT3BWX1T0WBSRDT93DDQ5F) failed: 403 {"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}
    at Session.throwIfError (index.js:56398:23)
    at Session.resumeConversationToCompletion (index.js:56598:10)
    at async index.js:56683:5
    at async Session.withCallOverrides (index.js:55704:11)
    at async index.js:55881:70
    at async Session.runExclusive (index.js:55932:11)
```

Full `diagnosticsChannelEvents` for one failing run (parsed from raw tail output):

```
schedule:execute  agent=FlueSentryTriageAgent name=sentry-triage-scheduled payload={callback: __flueWakeAgentSubmissions}
schedule:create   agent=FlueSentryTriageAgent name=sentry-triage-scheduled payload={callback: __flueWakeAgentSubmissions}
fiber:run:started agent=FlueSentryTriageAgent name=sentry-triage-scheduled fiberName=flue:submission-attempt
fiber:run:failed  agent=FlueSentryTriageAgent name=sentry-triage-scheduled elapsedMs=781–1595 (varies by run)
  error: dispatch(sub_...) failed: 403 {"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}
```

Note there is no model-call (`chat`) or tool-call trace event anywhere between `fiber:run:started` and `fiber:run:failed` — the failure happens before any model turn, inside `resumeConversationToCompletion`'s own setup/continuation, in well under 1.6s.

Separately, the *admission* call that queues the submission — our own application code calling `dispatch(SentryTriage, {...})` from the Worker's `scheduled()` handler (not from inside a Durable Object alarm) — always succeeds:

```json
{ "event": { "request": { "url": "https://flue.invalid/__flue/internal/dispatch", "method": "POST" }, "response": { "status": 200 } }, "eventType": "fetch", "entrypoint": "FlueSentryTriageAgent" }
```

So: dispatch/admission from a normal fetch-context succeeds; the subsequent processing, kicked off from the Durable Object's own `alarm()`-driven `__flueWakeAgentSubmissions` (per the source comment below), fails with a 403 whose body looks like a generic Cloudflare-edge rejection rather than an application-level error from any provider we call (Anthropic, Sentry, Slack, GitHub — none of which use this JSON shape, and none of which are reached before the failure per the trace above).

### What we ruled out via bisection

Built a minimal second agent (`ScheduleDebug`: `useModel` + `usePersistentState` + one trivial tool, no external API calls) and dispatched it on its own cron to isolate variables one at a time:

1. **Sandbox-less, 1-minute cadence** — 3/3 clean runs, while `SentryTriage` failed on its one concurrent attempt in the same capture window. Rules out a blanket bug affecting every scheduled Flue/Cloudflare agent.
2. **Same `cloudflareSandbox`/`getSandbox` container as `SentryTriage`, still 1-minute cadence** — still 3/3 clean (2.5–3.4s per run, so the sandbox/container RPC calls — three `exists` calls per run against the Sandbox DO, each logged `"outcome": "ok"` — are not the failure point). Rules out the sandbox/container attachment itself as the sole cause.
3. Currently testing: offsetting `ScheduleDebug` to a ~5-minute cadence (matching `SentryTriage`'s) to see whether cadence/an idle gap between runs correlates with the failure (results pending at time of filing).

Also ruled out: a stale/mismatched `agents` SDK version (already at the latest published 0.20.1, resolved only from `@flue/vite`'s own pin, no override in this project) and any application-level provider error (the failure precedes any model or tool call in the trace).

### Working theory

`@flue/runtime`'s Cloudflare target source contains this comment (`dist/cloudflare/internal.mjs`, on the generated Durable Object class):

```js
/**
* Durable schedule target that owns submission supervision: armed at
* zero delay by admission/abort/recovery/fiber-settle boundaries and
* at 30s as the heartbeat while unsettled work exists. Dispatched
* from the Durable Object's alarm invocation as one bounded,
* storage-only pass that reconciles, enforces deadlines, and starts
* attempt fibers detached — the fibers outlive the invocation on the
* SDK's runFiber keepAlive/recovery machinery.
*/
__flueWakeAgentSubmissions() {
    return runtime.drainSubmissions(this);
}
```

So every submission's actual processing is kicked off from inside the DO's own `alarm()` handler, and that processing appears to make its own internal continuation call (surfaced generically in the error as `dispatch(submissionId)`) — most likely another `getAgentByName(...).fetch(...)`-style self-call through the `agents` SDK, matching `fetchAgent()` in `dist/cloudflare/internal.mjs` (`(await getAgentByName(binding, instanceId)).fetch(request)`).

This matches a reported Cloudflare platform behavior: outbound `fetch()` calls made from *within* a Durable Object's `alarm()` handler have been reported to return HTTP 403 "Direct IP access not allowed" (Cloudflare Error 1003), even when the identical call succeeds from a normal fetch-handler context: https://community.cloudflare.com/t/workers-durable-objects-outbound-fetch-returning-error-1003-across-multiple-us-data/913410

### Open questions for Flue

1. Does the Cloudflare-target continuation path (`resumeConversationToCompletion` → whatever `dispatch(submissionId)` calls) make a self-fetch from inside the DO's `alarm()` handler?
2. If so, is that hitting the Cloudflare edge restriction described above, and is there a way to avoid the self-fetch entirely in that path (e.g. an in-process call instead of a fetch, or a documented pattern for DO-to-self calls that stays off the public/edge routing)?
3. Why would this correlate with agent complexity/duration — `SentryTriage` (5 tools, one mounted skill, `claude-sonnet-4-6`) fails on effectively every run, while a much lighter agent on a faster cadence has not reproduced it in our testing so far? Is there a timing window during render/setup that affects whether the internal continuation call happens to hit this path?

Happy to share full raw `wrangler tail --format json` captures on request.

### Describe the Bug

Using Flue with the latest version of Hono causes a TypeScript compilation error (`TS2345`) in `src/app.ts`. A recent breaking type change in Hono means that `Hono<Env, BlankSchema, "/">` is no longer assignable to `Hono<Env, Schema, string, string>` — the `query` property is missing.   Property 'query' is missing in type 'Hono<Env, BlankSchema, "/">' but required in type 'Hono<Env, Schema, string, string>'.
 ELIFECYCLE  Command failed with exit code 2.
```

### Expected Behavior

Projects using Flue should typecheck successfully against the installed version of Hono. Pinning the workspace-wide Hono dependency to a known-compatible version (e.g., `4.13.1`) should resolve the type mismatch.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and run `pnpm install` (allowing pnpm to resolve the latest unpinned version of Hono).
2. Open any example that uses Hono (e.g., `examples/hello-world`).
3. Run the TypeScript type check (`pnpm check:types`) and observe the `TS2345` error in `src/app.ts`.

title: Docs sidebar and table of contents clip scrolled items at top and bottom boundaries
body:
> _Originally reported by @fabian-hiller in [#584](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/584)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

On `/docs/*` pages, the sidebar navigation and the "On this page" table of contents use `sticky` scroll containers with `overflow-y-auto`. The vertical spacing (`pt`/`pb` padding) is applied to the wrapping `<aside>` element — outside the scroll container. This means the scrollable bounds start 2 rem below the header and end 2 rem above the viewport bottom. When the list is long enough to require scrolling, items get clipped mid-letter at those boundaries, leaving dead zones above and below where content is chopped off rather than scrolling cleanly out of view.

![CleanShot 2026-08-11 at 18 00 17@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40d3f326-d5cf-4361-b1d1-01b5d562bff1)

### Expected Behavior

Scrolled items in the sidebar and table of contents should remain fully visible while passing through the padding zone and disappear cleanly at the header border and the viewport bottom, without being clipped mid-letter at floating boundaries.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a docs page with a long sidebar navigation, such as `/docs/guide/channels/`.
2. Reduce the viewport height so that the sidebar or table of contents list is long enough to require scrolling.
3. Scroll the sidebar or table of contents and observe that items are clipped mid-letter at the top and bottom boundaries of the scroll container.

title: feat: add native referenced attachments
body:
## Summary

Adds Flue-native, format-agnostic attachment references. Raw uploads stage against an agent instance, then referenced user or signal deliveries atomically reserve the ordered set before durable admission and bind it to canonical conversation history during materialization.

The runtime owns byte persistence, integrity metadata, idempotency, expiry/reclaim, canonical binding, safe downloads, model-facing escaped manifests, and user/signal file projections. Atlas and other clients submit opaque file IDs; arbitrary binary is never coerced into provider image input.

## Lifecycle guarantees

- First-message uploads work before a root conversation exists.
- Exact upload replays return 200; changed bytes or metadata conflict.
- Referenced direct submissions require an idempotency key.
- Missing, foreign, expired, or partial reference sets reject before durable admission/model execution.
- Failed admission releases only a proven-absent exact reservation; bound files cannot move between conversations.
- SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, LibSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and in-memory stores implement the same lifecycle.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @flue/runtime test`
- `pnpm --filter @flue/runtime check:types`
- `pnpm --filter @flue/runtime build`
- Type checks for `@flue/postgres`, `@flue/mysql`, `@flue/libsql`, `@flue/mongodb`, `@flue/redis`, and `@flue/sdk`
- `git diff --check`

An adversarial review was performed and all lifecycle findings were resolved, including first-message staging, reservation reclaim, immutable binding, opaque-ref restoration, exact upload idempotency, and user/signal projections.

`pnpm test` remains unsuitable as a workspace gate because several packages, including `@flue/mongodb`, invoke Vitest with no test files and exit nonzero.

title: Fold-host resident state during long high-reasoning drafts is a significant share of a 128 MB DO isolate — bounding/spill options?
body:
**Environment:** `@flue/runtime@2.0.2`, one-shot draft agent in a Cloudflare Durable Object (128 MB isolate limit).

## Observation

While investigating a production OOM crash-loop on a long, high-reasoning draft (large thinking deltas over many turns), heap snapshots attributed ~21% of retained memory to `ConversationRecordWriter` and its pinned conversation fold host (`getConversationFoldHost` → cached `reducedState`). The majority (~79%) was our own observability adapter's queue — separate issue, fixed on our side (braintrustdata/braintrust-sdk#2353) — but the fold-host share alone is meaningful against a 128 MB budget once conversations get long.

We can see the design already bounds much of this deliberately: non-retain-set records downgrade to `ConversationRecordStub` at application, and streaming-record stubs are released when the message materializes. What remains resident for the writer's lifetime appears to be the materialized entries (including completed reasoning block bodies) and the retain-set record bodies — plus, while a message is in progress, its accumulated blocks.

## Asks / questions

1. Is there (or could there be) an option to drop completed reasoning/thinking block bodies from resident reduced state when the harness does not re-send thinking to the model? For reasoning-heavy models these bodies dominate entry size.
2. A windowed or spillable fold host — reconstruct older entries from the log on demand — for agents whose conversations outlive what a 128 MB isolate can comfortably keep resident.
3. Failing either, documented guidance on expected resident-memory shape per conversation size, so consumers can set compaction/abort budgets against it.

title: Transient model retry duplicates the reply: superseded error entries are merged into the UI projection and replyFromSnapshot
body:
### Describe the Bug

`@flue/runtime` 2.0.2 (Node target; line refs below point into `dist/dispatch-nU3cIlT-.mjs` of the published build — we don't have the source tree).

The context builder and the UI projection disagree about what an assistant entry with `stopReason: "error"` means. The context builder treats it as *superseded* and excludes it from the model context; the UI projection treats it as *part of the answer* and merges its text into the submission's response message. After an in-loop transient retry, the visible reply therefore contains the partial answer **and** the regenerated full answer, concatenated.

Sequence:

1. A model stream fails mid-turn with a retryable error (`isRetryableModelError`: overloaded / rate limit / 429 / 5xx / timeout / socket hang up / terminated) **after** text has already streamed. The partial assistant message is committed with `stopReason: "error"` and the streamed content intact (message_end handling force-completes the open blocks).
2. `runModelTurnWithRecovery` backs off, rebuilds the canonical context and continues the loop. The context builder (≈ dispatch:757-765) **skips** assistant entries with `stopReason` `"error"`/`"aborted"` (aborted only survives with an adjacent `stream_interrupted` + `stream_continued` pair). The model sees no partial, so it regenerates the whole answer — a second assistant entry with the **same submissionId**.
3. `projectConversationUi` (≈ dispatch:1795-1861) folds all assistant entries of a submission into one message via `mergeAssistantContinuation`, which is a plain `parts.push(...)` (≈ :1867) with **no stopReason filter**; `projectCompletedMessage` (≈ :1961-1988) projects error/aborted entries as `display: "visible"` with all their text parts.
4. `replyFromSnapshot` (≈ :2852-2877) joins the merged message's text parts with `"\n\n"`.

Result: `handle.read(receipt).reply.text`, `view=history` and `view=updates` all return `partial + "\n\n" + full answer`. This is deterministic on every retryable mid-stream failure that occurs after the first text delta — no race required — and with provider overload being a routine event, it shows up often in production.

Today no marker of the retry survives into the snapshot — `ConversationUiPart` carries no stopReason or entry provenance, and no signal record is written on the transient-retry path — so downstream consumers cannot distinguish the duplicate from a legitimate multi-block answer.

**Secondary observation:** for the rescued path (aborted partial + `stream_interrupted`/`stream_continued`, where keeping the partial is correct), the `"\n\n"` join inserts a paragraph break at the interruption point — even a perfect continuation renders with a break mid-sentence. A seam-aware join would render seamlessly.

**Workaround we ship today:** we recompose the reply text app-side from the raw `ConversationStreamStore` records, where `assistant_message_completed.stopReason` survives, applying the context builder's predicate — with fallback to `reply.text`. It works, but it re-implements a slice of the reducer and has to track dist behavior across versions, which is why we'd prefer the fix upstream.

### Expected Behavior

The projection agrees with the context builder: an errored entry that was superseded by a rerun is not part of the answer. Either exclude such entries from the visible projection and `replyFromSnapshot` (reusing the exact predicate at dispatch:757-765), or at minimum expose provenance (per-part or per-entry `stopReason`) on `ConversationUiMessage`/`ConversationUiPart` so consumers can filter.

### Steps to Reproduce

Starting from a basic hello-world agent with a scripted provider (we used pi-ai's `fauxProvider`):

1. Script the provider to fail retryably mid-answer, then answer fully:
   ```ts
   faux.setResponses([
     fauxAssistantMessage([fauxText("partial-A")], {
       stopReason: "error",
       errorMessage: "socket hang up", // matches isRetryableModelError
     }),
     fauxAssistantMessage([fauxText("full-answer-B")]),
   ]);
   ```
2. `const receipt = await init(Agent, { id }).dispatch({ message: "hi" });`
3. `const reply = await init(Agent, { id }).read(receipt);`

`reply.text` is `"partial-A\n\nfull-answer-B"` — expected `"full-answer-B"`. The same duplicated text appears in `view=history` and `view=updates`.

title: Record tool payloads of every shape on gen_ai.tool.call.*
body:
## Summary

- Record tool arguments/results on `gen_ai.tool.call.*` for every payload shape; drop the `flue.tool.call.*` fallback keys (`FLUE_TELEMETRY_EXTENSION_REVISION` → 5).
- Best-effort JSON-parse string payloads ([the spec asks for this](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/4c8addb53718b544134be47e256237026fe88875/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md)) so serialized objects record structured and double-encoded results un-nest.
- Update `@flue/opentelemetry` README and the ecosystem docs page.

## Why

Fixes #568. String tool results — every MCP tool, most local tools — landed on vendor keys no backend reads, so consumers of the semconv keys showed tool inputs with no outputs. The spec types these attributes `any` and sanctions JSON-string form on spans; the adapters already stringify objects, so the object-only fork changed nothing but the key.

**Considered and skipped:** dual-writing `flue.tool.call.*` for a deprecation window. Both keys draw from the same per-span content pool (sized against workerd's 64 KiB span-attribute cap), so duplicating the largest payloads in the system would make truncation kick in twice as early. Easy to switch if you'd rather keep a compat window.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=@flue/runtime --filter=@flue/opentelemetry` — pass
- `pnpm -w exec tsc --noEmit -p packages/runtime` / `-p packages/opentelemetry` — clean
- `biome lint` on the four changed source files — clean (`@flue/runtime` has no vitest files to run)
- Against the built dist: `'hello'` records as-is on `gen_ai.tool.call.result`; `'{"a":1}'` and `{a: 1}` record structured
- Live against Sentry: every successful `execute_tool` span (MCP tools included) carries `gen_ai.tool.call.result` and renders in the AI trace views

title: Tool results are invisible to OTel backends: string payloads land on flue.tool.call.* instead of gen_ai.tool.call.result
body:
Tool results never show up on `gen_ai.tool.call.result`. Any payload that isn't a plain object — which is most tool returns, including every MCP tool result — is recorded under the vendor key `flue.tool.call.result` instead ([semconv.ts#L46-L47](https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/bf86b872/packages/runtime/src/telemetry/semconv.ts#L46-L47)), and no backend reads that key. In Sentry's AI trace views, for example, every tool call shows its arguments but never its output.

The fork is in [`setToolContent`](https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/bf86b872/packages/opentelemetry/src/index.ts#L736-L743) and its Cloudflare twin [`toolPayloadEntry`](https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/bf86b872/packages/runtime/src/cloudflare/tracing/index.ts#L744-L751), justified by the comment that the semconv keys "are specified as object-shaped." But at the revision pinned in `GEN_AI_SEMCONV_REVISION`, [the spec](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/4c8addb53718b544134be47e256237026fe88875/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md) types these attributes `any`:

> in case a serialized string is available to the instrumentation, the instrumentation SHOULD do the best effort to deserialize it to an object. When recorded on spans, it MAY be recorded as a JSON string if structured format is not supported and SHOULD be recorded in structured form otherwise.

OTel span attributes can't hold objects, so the JSON-string branch is the operative one — and the adapters already `JSON.stringify` object payloads before `setAttribute`. The fork doesn't change what's emitted, only which key it lands on.

Proposed fix (PR #569): always record on `gen_ai.tool.call.*`, best-effort JSON-parse string payloads as the spec asks, drop the `flue.tool.call.*` keys.

title: Cloudflare Shell code tool: Promise nested in sandbox result fails as raw DataCloneError instead of being resolved or corrected
body:
### Describe the Bug

With `@flue/runtime@2.0.2` + `@cloudflare/shell@0.4.3` + `@cloudflare/codemode@0.5.1`, model-authored code whose return value contains an unresolved `Promise` fails the entire `code` tool call with a raw structured-clone error:

```text
DataCloneError: #<Promise> could not be cloned.
    at async DynamicWorkerExecutor.execute (...)
```

The executor awaits the *top-level* result inside the sandbox (`await Promise.race([(fn)(), timeout])`), but the `{ result, logs }` object then crosses the Workers RPC boundary from the dynamic Worker's `evaluate()` back to the host via structured clone. Any Promise *nested* inside the result — a shape models produce constantly, e.g.

```js
async () => ({ files: paths.map((p) => state.readFile(p)) })  // missing Promise.all
```

— throws `DataCloneError` at the RPC boundary, and the tool call fails terminally.

Two problems compound here:

1. **The failure is avoidable by construction.** The sandbox already ships a codec (`__stringifyForCodemode` / `__parseForCodemode`) used for tool-call arguments and results between sandbox and host, but `evaluate()`'s own return value rides raw structured clone. The result channel is the one channel that skips the codec.
2. **The error is unactionable for the model.** `#<Promise> could not be cloned.` names the transport mechanism (structured clone) three abstraction layers below the model's actual mistake (a missing `await`). In our production traces this class of thrown code-tool error produces blind identical retries rather than a corrected call; errors returned to an LLM need to state the API contract that was violated, not the transport symptom.

Observed in production (Sentry, support-seal): the model batched `state.readFile` calls into a returned container without awaiting them; the whole read failed and the draft degraded to other tool calls.

### Expected Behavior

In preference order:

1. **Deep-resolve the result before it crosses the boundary.** After awaiting the top-level value, resolve nested thenables (or JSON-roundtrip the result inside the sandbox with the existing codemode codec, which both flushes non-serializable values deterministically and reuses the binary-tagging path tool results already use). "Return what you computed" should always work; this deletes the error class for every consumer of the executor.
2. **If a non-cloneable value must remain an error, make it corrective.** Return an execution error stating the contract — e.g. `Your function's return value must be plain JSON-serializable data. It contained a Promise: await every async call (use await Promise.all(...) for arrays) before returning.` — instead of the raw `DataCloneError`, so the model self-corrects in one turn.
3. **Document the result contract** in the generated tool description ("the returned value must be plain JSON data; await all promises").

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a `DynamicWorkerExecutor` with any `WorkerLoader` binding.
2. Execute:

```js
async () => ({ files: [Promise.resolve("a"), Promise.resolve("b")] })
```

3. The sandbox `evaluate()` returns successfully inside the isolate, but the host-side RPC deserialization throws `DataCloneError: #<Promise> could not be cloned.`, which surfaces as a terminal `code` tool failure.

### Related observation (same affordance-mismatch family)

The same day we also saw `entry.isDirectory is not a function` from model code iterating `state.readdir(...)` output — the model's Node.js prior expects `fs.Dirent` entries while the state API returns name strings. Follow-on data point for the 2026-07-15 code-tool feedback: where the sandbox API diverges from the strongest model prior (Node `fs`), either aligning the API shape or stating the return shape in the tool schema prevents the misuse class at the source.

title: Update Sentry tooling blueprint to v2: recovery logs and dataCollection defaults
body:
## Summary

- Record `submission_recovery` events as Sentry Logs instead of breadcrumbs (Node and Cloudflare variants)
- Default content capture from the SDK's resolved `dataCollection` policy ([added in `@sentry/node` 10.54](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/releases/tag/10.54.0)); `SENTRY_AI_RECORD_*` stays as per-direction overrides
- Rewrite the content guidance: state the metadata-only vs turn-by-turn trade-off, recommend content on for dev/staging, ship the example with it on
- Point per-project PII policy at [server-side data scrubbing](https://docs.sentry.io/security-legal-pii/scrubbing/server-side-scrubbing/); the local `scrub` stays a fixed credential-key pass instead of growing per project
- Drop `streamGenAiSpans: true` (SDK default since 10.61), add `WorkersAI` to the suppressed provider integrations, note v11 needs `skipOpenTelemetrySetup: false`
- Bump to `tooling/sentry@2` (also fixes the example's stale pre-2.0 `@4` marker)

## Why

Breadcrumbs only surface if a later error is captured, and a stuck submission may never produce one — recovery events re-emit on every coordinator wake, so searchable, alertable logs fit them better. `dataCollection` is the same switch Sentry's own AI integrations use, so one vocabulary governs content instead of two (nothing configured still records no content; on Cloudflare no client exists at module scope, so the env vars remain the only control there). The guide also now says what content capture buys — turn-by-turn reconstruction of each run — instead of framing it only as risk.

## Verification

- `pnpm --dir packages/cli exec tsx scripts/generate-blueprint-index.ts` — 38 blueprints, contract passes
- `pnpm -w exec tsc --noEmit -p examples/sentry` — clean
- `pnpm exec biome check examples/sentry/src/sentry.ts` — clean
- The same integration changes ran live under `flue run` against a real Sentry project: full trace, tool logs in Sentry Logs, content gated by the resolved policy
