title: User prompt missing from durable event stream after page refresh
body:
> _Originally reported by @odysseus0 in [#367](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/367)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

When a user sends a direct prompt to an agent, the user's message is written to canonical session state but is not appended to the public durable event stream. Since `@flue/react` reconstructs conversation history from that stream, refreshing the page after a prompt/response exchange recovers the assistant's response but permanently loses the corresponding user message. This affects both Node and Cloudflare Durable Object runtimes.

### Expected Behavior

After a page refresh, the full conversation history — including user prompts — should be reconstructed from the durable event stream. Every user message submitted via a direct prompt should appear alongside its corresponding assistant response.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a Flue project with `@flue/react` on the frontend and either the Node or Cloudflare runtime
2. Send a direct prompt to an agent and wait for the assistant response to appear
3. Perform a full browser refresh
4. Observe that the assistant response is recovered in the conversation history, but the user prompt that triggered it is missing

---

Original implementation from [#367](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/367) by @odysseus0

title: [codex] Persist direct prompt user events in durable stream
body:
## What changed

- append a durable `message_end` user event for every direct prompt
- reserve event index `0` for that input and begin runtime output at index `1`
- use `appendEventOnce` with a deterministic submission key so normal processing and crash reconciliation can both deliver the event safely
- cover Node end-to-end replay, Node recovery deduplication, and Cloudflare recovery projection

## Root cause

Direct submissions wrote the user input to canonical session state, but only runtime-generated events were subscribed into the public durable event stream. `@flue/react` reconstructs history from that stream, so a refresh could recover the assistant response while permanently omitting the corresponding user prompt.

Fixes #307.

## Validation

- `pnpm --dir packages/runtime run build`
- `pnpm --dir packages/runtime run check:types`
- `pnpm --dir packages/runtime exec vitest run test/node-agent-coordinator.test.ts test/cloudflare-agent-coordinator.test.ts` (57 passed, 1 skipped)
- Biome and Prettier checks for all changed files
- local Cloudflare Durable Object integration: a new user prompt and assistant response both reconstructed after a full browser refresh

title: ActionOutputSerializationError rejects undefined object properties and fails entire run
body:
### Describe the Bug

`cloneJsonSerializable` (packages/runtime, src/json-snapshot.ts) calls `assertJsonLike` before `JSON.stringify`. `assertJsonLike` throws on any nested `undefined`, so an Action/workflow whose result contains an optional property left undefined fails its entire run with:

```
ActionOutputSerializationError: Action "<name>" output.<field> must not contain undefined values
```

… even when no output schema is declared. This is surprising because the very next line - `JSON.stringify` — already handles undefined with standard semantics (it drops undefined-valued keys). The strict pre-check therefore rejects exactly what the serializer it wraps would have normalized harmlessly.

Optional properties (`field?: T` left unset) are idiomatic TypeScript and the natural shape when building a result from API responses or spreads. On the Node target the run is marked failed and left orphaned (status: active, no crash-terminalize) even though all the action's side effects already completed — the only casualty is an optional output field.

### Expected Behavior

For object properties, match JSON.stringify semantics — omit undefined-valued keys instead of throwing (at least when no output schema is declared). The genuinely-unrecoverable cases (circular references, non-finite numbers, non-plain objects, functions/symbols/bigint) can keep failing loud.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a workflow whose run() returns an object with an optional property left undefined, e.g. `return { ok: true, detail: undefined }` (no output schema declared).
2. Run it on the Node target (flue run <workflow>).
3. It fails with `ActionOutputSerializationError: … output.detail must not contain undefined values` — even though `JSON.stringify({ ok: true, detail: undefined })` yields valid JSON (`{"ok":true}`).

Version: `@flue/runtime@1.0.0-beta.3`, Node target.

title: cloudflare target: custom Durable Object exported from app.ts is dropped from generated entry (Class extends undefined)
body:
## Summary

On the `cloudflare` target, a custom **Durable Object class exported from `.flue/app.ts`** is **not forwarded** into the generated Worker entry. Wrangler still gets the binding + migration (so the class name is referenced), but the class itself is tree-shaken out, so the Worker crashes at startup:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Class extends value undefined is not a constructor or null
    at createDurableObjectWrapper
```

This also fails a real `wrangler deploy`, not just local dev.

## Cause

In `packages/cli/src/lib/build-plugin-cloudflare.ts`, the generated entry re-exports named exports **only from the dedicated `cloudflare` entry** (`discoverOptionalEntry(sourceRoot, 'cloudflare')`):

```js
const userCloudflareReExport = cloudflareEntry
  ? `export * from ${JSON.stringify(cloudflareEntry...)};`
  : '';
```

The `app` entry is imported **default-only** (`import userApp from ...`), so any *named* export from `app.ts` — including a custom DO class — is dropped and tree-shaken. Meanwhile the user (or their wrangler config) still declares the binding/migration for that class, producing a class_name with no exported class.

Confirmed the same code path on `main` (`build-plugin-cloudflare.ts` `userCloudflareReExport`) in addition to the released beta.

## Repro

1. Define a Durable Object class, e.g. `src/MyStore.ts`.
2. Re-export it from `.flue/app.ts`: `export { MyStore } from "../src/MyStore";`
3. Add its binding + migration to `wrangler.jsonc`.
4. `flue build --target cloudflare` → the generated `dist/<app>/index.js` exports the Flue-managed DOs and `default`, but **not** `MyStore`.
5. Boot → `Class extends value undefined`.

## Workaround (and maybe the intended design?)

Moving the export to a dedicated `.flue/cloudflare.ts` makes it work, because that file *is* re-exported via `export * from`:

```ts
// .flue/cloudflare.ts
export { MyStore } from "../src/MyStore";
```

If `cloudflare.ts` is the intended home for custom DO/Worker exports, that's reasonable — but the current behavior is a silent footgun:
- `app.ts` named exports are accepted by TS/build with no error, then dropped.
- The wrangler binding/migration are still emitted, so the failure only shows up as an opaque runtime `Class extends value undefined` at startup.

## Suggested fixes (any one)

1. Document that custom DO/Worker named exports must live in `.flue/cloudflare.ts` (the README mentions ownership of DOs but not the entry-file requirement).
2. Validate at build time: if `wrangler` declares a `class_name` that isn't exported by the generated entry, fail with a clear message naming the class and pointing to `cloudflare.ts`.
3. Also forward named exports from `app.ts` (or warn when `app.ts` has named exports that look like DO classes).

## Environment

- `@flue/cli` / `@flue/runtime` `1.0.0-beta.3` (code path unchanged on current `main`)

title: cloudflare target: eager createRequire(import.meta.url) crashes Worker at startup in workerd

labels.name: fix pending
labels.description: Fixed on a development branch; lands with the next release

body:
## Summary

On the `cloudflare` target, the generated Worker bundle crashes at **startup** in workerd with:

```
Uncaught TypeError: The argument 'path' must be a file URL object, a file URL string, or an absolute path string.. Received 'undefined'
    at node:module:34:15 in createRequire
    at assets/rolldown-runtime-<hash>.js:42
```

The Worker never boots — `wrangler dev` (local), and `wrangler deploy` both fail.

## Cause

Rolldown's runtime chunk emits an **eager** CJS-interop shim at module top level:

```js
// dist/<app>/assets/rolldown-runtime-<hash>.js
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
var __require = /* #__PURE__ */ (() => createRequire(import.meta.url))();
```

In workerd, `import.meta.url` is `undefined`, so `createRequire(undefined)` throws during module initialization, before any user code runs. `nodejs_compat` is enabled and `createRequire` exists — the only problem is the `undefined` argument.

The shim is pulled in by Node-only code that gets bundled even though it's unreachable on workerd. In my build the live `__require` call sites were:
- `@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/provider-env.js` → `__require("node:fs")` (a Bun-compiled-binary sandbox env workaround, dead on workerd — guarded by `process.versions.bun`)
- `mimetext.node.es` → `__require("path").extname`

Both are dead at runtime on workerd, so only the eager *construction* of `__require` actually breaks. `__require` is never invoked in the entry (0 call sites in `index.js`).

## Repro

- `flue build --target cloudflare` on an app whose agent uses a model provider that transitively pulls `@earendil-works/pi-ai` (e.g. a Workers AI model).
- `wrangler dev --config dist/<app>/wrangler.json --local` → crash above.

## Environment

- `@flue/cli` / `@flue/runtime` `1.0.0-beta.3`
- wrangler 4.10x, workerd via miniflare, `nodejs_compat`, recent compatibility_date

## Suggested fixes (any one)

1. Make the emitted shim safe — e.g. `createRequire(import.meta.url || "file:///worker.js")`, or wrap construction in try/catch so an unused `__require` can't abort startup.
2. Set worker/browser resolve conditions for the cloudflare target so Node-only builds (`*.node`, Bun-sandbox fallbacks) aren't selected, letting the shim tree-shake away.
3. Strip/guard provider env-detection code that calls `require` for non-Node targets.

## Workaround

Postbuild step that rewrites `createRequire(import.meta.url)` → `createRequire(import.meta.url || "file:///worker.js")` in the emitted assets. After this the Worker boots normally. Happy to PR the resolve-conditions approach if that's the preferred direction.

title: docs(ecosystem): add Jetty tooling integration
body:
Adds **Jetty** to the Ecosystem → Tooling docs, alongside Braintrust, Sentry, and
Vitest Evals.

## What & why

Flue owns the agent loop; Jetty is the *check* beside it. In a workflow you draft
with the agent, then hand the draft to an independent Jetty **grading task** and
get back a durable, labelled [trajectory](https://docs.jetty.io) — every run
becomes a queryable record you can diff across versions, so a regression shows up
before a customer finds it. This fills the eval/observability gap next to
[Vitest Evals](/docs/ecosystem/tooling/vitest-evals/) (in-process assertions) and
[Braintrust](/docs/ecosystem/tooling/braintrust/) (tracing): Jetty stores each
run, scored by a grader the agent didn't write.

## Changes

- New page: `apps/docs/src/content/docs/ecosystem/tooling/jetty.md`
  (Quickstart · Overview · Configure · What Jetty captures · Protect sensitive
  content · Free trial · Verify · Next steps — matching the existing tooling
  pages).
- Nav: one entry added to the Tooling block in
  `apps/docs/src/lib/docs-navigation.ts` (alphabetical, between Braintrust and
  OpenTelemetry).

## Docs-only

No package or runtime changes. Jetty integrates through its published SDK
([`@jetty/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jetty/sdk)) rather than a
`flue add tooling` blueprint, so the Quickstart is `npm install @jetty/sdk` (the
page says so explicitly). The SDK ships a one-call eval primitive,
`gradeWithJetty`, used in the snippet (shown with the `defineWorkflow` API).

## Worked example

A complete, runnable A/B-eval that catches a regression lives at
[`jettyio/jetty-sdk` → `examples/flue-jetty`](https://github.com/jettyio/jetty-sdk/tree/main/examples/flue-jetty):
Flue runs the agent, Jetty grades and stores every run, and an offline
`npm run demo` reproduces the verdict table with no keys. It runs on
`@flue/runtime` 1.0.0-beta.3.

## Verification

- Links resolve to existing pages (`/docs/guide/evals/`,
  `/docs/ecosystem/tooling/vitest-evals/`, `/docs/ecosystem/tooling/braintrust/`).
- Page frontmatter and section structure follow `vitest-evals.md` /
  `braintrust.md`.

---

*Happy to add a `flue add tooling jetty` setup blueprint as a follow-up if the
maintainers would like the install guided like the other tooling integrations.*

title: High Durable Object active memory (GB-sec) usage due to HTTP SSE/Long-polling streams instead of WebSockets with Hibernation
body:
### Description of the Issue

Currently, Flue’s Durable Object target implements the Durable Streams protocol entirely over standard HTTP/HTTPS:
- Catch-up GET (plain HTTP response returning a JSON array of events)
- HTTP Long-polling (`live=long-poll`)
- HTTP Server-Sent Events (`live=sse`)

While this is standard and highly compatible, it has significant cost and resource implications on Cloudflare Workers:
1. **Continuous DO Execution:** When a client keeps an SSE connection or long-poll request open, the Durable Object must remain active in memory to serve the persistent HTTP connection.
2. **Active Billing (GB-seconds):** Under Cloudflare’s pricing model, Durable Objects are billed for the entire duration they are active in memory (CPU + Memory). Because Cloudflare does not support hibernating standard HTTP streams, the DO incurs billing charges for 100% of the connection duration. 
3. **Scale Issues:** With multiple active users keeping tabs open, the accumulated GB-seconds can lead to high and unexpected Cloudflare Workers bills.

### Proposed Solutions

We would like to propose a few options to improve cost-efficiency when deploying Flue on Cloudflare Durable Objects:

#### Option A: Implement Native WebSocket Support with Hibernation
Introduce native WebSocket support into Flue's runtime, letting generated DO-backed agents/workflows handle connections via WebSockets. This would allow the generated Durable Objects to use Cloudflare’s **WebSocket Hibernation API** (`state.acceptWebSocket()`):
* The Durable Object can safely hibernate (unload from memory, stopping the GB-sec billing meter) while keeping client connections open.
* The DO is only woken up when a new event needs to be broadcast or a client sends a message.

#### Option B: Centralized / Decoupled WebSocket Gateway DO
To keep the individual Agent/Workflow DOs simple and fast to spin down:
* Introduce a shared, lightweight `WebSocketGateway` Durable Object.
* Clients establish hibernating WebSocket connections to this gateway DO.
* When an Agent DO runs a turn and writes events, it fires a brief HTTP broadcast call to the gateway DO, which wakes up to push events and immediately sleeps.
* The Agent DOs can continue to spin down immediately after completing their turn execution.

#### Option C: Better Documentation and Polling Helpers
If WebSockets are out of scope for the current design, we should:
* Explicitly document the billing implications of `live=sse` on Cloudflare Durable Objects.
* Document/recommend short-polling using regular `GET /agents/:name/:id?offset=<offset>` requests (which let the DO spin down immediately after returning the JSON response) as a cost-efficient alternative.

title: beta 3 regression: `flue dev` externalizes workspace `SKILL.md` imports → "Unable to resolve skill import"
body:
### Describe the Bug

`flue dev --target node` fails to start when an agent statically imports a skill
(`with { type: "skill" }`) that is exported from a **workspace package** through a package
`exports` subpath. Startup aborts with:

```
Dev server failed: [flue] Unable to resolve skill import: @repo/github/skills/explore-repo/SKILL.md
```

`flue build --target node` and `flue build --target cloudflare` resolve the **same** import
without error and produce a working artifact — only the dev server fails. Markdown imports
(`with { type: "markdown" }`) from a workspace package subpath are affected the same way.

**This is a regression in `1.0.0-beta.3`.** The exact same project (same skill, same workspace
package subpath import) ran `flue dev` fine on `1.0.0-beta.2`; bumping only the `@flue/*` packages
to `1.0.0-beta.3` introduced the failure.

**Possible root cause (from reading `@flue/cli@1.0.0-beta.3`'s `dist/flue.js`):**

The node dev server registers `viteGeneratedEntryDependencyResolver(root, { external: true })` as
an `enforce: "pre"` Vite plugin (in the `createServer({ ... plugins: [...] })` call). Its
`resolveId` externalizes every resolvable bare specifier:

```js
async resolveId(source, importer) {
  // This guard is SKIPPED in dev because dev passes no `importers`:
  if (options.importers && (!importer || !options.importers.includes(importer)) && source !== "@flue/runtime" && ...) return null;
  if (source.startsWith(".") || source.startsWith("/") || ...) return null;
  ...
  for (const resolve of resolvers) try {
    const id = resolve.resolve(source);
    return options.external ? { id, external: true } : id;  // <-- skill .md marked external
  } catch {}
  return null;
}
```

Because the dev call omits `importers`, the first guard is a no-op, so the resolver marks
`@repo/github/skills/explore-repo/SKILL.md` (resolvable via the package's `exports` map) as
`{ external: true }`. Flue's own import-attribute/skill plugin then does
`this.resolve(specifier, importer, { skipSelf: true })`, sees `resolved.external === true`, and
throws `Unable to resolve skill import`.

The **build** path calls the same helper as `viteGeneratedEntryDependencyResolver(root)` (no
`{ external: true }`), so the skill resolves to a real filesystem path and the skill plugin
handles it — which is why build works and dev does not.

### Expected Behavior

`flue dev` should resolve statically-imported `SKILL.md` / `.md` files exported from a workspace
package subpath the same way `flue build` does (hand them to the skill/markdown plugin), instead of
externalizing them. The dev entry-dependency resolver should not externalize `.md` skill/markdown
specifiers (and arguably should apply the same `importers` scoping the build path relies on).

### Steps to Reproduce

Starting from a basic hello-world in a pnpm workspace:

1. Add a workspace package (e.g. `packages/skills`) that exposes a skill through its `exports` map:
   ```jsonc
   // packages/skills/package.json
   { "name": "@repo/skills", "exports": { "./explore/SKILL.md": "./src/explore/SKILL.md" } }
   ```
   with a valid `packages/skills/src/explore/SKILL.md` (frontmatter `name: explore`, a description,
   and body).
2. In the agent, import it from the package subpath:
   ```ts
   import explore from "@repo/skills/explore/SKILL.md" with { type: "skill" };
   ```
   and register it on the agent.
3. Run `pnpm flue dev --target node`.
   → Dev server aborts: `[flue] Unable to resolve skill import: @repo/skills/explore/SKILL.md`.
   Run `pnpm flue build --target node` (and `--target cloudflare`) → both succeed.

**Environment**

- Broken on `@flue/cli` / `@flue/runtime` `1.0.0-beta.3`; worked on `1.0.0-beta.2`
- pnpm `11.8.0` (workspace with `workspace:*` source-only packages), Node `24`, macOS
- Skill imported via a package `exports` subpath (not a relative path; relative `./…SKILL.md`
  imports are unaffected because the resolver early-returns for specifiers starting with `.`)

title: Agent history needs backward cursor pagination
body:
## Problem

Flue supports starting at `offset: "-1"` with `tail: N`, which is useful for loading the latest N agent events. However, the returned Durable Streams offset continues forward from that page; there is no cursor/API for retrieving the preceding N events.

As a result, React chat UIs must choose between:

- loading all durable history up front, or
- loading only the latest N events with no supported way to fetch older history when the user scrolls upward.

This blocks conventional chat pagination such as “latest 100, then previous 100 on scroll.”

## Requested API

Provide backward history pagination for agent streams. Possible shapes:

```ts
const page = await client.agents.history(name, id, {
  before: cursor,
  limit: 100,
})

page.events
page.previousCursor
page.nextOffset
page.hasMore
```

Or extend the Durable Streams history contract with an opaque backward cursor returned by a `tail=N` read.

## Requirements

- Fetch the latest N durable events without reading the entire stream.
- Fetch the immediately preceding page using an opaque cursor.
- Stable behavior while new live events are appended.
- No duplicate or missing events between pages.
- Compatible with continued live streaming from the initial page's forward offset.
- Suitable for `useFlueAgent` infinite-scroll integration.
- Task/subagent events remain correlated across page boundaries.

## React integration

Ideally `useFlueAgent()` could expose:

```ts
{
  messages,
  hasOlderHistory,
  isLoadingOlderHistory,
  loadOlderHistory(),
}
```

The hook should prepend older messages without disturbing current scroll position or duplicating already-hydrated messages.

## Context

Observed with `@flue/react` / `@flue/sdk` `1.0.0-beta.1`. The current stream contract documents `tail` as modifying only the `-1` start sentinel and concrete offsets as forward-resume coordinates.

title: useFlueAgent should expose atomic history hydration state
body:
## Problem

`useFlueAgent()` replays durable history and updates `messages` incrementally as history batches arrive. Consumers cannot distinguish:

1. initial durable-history catch-up,
2. a complete hydrated transcript, and
3. subsequent live streaming.

For long histories this causes visible layout churn: the transcript repeatedly grows and reorders during page load. It is especially problematic when applications need to derive cross-message structures such as delegated task/session boundaries, because child messages can briefly render in the parent before later history establishes their task identity.

## Requested API

Expose explicit hydration state and an atomic initial snapshot, for example:

```ts
type AgentHydrationStatus =
  | "idle"
  | "loading-history"
  | "ready"
  | "streaming"
  | "reconnecting"
  | "error"

const { messages, hydrationStatus, historyReady } = useFlueAgent(...)
```

A callback or separate promise/snapshot API would also work:

```ts
const history = await client.agents.history(...)
// render an atomic snapshot, then continue live from history.offset
```

## Desired behavior

- Initial catch-up can be withheld until a coherent snapshot is available.
- The hook clearly signals when durable history is complete.
- Live deltas continue from the exact catch-up offset without gaps or duplicate semantic messages.
- Reconnect state is distinguishable from initial hydration.
- Consumers can choose progressive rendering or atomic rendering.
- Task/session projection can be completed before first paint.

## Why status is insufficient today

The current agent status describes connection/submission/streaming behavior, but does not tell the consumer whether full requested history has finished replaying.

## Context

Observed with `@flue/react` / `@flue/sdk` `1.0.0-beta.1`, using `history: "all"` on a persistent agent with a large durable stream.

title: useFlueAgent should preserve delegated task session boundaries
body:
## Problem

Flue emits delegated task activity into the parent agent instance stream with enough correlation metadata to build a task tree (`session`, `parentSession`, `taskId`, `task_start.prompt`, and terminal `task` status/result). However, `useFlueAgent()` flattens child-session messages into the parent `messages` array and drops that metadata.

This makes a delegated subagent's reasoning, tool calls, and answer appear as if they came from the parent conversation. Applications cannot reliably show one collapsed task row or open a dedicated subtask view without opening a second raw SDK event stream and reverse-engineering the React reducer's generated message IDs.

## Current behavior

- Child messages/reasoning/tools are mixed into `useFlueAgent().messages`.
- `UIMessage.metadata` retains model/usage but not session/task identity.
- `task_start` and terminal `task` are not projected by the React reducer.
- The original delegated prompt, task duration/status/result, and nested-task relationship are unavailable through the hook.

## Requested API

Expose first-class task/session information from `useFlueAgent()`, for example:

```ts
{
  messages, // parent-session messages only, or messages carrying session identity
  tasks: [{
    taskId,
    session,
    parentSession,
    prompt,
    agent,
    status,
    startedAt,
    completedAt,
    durationMs,
    result,
    messages,
    tasks,
  }],
}
```

Alternatively, preserve `session`, `parentSession`, `taskId`, timestamps, and event identity in every projected message and expose task lifecycle events separately.

## Requirements

- Parent views can hide child-session activity by default.
- Child sessions can be rendered as dedicated read-only transcript views.
- Original delegated prompts and terminal task results are available.
- Nested tasks retain their immediate parent session.
- No inference from timestamps, message text, or `toolCallId` is required.
- Replay and live updates produce the same task tree.

## Context

Observed with `@flue/react` / `@flue/sdk` `1.0.0-beta.1` and Flue runtime `1.0.0-beta.2`. Raw `AttachedAgentEvent` already contains the required data; the missing layer is the React projection.

Support anthropic models via cloudflare's unified billing
body:
Hey @FredKSchott! Really enjoying playing with flue, you've done a great job here. I essentially build all my projects on cloudflare and have been leaning into cloudflare's AI gateway unified billing so that I don't have to provision keys for openai/anthropic directly. Ran into a bit of an issue where using anthropic's models in this way doesn't quite work. 

I've fixed it locally with a patch. Here's a partial LLM summary of the specific issue and fix. I've cleaned it up and verified these steps by having it re-apply on a bare setup. 

##  Summary

`@flue/runtime` currently does not handle `cloudflare/anthropic/...` model IDs correctly when using the Cloudflare Workers AI binding path.

The built-in Cloudflare binding adapter formats every `cloudflare/...` request as an OpenAI-compatible / Workers AI chat-completions payload. That works for Workers AI model IDs such as `cloudflare/@cf/...`, but fails for Anthropic AI Gateway model IDs such as:

```ts
model: 'cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6'
```

Cloudflare's Anthropic gateway path expects Anthropic Messages API payload shape and Anthropic SSE response parsing.

## Environment

- `@flue/runtime`: `1.0.0-beta.2`
- `@flue/cli`: `1.0.0-beta.1`
- Target: `cloudflare`
- Runtime path: `env.AI.run(...)` via Flue's `cloudflare/...` provider
- Model: `cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`

## Original Failure

Submitting a prompt to an agent configured with `cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` failed with:

```text
Cloudflare AI binding returned 400 Bad Request:
Required value missing: max_tokens.
Invalid value at messages[0].role: Invalid option: expected one of "user"|"assistant"
```

That indicates the request sent to Cloudflare used an OpenAI-style shape:

- system/developer content included inside `messages`
- `max_completion_tokens` or no `max_tokens`
- OpenAI-compatible tool format

Cloudflare's Anthropic endpoint expects:

- top-level `system`, not `messages[].role = "system"`
- `max_tokens`
- Anthropic tool schema (`name`, `description`, `input_schema`)
- Anthropic Messages SSE events on streaming responses

## How I patched it locally

_Note: this may not be the best or even right solution_

I added a Bun patch for `@flue/runtime@1.0.0-beta.2` in:

```text
patches/@flue%2Fruntime@1.0.0-beta.2.patch
```

The patch does three things.

### 1. Route `cloudflare/anthropic/...` through Anthropic parsing

The patch detects:

```ts
model.provider === 'cloudflare' && model.id.startsWith('anthropic/')
```

For those models, it delegates streaming conversion to Pi's existing Anthropic provider implementation (`streamAnthropic`) instead of using the OpenAI-compatible Workers AI stream parser.

The wrapped client still calls Cloudflare's binding:

```ts
env.AI.run('anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6', params, {
  returnRawResponse: true,
  extraHeaders,
  gateway,
})
```

but the request and stream are shaped/parsed as Anthropic Messages API data.

### 2. Normalize `system` for Cloudflare

Pi's Anthropic provider can emit `system` as an array of text blocks. Cloudflare's Anthropic gateway rejected that with:

```text
Invalid value at system: Invalid input: expected string, received array
```

The patch normalizes `system` into a string before passing params to `env.AI.run(...)`.

## Verified Behavior

After applying the patch, a live local request succeeds:

```text
model: cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
prompt: Reply with exactly: pong
response: pong
```

## Proposed Upstream Changes

Flue should treat Cloudflare binding model IDs by model family / gateway provider instead of sending all `cloudflare/...` IDs through one OpenAI-compatible adapter.

_Human Note: Again, not really sure if this is the right fix. Right now it's only the anthropic code path that I know of that doesn't work_. 

Suggested changes:

1. Detect `cloudflare/anthropic/...` model IDs and use Anthropic Messages request construction and Anthropic SSE response parsing.
2. Normalize Anthropic `system` to the shape Cloudflare's Anthropic AI Gateway accepts.
3. Keep existing OpenAI-compatible / Workers AI behavior for `cloudflare/@cf/...`, `cloudflare/openai/...`, and other compatible model IDs.
4. Surface non-2xx binding responses in the Anthropic branch before stream parsing, so provider errors do not turn into empty assistant messages.

## Minimal Reproduction

Configure an agent like this:

```ts
import { createAgent } from '@flue/runtime';

export default createAgent(() => ({
  model: 'cloudflare/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6',
  instructions: 'You are a helpful assistant.',
}));
```

Use Cloudflare target with an `AI` binding:

```jsonc
{
  "ai": { "binding": "AI" }
}
```

Submit a direct prompt to the exposed agent route. Without the patch, Cloudflare rejects the request with the `max_tokens` / invalid system role error.

_Note: If you're trying to reproduce this you'll need unified billing enabled which means you'll need credits in your AI gateway and you'll need to enable authenticated requests and pass the `cf-aig-authorization` header_

flue dev needs configurable watcher ignores for generated project directories
body:
## Summary

`flue dev` recursively watches the project root and filters only a small built-in set of paths after events arrive:

- build output directory (`dist` by default);
- `node_modules`;
- dotfiles / dot-directories, except selected `.flue`;
- editor backup/swap files.

There does not appear to be a documented way to add project-specific ignored directories, and the watcher does not appear to consult `.gitignore`.

That means generated non-dot directories such as `evals/results`, local benchmark output, snapshots, reports, coverage-like custom folders, or tool-generated artifacts can be tracked by `flue dev` even when they are intentionally ignored by Git.

## Why this matters

In downstream testing, an eval harness writes result files under:

```txt
evals/results/
```

That directory is ignored in `.gitignore`, but it is still under the Flue project root. Because `flue dev` watches the root recursively, writes under that directory can be seen as project changes and can trigger rebuild/restart churn.

This is a separate issue from #314:

- #314 is about `flue dev` failing to start when the parent config watcher hits `EMFILE` / `ENOSPC`.
- This issue is about normal project watching having no user-configurable ignore mechanism for generated directories that should not trigger rebuilds.

## Expected behavior

Flue should let projects exclude generated paths from the dev watcher.

Possible approaches:

1. Add a `watch.ignore` / `dev.ignore` config option with glob patterns.
2. Honor `.gitignore` for root-relative paths, perhaps with Flue’s required internal paths re-included.
3. Add a documented CLI flag such as `--ignore <glob>` that can be repeated.

Any of these would be better than requiring app-specific patching of Flue's generated CLI bundle.

## Current downstream workaround

We patched the installed CLI to ignore one project-specific path:

```ts
const EVAL_RESULTS_WATCH_IGNORE = "evals/results";
if (normalized === EVAL_RESULTS_WATCH_IGNORE || normalized.startsWith(`${EVAL_RESULTS_WATCH_IGNORE}/`)) return true;
```

That solved local rebuild churn for the eval harness, but it is not a general solution and should not be necessary for every project with generated output under the repo root.

## Suggested scope

A focused upstream fix could live in `packages/cli/src/lib/dev.ts` around `createWatcher()` / `isIgnoredPath()`:

- extend `WatcherOptions` with additional ignore globs or paths;
- derive those from `flue.config.*`, CLI args, and/or `.gitignore`;
- add tests that writing under an ignored generated directory does not call `onChange`.

This should be independent from the config watcher fallback in #314.

title: flue dev exits when config watcher hits EMFILE/ENOSPC
body:
## Summary

`flue dev` can fail before starting the local development server when the parent process cannot create its config-directory watcher:

```txt
Error: Config watcher failed: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
```

This is especially likely in large repos, repos with many generated files, or developer machines that already have watcher pressure from editors, agents, test runners, Vite/Wrangler, or other dev servers.

## Why this matters

The failure happens in the parent `flue dev` supervisor while watching the resolved config file directory. In the common case where `flue.config.*` lives at the project root, this means a single failed `fs.watch(root)` aborts the entire dev command before the actual Node/Cloudflare local server can run.

That blocks the normal documented development path:

- `flue dev` does not reach the app server startup.
- Cloudflare-target apps never get to Vite/Wrangler.
- Workarounds like running generated Wrangler output directly bypass Flue's normal dev supervisor and are not equivalent to the intended development flow.

## Observed reproduction

Downstream, on a Cloudflare-target Flue app:

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/flue dev --target cloudflare --port 3593
```

failed immediately with:

```txt
Error: Config watcher failed: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
```

Instrumentation of `fs.watch` showed the first failed watch target was the project root:

```txt
[debug-fs-watch] #1 /path/to/project
Error: Config watcher failed: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
```

After a fallback patch, the same normal command started successfully and served `/health`.

## Expected behavior

If the config-directory watcher fails specifically because of watcher resource exhaustion (`EMFILE` or `ENOSPC`), `flue dev` should degrade gracefully instead of aborting.

Since the supervisor already has the exact resolved config file list, it can safely poll those specific files with `fs.watchFile()` as a fallback while preserving config restart behavior.

Non-resource watcher errors should still fail fast.

## Proposed fix

PR #313 implements this:

- catches synchronous `fs.watch(directory)` failures for config directories;
- catches async watcher `error` events;
- falls back to polling the resolved config files for `EMFILE` / `ENOSPC`;
- keeps the current fail-fast behavior for unrelated watcher errors;
- adds a regression test that forces `fs.watch(projectRoot)` to throw `EMFILE`, verifies `flue dev` still starts, and verifies a config edit still restarts the dev session.

## Related PR

Fix proposed in:

- https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/313

title: Add a public API for programmatic workflow admission
body:
## Problem

Flue has a public `dispatch(...)` API for asynchronously submitting input to a created agent from application-owned code, but there is no equivalent public API for starting a workflow run.

Application code such as `app.ts`, `cloudflare.ts`, queue consumers, cron handlers, and other trusted host integrations currently has two unsatisfactory choices:

- submit an in-process HTTP request to the mounted `POST /workflows/<name>` route; or
- import the workflow module and call `run(...)` directly.

The HTTP approach couples internal application code to route exposure, mount paths, request construction, and route authentication. Calling `run(...)` directly is not a valid substitute because it bypasses workflow admission, run identity and persistence, events and streaming, route middleware, and run inspection.

This is especially visible when documenting scheduled work. A Cloudflare `scheduled()` handler can call `dispatch(...)` directly for an agent, but starting a workflow requires routing back through the application HTTP surface. The same issue applies to an in-process Node scheduler.

## Missing functionality

Flue should expose a supported public runtime API for application-owned code to admit a discovered workflow programmatically while preserving the normal workflow-run lifecycle. It should occupy the same conceptual role for workflows that `dispatch(...)` occupies for agents, without requiring callers to know generated runtime internals or synthesize HTTP requests.

The exact API shape is intentionally left open. The important contract is that programmatic invocation creates a real workflow run with the same identity, persistence, events, streaming, inspection, and target-specific behavior as ordinary workflow admission.

## Relevant contexts

- Cloudflare Cron Triggers in `src/cloudflare.ts`
- Node schedulers in `src/app.ts`
- queue and email handlers
- application-owned Hono routes
- trusted internal integrations that need to start finite background work

Generated helpers under `@flue/runtime/internal` and direct workflow Durable Object access should not become the user-facing workaround.

title: Cloudflare direct prompts persist user input but do not append user message events to durable agent stream
body:
### Describe the Bug

Cloudflare direct agent prompts persist the submitted user message into canonical session history, but do not append a corresponding user `message_start` / `message_end` event to the durable agent stream.

That means consumers that rebuild UI state from `GET /agents/:name/:id` / `client.agents.stream()` do not see any `role: "user"` event for direct prompts. The message may appear temporarily in React because `@flue/react` adds a local optimistic message, but after a page refresh the hook replays only the durable stream and the user message is missing.

This appears to contradict the public durability/log contract in the beta blog:

> the source of truth is the log. Durable Streams give us a guaranteed append-only record of everything an agent sees: every human prompt, model response, and tool result is recorded to a durable, replayable stream.

Code path observed on current `main` (`df62fe375c5a5832b380a9588dff319c09cd6a56`) and `v1.0.0-beta.2`:

- `packages/runtime/src/session.ts` persists direct input via `runPersistedDirectSubmissionInput()` by appending a user message to `SessionHistory` with `directSubmissionId`.
- `runPersistedContextInput()` then calls `save()` after `persistInput()` succeeds.
- No user `message_start` / `message_end` event is emitted on that path.
- Cloudflare durable streams only append events emitted through `ctx.subscribeEvent(...)` in `packages/runtime/src/cloudflare/agent-coordinator.ts`, so the persisted direct user input never reaches the event stream.

The React package seems to expect the missing server event:

- `packages/react/src/agent-reducer.ts` has reconciliation logic for a streamed user echo keyed by `submissionId`.
- `apps/docs/src/content/docs/guide/react.md` says: “The stream then reconciles that optimistic message with its durable copy.”

But the runtime does not currently emit that durable copy for Cloudflare direct prompts.

### Expected Behavior

For a Cloudflare direct prompt sent through `POST /agents/:name/:id` or `client.agents.send()`:

1. Flue durably admits the submission.
2. Flue persists the user input into canonical session history.
3. Flue appends a corresponding user message event to the durable agent stream, with the same `submissionId` used for the direct submission.
4. Replaying `client.agents.stream(name, id, { offset: '-1' })` after a page refresh includes the user message as a `role: "user"` message event.

A normal stream replay should be sufficient to reconstruct the conversation transcript. Local optimistic UI state should only be temporary, not the only source of user messages.

The user message event should be emitted only once per submitted input. Retry/recovery paths that find an already-persisted direct input should not append duplicate user events.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or use a basic Cloudflare Flue app with an HTTP-routed agent and the React hook or SDK stream reader.

2. Send a direct prompt:

```ts
await client.agents.send('support-assistant', 'conversation-1', {
  message: 'hello',
});
```

3. Read the durable stream from the beginning, or refresh a React page that rebuilds from stream history:

```ts
for await (const event of client.agents.stream('support-assistant', 'conversation-1', {
  offset: '-1',
  live: false,
})) {
  console.log(event.type, 'message' in event ? event.message : undefined);
}
```

4. Observe that assistant/model/tool events are present, but there is no `message_start` or `message_end` event whose `message.role` is `"user"` for the submitted prompt.

5. If using `@flue/react`, the user message may appear immediately after submit because of local optimistic state. Refresh the page and rebuild from durable stream history: the user message is gone.

### Additional Context

Current package/version check:

- A downstream app pinned to `@flue/runtime@1.0.0-beta.1` shows the behavior.
- `@flue/runtime@1.0.0-beta.2` is the latest published runtime as of 2026-06-19, and the same code path is still present there.
- Current upstream `main` (`df62fe375c5a5832b380a9588dff319c09cd6a56`) also still has the same path.

Implementation direction that would match the documented contract:

- When `runPersistedDirectSubmissionInput()` first appends the canonical user message and `save()` succeeds, emit a durable user `message_end` event, or both `message_start` and `message_end` for consistency.
- Include the direct submission's `submissionId` so React/SDK consumers can reconcile it with the optimistic local message (`submission:${submissionId}:user:0`).
- Do not emit on retries where `findDirectSubmissionInput(submissionId)` already finds the input.

Expose a remote abort endpoint for a running agent prompt (the HTTP half of #49)
body:
## Problem

#49 shipped the **in-process** abort (`session.prompt(text, { signal })` / `CallHandle.abort()`), which works great when you hold the handle. But it also proposed an **HTTP / remote** abort — *"expose a run id and provide an abort endpoint"* — for streamed / SDK-driven callers. That half moved to discussion #91 ("Agent lifecycle control API") and closed without landing.

The result: apps that drive agents over `@flue/sdk` (`agents.send` / `agents.stream`) have **no way to stop a running turn**. Passing a `signal` to `agents.send` only cancels the client's wait — it does not stop the server-side run (the request-abort is a no-op server-side). For a headless app that wants a reliable "Stop" button, there's currently no supported mechanism.

Notably, the hard part already exists in the runtime: `agent-submissions.ts` holds the `CallHandle` and wires an incoming `AbortSignal` to `handle.abort(reason)` (today used for shutdown). So the cancellation machinery is in place — what's missing is an **external trigger**.

## Proposal

Expose the existing cancellation over the transport:

1. A `POST /agents/:name/:id/abort` (or `/runs/:runId/abort`) endpoint that aborts that instance's in-flight submission via the existing signal → `handle.abort()` path, without deleting the session or losing conversation history.
2. An `agents.abort(name, id)` method on the SDK client.

This is the HTTP counterpart to the in-process API from #49, reusing the runtime's existing abort wiring.

## Why

Stop / interrupt is the one piece of agent control that SDK / remote-driven apps can't do today, even though the runtime already supports it internally. It also provides a clean basis for "stop + resend" steering on top of the durable session store.

Happy to open a PR — the abort plumbing already exists, so this is largely a route + a small controller registry + the SDK method.

title: Forward per-call model / thinkingLevel through agents.send / agents.prompt
body:
## Problem

`FlueSession.prompt(text, options)` already accepts per-call `model` and `thinkingLevel` via `PromptOptions`, but the SDK / HTTP path drops them. As a result, apps driving agents through `@flue/sdk` (`agents.send` / `agents.prompt`) cannot change the model or reasoning effort **between turns** without tearing down and recreating the session — the agent's model is effectively fixed at agent-factory time.

The gap is purely in the transport surface:

- SDK: `AgentPromptOptions` (`packages/sdk/src/public/invoke.ts`) is only `{ message, images?, signal? }`.
- Runtime: the direct-agent request body schema (`packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts`) is `{ message, images? }`.

So even though the underlying primitive supports per-call overrides, there's no way to pass them over the wire.

## Proposal

Surface the existing `PromptOptions.model` / `PromptOptions.thinkingLevel` through the SDK + HTTP path:

1. Add optional `model?: string` and `thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel` to `AgentPromptOptions` and forward them in the request body in `promptAgent` / `sendAgent` (same shape as the existing `images` passthrough).
2. Allow `model` and `thinkingLevel` in the direct-agent body schema.
3. Pass them into the `session.prompt(...)` call in `agent-submissions.ts`.

Per-call values already override agent defaults at the `PromptOptions` layer, so this is additive and a no-op when omitted.

## Why

This enables a common interactive flow for headless / daemon-driven apps: "switch model (or change reasoning effort), then send the next message" — currently only achievable by recreating the session. It's a small, backwards-compatible change that just exposes a capability the runtime already has.

Happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

title: Make the React agent stream transport configurable
body:
## Request

Please allow `useFlueAgent` consumers to choose the live stream transport, including SSE. Alternatively, consider making SSE the default React behavior.

## Use case

We want a browser client to maintain one continuous SSE connection for live agent events. Currently, `useFlueAgent` passes `live: true`, which selects long-polling, and the hook does not expose a way to request `live: "sse"`. This results in repeated requests as event batches and offsets advance, even though the SDK already supports SSE.

An API such as the following would solve this:

```ts
useFlueAgent({
  client,
  name,
  id,
  live: "sse",
})
```

A `transport: "sse" | "long-poll"` option would also be clear. The important part is that React consumers can select SSE without replacing or patching the hook.

title: OpenAPI response schemas omit submissionId returned by agent prompt endpoints
body:
## 1. Problem

The mounted Flue runtime returns `submissionId` from agent prompt responses, and the public SDK/React consumers treat that field as part of the response contract. However, the public OpenAPI response schemas for the same POST route omit `submissionId`.

This creates a contract drift between the runtime/clients/tests and the machine-readable `/openapi.json` contract.

Source anchors:

- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:37` declares `AgentAdmissionResponseSchema`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:38` declares `streamUrl: v.string()`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:39` declares `offset: v.string()`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:42` declares `AgentInvocationResponseSchema`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:43` declares `result: v.unknown()`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:44` declares `streamUrl: v.string()`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/schemas.ts:45` declares `offset: v.string()`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:451` uses `jsonResponse(AgentAdmissionResponseSchema, 'Prompt accepted.')` for the 202 response.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:456` uses `resolver(AgentInvocationResponseSchema)` for the 200 synchronous result response.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/handle-agent.ts:180` returns `{ streamUrl, offset, submissionId: receipt.submissionId }` for prompt admission.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/handle-agent.ts:490` to `packages/runtime/src/runtime/handle-agent.ts:494` serializes `result`, `streamUrl`, `offset`, and `submissionId` for the synchronous result response.
- `packages/sdk/src/public/invoke.ts:27` declares `submissionId: string` on `AgentSendResult`.
- `packages/react/src/agent-session.ts:68` consumes `receipt.submissionId` to dispatch `local_send_admitted`.
- `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts:297` to `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts:300` asserts that the 202 response body includes `submissionId`.
- `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts:368` to `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts:372` asserts that the 200 response body includes `submissionId`.

## 2. Reproduction

Use a runtime manifest with an HTTP-enabled attached agent, mount `flue()`, and inspect the generated `/openapi.json` route for:

- `POST /agents/{name}/{id}` 202 response
- `POST /agents/{name}/{id}` 200 response when using synchronous result mode

The response schemas are built from `AgentAdmissionResponseSchema` and `AgentInvocationResponseSchema`, but those schemas currently do not contain `submissionId`.

Then call the same runtime route:

- A normal prompt admission returns `streamUrl`, `offset`, and `submissionId`.
- A synchronous result response returns `result`, `streamUrl`, `offset`, and `submissionId`.

The runtime tests already assert the response body shape, but the OpenAPI schema side does not currently encode the same shape.

## 3. Impact

This does not break the runtime handler itself. The runtime still returns `submissionId`.

The impact is on integrations that rely on `/openapi.json` as the public machine-readable contract:

- OpenAPI-generated clients may not expose `submissionId`.
- Strict response validators may treat `submissionId` as an undeclared response field.
- API docs generated from OpenAPI will omit a field that the SDK and React package already rely on.
- Consumers may miss the correlation identifier needed to connect the admitted prompt with attached agent events.

## 4. Existing issue / PR coverage

I checked existing issues and PRs for the affected schema/type names and behavior:

- `submissionId OpenAPI`
- `AgentAdmissionResponseSchema`
- `AgentSendResult submissionId`

Related but not duplicate:

- #266 reports that public OpenAPI omits Durable Streams `GET/HEAD` read routes exposed by runtime. This is the same broad class of OpenAPI contract drift, but it is route-surface drift.

This issue is different: the POST route is already present in OpenAPI, but its response body schemas omit `submissionId`.

Coverage conclusion: not covered by #266 or the existing related OpenAPI work.

## 5. Should this be fixed?

Yes, if `/openapi.json` is intended to describe the public mounted runtime API.

`submissionId` is not just an incidental extra field: it is returned by the runtime, required by the public SDK type, consumed by the React session state machine, and asserted by runtime routing tests.

## 6. Proposed fix

Add `submissionId: v.string()` to both response schemas:

- `AgentAdmissionResponseSchema`
- `AgentInvocationResponseSchema`

Then add or update an OpenAPI-focused test so the generated schema for `POST /agents/{name}/{id}` includes `submissionId` in both:

- the 202 prompt admission response
- the 200 synchronous result response

Suggested validation:

```bash
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime test -- --run packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts -t "openapi.json"
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime test
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime check:types
```

Non-goals:

- Do not change runtime response behavior.
- Do not change Durable Streams route behavior.
- Do not change SDK or React semantics except as needed to keep generated API contracts aligned.

title: SQLITE_TOOBIG persisting large text/tool-output session entries (follow-up to #240, which only chunked images)
body:
### Describe the bug

Follow-up to #240 (closed/completed). The fix for #240 split sessions into per-entry rows and chunks **image** content across `flue_image_chunks` (256 KB/chunk), which keeps image data under Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite's ~2 MB per-cell string/blob limit. But the same overflow still occurs for **large non-image text entries** — a single tool result or verbose model turn whose JSON `data` cell exceeds 2 MB.

In `@flue/runtime` 1.0.0-beta.1, `createSqlAgentExecutionStore*` (the Cloudflare DO path) persists session state across three tables, but each entry's text content is stored as **one un-chunked `data` cell**:

```ts
// flue_session_entries — one row per entry, but `data` is a single JSON cell
INSERT INTO flue_session_entries (session_id, entry_id, position, data)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
ON CONFLICT (session_id, entry_id) DO UPDATE SET ...
// (data = JSON.stringify(entry) with images extracted out)

// flue_sessions — session header, also a single JSON cell
INSERT INTO flue_sessions (id, data) VALUES (?, ?)
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET data = excluded.data
```

Image blocks are extracted and chunked (`flue_image_chunks`, `IMAGE_DATA_CHUNK_LENGTH = 256 * 1024`), so images are safe. The remaining **text** `data` is stored whole. When a tool returns a large text payload (web search / full-page extraction / deep-research output) — or a model turn is very long — `JSON.stringify(entry)` for that single entry can exceed the 2 MB per-value limit and the save fails:

```
FlueError: direct(<submission-id>) failed: string or blob too big: SQLITE_TOOBIG
    at Session.throwIfError
```

This interrupts otherwise-valid agent runs and is non-deterministic (depends on per-run tool-output size).

### Expected behavior

Persist sessions containing large **text** entries without exceeding the per-cell limit — i.e. give text the same treatment images already get. Options:

- Chunk/externalize large entry `data` the way image blocks are chunked (a text analog of `flue_image_chunks`), rehydrating on load so model context is unchanged.
- And/or compress entry `data` (e.g. gzip) before storing.
- And/or spill oversized entries to R2 with a pointer, deleting on session/tree deletion.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy a Cloudflare-target Flue agent using Durable Object SQLite persistence, with one or more tools that can return large text payloads (e.g. web research or full-page extraction).
2. Ask a question that triggers a large text tool result (hundreds of KB to >2 MB) within a single entry.
3. Observe the session save fail with `string or blob too big: SQLITE_TOOBIG`.

### Version

`@flue/runtime` 1.0.0-beta.1 — Cloudflare Workers target (Durable Object SQLite backend).

### Additional context

- Hit repeatedly in a model bake-off eval harness across several models (grok, glm, kimi, nemotron); non-deterministic across runs.
- App-side workaround we're applying: cap tool-output size (~256–512 KB/result) so no single entry approaches the limit. That avoids the crash but truncates legitimately large research output — hence this framework-side request to handle large text entries the way images are already handled.

title: Expose a terminal result/state observation path for dispatched agent runs
body:
Flue agent `dispatch(...)` currently appears to return an acceptance receipt, but consumers that delegate work to a native agent also need a supported way to observe the run through completion.

## Requested capability

- Start an agent run and receive a stable run/dispatch id.
- Observe terminal state: succeeded, failed, canceled, or timed out.
- Retrieve the terminal result or structured error.
- Correlate intermediate events/logs with that run id.
- Support stale-result protection so callers can ignore older runs when a newer run supersedes them.

## Why this matters

- App code currently has to build bespoke callback routes or side-channel storage to learn when native agent work completes.
- That makes native-agent adoption harder to test end to end.
- A first-class result/state API would let consumers remove custom callback protocols and treat native agent state as the durable authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- A caller can dispatch an agent run and later query or subscribe to its terminal outcome.
- The API works without exposing the agent publicly.
- The result path is deterministic enough for integration tests.
- Docs include the recommended pattern for replacing custom callback routes.

title: Add React hook/client support for proxied Flue agent state and callable methods

## Request

Add a first-class React/client API for connecting to a Flue agent through an application-owned proxy route, rather than requiring a direct public Flue route.

## Use case

Internal agent runs Flue behind a private Cloudflare service binding. Browser traffic must go through the web Worker so existing CF Access, app group checks, Salesforce OAuth, and per-case authorization remain authoritative.

We want to replace a custom SSE/view adapter with an official Flue React hook/client, but the hook needs to support this shape:

- connect through `/api/...` proxy routes
- receive replayable sequenced state/events
- call typed agent methods/actions through the same proxy boundary
- preserve app-owned auth headers/cookies
- avoid exposing the Flue Worker publicly

## Needed API shape

Something like:

```ts
useAgent({
  endpoint: "/api/cases/:caseNumber/agent",
  transport: "proxy",
  agentId: `case:${caseNumber}`,
})

title: Cloudflare sandbox shell calls throw DataCloneError due to non-cloneable AbortSignal
body:
> _Originally reported by @ghostwriternr in [#279](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/279)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

The `cloudflareSandbox()` adapter in `packages/runtime/src/cloudflare/cf-sandbox.ts` forwards the operation `AbortSignal` into `@cloudflare/sandbox`'s `getSandbox(...).exec(...)`. That call crosses a Durable Object RPC boundary where options are structured-cloned, and `AbortSignal` is not structured-cloneable. As a result, every sandbox-backed shell call (`harness.shell()`, `session.shell()`, and the model's `bash` tool) throws before the command even runs:

```
DataCloneError: AbortSignal serialization is not enabled.
```

This means shell execution through the Cloudflare sandbox adapter is completely broken — no command can succeed.

### Expected Behavior

Shell calls through the Cloudflare sandbox adapter should execute successfully. Only structured-cloneable options (`cwd`, `env`, `timeout`) should be sent across the Durable Object RPC boundary. Abort handling should remain local to the Flue runtime: an already-aborted call should reject up front, and an in-flight abort should surface as an `AbortError` once the remote command returns.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a Flue project using the Cloudflare target with `cloudflareSandbox()` configured (e.g., based on `examples/cloudflare/`).
2. Invoke any sandbox-backed shell call — for example, `harness.shell()`, `session.shell()`, or trigger the model's `bash` tool.
3. Observe a `DataCloneError: AbortSignal serialization is not enabled.` thrown before the command executes.

---

Original implementation from [#279](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/279) by @ghostwriternr

title: Keep Cloudflare Sandbox cancellation local
body:
Flue's `cloudflareSandbox()` adapter forwarded the operation `AbortSignal` into `@cloudflare/sandbox`'s `getSandbox(...).exec(...)`. That call crosses a Durable Object RPC boundary where options are structured-cloned and `AbortSignal` is not cloneable, so every sandbox-backed shell call (`harness.shell()`, `session.shell()`, and the model's `bash` tool) threw before running:

    DataCloneError: AbortSignal serialization is not enabled.

Stop sending the signal across that boundary. Only cloneable options (`cwd`, `env`, native `timeout`) reach the sandbox. Flue keeps its local pre/post abort checks, so an already-aborted call still rejects up front and an in-flight abort still surfaces as `AbortError` once the remote command returns. This matches Flue's `SandboxApi` contract, where `signal` is optional and `timeoutMs` is the portable cancellation mechanism.

Shortcoming: a long-running command can't be cancelled mid-flight and runs until it finishes or hits its `timeout`. That never worked on this path anyway (it threw); real remote cancellation needs a cloneable protocol in the Sandbox SDK, which is out of scope here.

title: Add trusted handlers for addressable agent submissions
body:
## Problem

Addressable agents currently process every `dispatch()` input through the coordinator model. Trusted application code can configure the agent and expose model-callable tools, but it cannot handle a typed dispatched command with access to the initialized Flue session.

This blocks applications that need deterministic orchestration around named subagents. A concrete example is Support Seal proposal generation:

- trusted Worker code hydrates Salesforce and derives verified customer scope;
- bounded router and proposal-writer profiles perform reasoning;
- trusted code must select the exact result schema, tools, retry/repair count, and companion escalation pass;
- image bytes must be attached directly to `proposal-writer` with `session.task(..., { agent, result, tools, images, signal })`;
- image bytes must not pass through coordinator text, tool output, or persisted JSON commands.

`dispatch()` accepts JSON only, `createAgent()` initialization receives no session/harness, and custom tools intentionally receive no session handle. Direct HTTP images attach to the coordinator turn and do not propagate to isolated named subagents.

## Proposed API

Add an optional trusted handler for addressable dispatched submissions, for example:

```ts
export default createAgent<Command, Env>(({ id, env }) => ({
  model: resolveModel(env),
  subagents: [proposalWriter],
  onDispatch: async ({ input, session, signal, dispatchId }) => {
    const context = await prepareTrustedContext(input, env)
    const { data } = await session.task(JSON.stringify(context.args), {
      agent: "proposal-writer",
      result: context.schema,
      tools: context.tools,
      images: context.images,
      signal,
    })
    return await context.finalize(data)
  },
}))
```

Naming is flexible (`onDispatch`, `handleSubmission`, typed command handlers, etc.). Important properties:

1. Runs only in trusted application code, not as a model-callable tool.
2. Receives the initialized submission `FlueSession` (or a narrower trusted task runner), parsed input, abort signal, and submission/dispatch correlation.
3. Can invoke named profiles using existing `session.task()` options, including structured result schemas, dynamic tools, and images.
4. Uses the existing durable submission lifecycle: admission, FIFO ordering, canonical input application, journaling, interruption handling, and terminal settlement.
5. Direct prompts can retain current model-driven behavior; the handler may initially apply only to `dispatch()` commands.
6. Handler output is the submission result and is observable through the normal stream/result surfaces.

A narrower alternative would expose a trusted `task()` runner instead of the full session.

## Implementation observation

The internal boundary already exists in `processSubmission()`: it calls `createAgentSubmissionSessionHandler(...)`, receives the initialized internal session, then calls `session.processSubmissionInput(...)`. The smallest implementation may be to select the configured trusted dispatch handler at this point while preserving the existing `onInputApplied`, timeout, abort, journal, and settlement callbacks.

## Why not an application workaround?

- Encoding base64 images in tool/model text is not multimodal and expands sensitive persistence/telemetry.
- Direct-agent `{ message, images }` attaches images to the coordinator, not the isolated named subagent.
- Adding a workflow only to obtain `ctx.init()` recreates a workflow primitive the persistent-agent architecture is removing.
- Giving model-callable tools a session handle would weaken the current clean authority boundary.

This would also enable deterministic application command handling beyond images: schema-selected specialist calls, bounded repair loops, routing pipelines, and other agent-native orchestration without forcing a coordinator model turn.

title: Public OpenAPI omits Durable Streams GET/HEAD routes exposed by runtime
body:
## 1. Problem

The mounted Flue runtime exposes Durable Streams read endpoints as part of its public route surface, but the public `/openapi.json` contract does not include those read endpoints.

Source anchors:

- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:257` to `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:263` lists the mounted public routes, including:
  - `GET/HEAD /agents/:name/:id`
  - `GET/HEAD /runs/:runId`
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:283` to `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:292` registers `/agents/:name/:id`, with non-POST requests routed to `agentRouteHandler`.
- `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:295` to `packages/runtime/src/runtime/flue-app.ts:296` registers `/runs/:runId` through `runStreamReadHandler`.
- `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts:208` to `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts:234` currently asserts that public OpenAPI contains only:
  - `/workflows/{name}` with `post`
  - `/agents/{name}/{id}` with `post`

This creates a contract drift between runtime behavior and the machine-readable OpenAPI contract. The runtime exposes stream read routes, while `/openapi.json` advertises only POST invocation routes.

### Reproduction

Use a runtime manifest with one HTTP-enabled agent and one HTTP-enabled workflow, mount `flue()` under `/api`, then request `/api/openapi.json`.

Current observed OpenAPI paths:

```json
{
  "/workflows/{name}": ["post"],
  "/agents/{name}/{id}": ["post"]
}
```

Missing from the OpenAPI contract:

- `GET/HEAD /agents/{name}/{id}`
- `GET/HEAD /runs/{runId}`

I also verified this with a minimal local Vitest repro against the latest synced `main` commit `aefd6ec791f3f88f5ed37b23ab9b4c0f0e5203a3`. The repro passed by confirming:

- `body.paths["/runs/{runId}"]` is absent.
- `body.paths["/agents/{name}/{id}"]` only contains `post`.
- `body.paths["/workflows/{name}"]` only contains `post`.

### Impact

This does not prevent users from manually calling the runtime stream routes. The runtime route still exists.

The impact is on integrations that rely on `/openapi.json` as the machine-readable public API contract:

- OpenAPI-generated clients will not contain a method for reading run events.
- API explorers and generated SDK docs will not show the stream read entry points.
- Contract validators or allowlists based on OpenAPI may treat `GET /runs/:runId` as an undeclared request.
- Users can start a workflow or agent invocation from the OpenAPI-visible POST route, but cannot discover the follow-up event stream route from the same machine-readable contract.

So the issue is not a broken handler; it is an incomplete public API contract for the runtime surface already exposed by Flue.

## 2. Existing issue / PR coverage

I checked existing open and closed issues and PRs using the affected route names, files, and behavior keywords.

Searches included:

- `openapi /runs`
- `flue-app openapi Durable Streams`
- `routing.test.ts openapi agents workflows`
- `streamUrl openapi agents runs`

Relevant result:

- PR #130, "Add run registry, admin API, and manual SDK scaffold", is related but does not cover this issue. It added run registry/admin API/SDK work and touched runtime OpenAPI areas, but the current public `/openapi.json` still omits the GET/HEAD stream read routes.

Coverage conclusion: not covered.

## 3. Should this be fixed?

Yes, this is worth fixing if `/openapi.json` is intended to describe the public mounted runtime API.

The fix is focused and low-risk: either document the stream read routes in OpenAPI, or explicitly decide that these routes are intentionally outside the OpenAPI public contract and adjust the route comments and POST descriptions accordingly.

Given the current runtime comments and route behavior, documenting the routes in OpenAPI appears to be the more consistent direction.

## 4. Proposed fix / PR draft

Add OpenAPI route specs for the Durable Streams read endpoints:

- `GET /agents/:name/:id`
- `HEAD /agents/:name/:id`, if the OpenAPI integration supports documenting HEAD separately
- `GET /runs/:runId`
- `HEAD /runs/:runId`, if supported

Implementation direction:

```ts
app.get(
  '/agents/:name/:id',
  describeRoute(agentStreamReadRouteSpec() as DescribeRouteOptions),
  validated('param', AgentRouteParamSchema),
  agentRouteHandler,
);

app.get(
  '/runs/:runId',
  describeRoute(runStreamReadRouteSpec() as DescribeRouteOptions),
  runStreamReadHandler,
);
```

Keep the existing `app.all(...)` handlers after the documented GET/HEAD routes so the current method fallback and canonical error envelope behavior remains intact.

The `runStreamReadRouteSpec()` should document:

- path parameter: `runId`
- query parameter: `meta`
- stream read semantics for Durable Streams
- relevant error envelopes, including not found and method not allowed

The `agentStreamReadRouteSpec()` should document:

- path parameters: `name`, `id`
- stream read semantics for the attached agent interaction
- relevant error envelopes

Tests should update the current OpenAPI assertion in `packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts` so the spec is expected to include the stream routes:

```ts
expect(body.paths).toMatchObject({
  '/workflows/{name}': { post: expect.any(Object) },
  '/agents/{name}/{id}': {
    post: expect.any(Object),
    get: expect.any(Object),
  },
  '/runs/{runId}': {
    get: expect.any(Object),
  },
});
```

Suggested validation:

```bash
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime test -- --run packages/runtime/test/routing.test.ts -t "openapi.json"
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime test
pnpm --filter @flue/runtime check:types
```

Non-goals:

- Do not change Durable Streams runtime behavior.
- Do not change the invocation POST route behavior.
- Do not change admin API behavior.

title: Bare skill specifiers from dependency packages fail to resolve
body:
> _Originally reported by @pupuking723 in [#249](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/249)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

The Vite skill reference plugin (`vite-skill-reference-plugin.ts`) treats all `SKILL.md` specifiers as project-relative paths. When a skill is imported from an external dependency package (e.g. a workspace package linked via symlink), the plugin fails to resolve the specifier because it only looks relative to the project root. This means reusable skill packages published as npm dependencies or used across a pnpm/yarn workspace cannot be imported by consumers.

Additionally, the bundled skill identity for dependency imports is derived from the consumer project's relative path rather than a stable package-based path, making the identity unstable across different consumers.

### Expected Behavior

Bare `SKILL.md` specifiers (e.g. `my-skill-package/SKILL.md`) should be resolved through Vite's standard module resolution, allowing them to traverse package-manager layouts such as symlinked workspace packages and `node_modules`. Relative and absolute skill imports should continue to use the existing project-root containment checks. The bundled skill identity for dependency imports should use a stable, package-based path that does not depend on the consumer project's directory structure.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!-- Either starting from one of the examples in `examples/`, or from a basic hello world. -->

1. Set up a pnpm workspace with a reusable skill package that exports a `SKILL.md` file (see `examples/imported-skill/` for reference).
2. In a consumer project within the same workspace, import the skill using a bare specifier (e.g. `my-skill-package/SKILL.md`).
3. Build the consumer project — the skill reference plugin fails to resolve the bare specifier because it is treated as a project-relative path rather than being resolved through Vite/module resolution.

---

Original implementation from [#249](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/249) by @pupuking723

fix(runtime): move large session blobs out of entry rows
body:
Builds on the session-entry storage added in `main` by moving large inline session payloads out of each entry JSON row.

## Summary

- Stores image/blob/document/file payloads in `flue_session_blobs` instead of inline in `flue_session_entries.data`.
- Chunks blob data in SQL by default, so built-in Node SQLite and Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite avoid oversized cells without extra configuration.
- Adds `SessionAttachmentStore` for optional external blob storage.
- Wires Cloudflare to use an R2 binding named `FLUE_SESSION_ATTACHMENTS` when present.
- Exposes the same attachment-store option from the Node SQLite adapter for filesystem, S3-compatible, or application-provided stores.
- Keeps SQL as the authoritative manifest for blob references and cleanup state.
- Adds retry tracking for failed external object deletes.
- Adds schema migration handling for intermediate `flue_session_blobs` schemas.

## Behavior

Without external attachment storage, blobs remain in SQL chunk rows.

On Cloudflare, defining an R2 binding named `FLUE_SESSION_ATTACHMENTS` stores large blobs externally in R2. Without that binding, Cloudflare falls back to SQL chunk rows.

On Node SQLite, callers can pass a custom `attachmentStore`; otherwise Node keeps using SQL chunk rows.

Fixes https://github.com/withastro/flue/issues/240

title: fix(runtime): store SQL sessions as entries with chunked blobs
body:
Fixes session persistence failures on Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite when session history contains large inline image/blob content.

This changes SQL-backed session storage from one JSON blob per session to:

- one metadata row per session
- one row per session entry
- chunked external rows for image/blob/document/file content

Large image data is rehydrated on session load, so model context remains unchanged while avoiding Cloudflare SQLite’s 2MB per-cell string/blob limit in normal usage.

Fixes #240

**NOTE** This is just one approach – another would be to persist large attachments to an external object store, like R2 – will explore that in a separate PR

title: SQLITE_TOOBIG when sessions are larger than 2MB
body:
### Describe the Bug

Cloudflare deployments can fail to persist agent sessions when session history contains large inline image content.

In Flue 0.11.0, image bytes are redacted from runtime events/run history, but persisted session history still stores the full `SessionData` object as a single JSON string in `flue_sessions.data` via `SqlSessionStore.save()`:

```ts
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO flue_sessions (id, data, updated_at)
VALUES (?, ?, ?)
```

On Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite, a single string/blob value is limited to 2MB. If a session contains a large image, or enough accumulated history, `JSON.stringify(sessionData)` can exceed that limit and the session save fails with:

```txt
Error: string or blob too big: SQLITE_TOOBIG
    at SqlSessionStore.save
```

This can interrupt otherwise valid agent runs. The durable-session storage shape seems to need a more granular design, ideally one row per session entry plus externalized or chunked blob/image content for large attachments.

### Expected Behavior

Flue should persist sessions containing large images or attachments without exceeding Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite’s per-cell string/blob limit.

A robust design might:

- Store session metadata separately from session entries.
- Store each `SessionEntry` as its own row instead of one JSON blob for the whole session.
- Externalize or chunk large image/blob/document content referenced by an entry.
- Rehydrate externalized content on session load so model context remains unchanged.
- Delete associated externalized blobs when the session/session tree is deleted.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a Cloudflare-target Flue agent using Durable Object SQLite persistence.
2. Send a prompt/skill/task call with an attached image large enough that the persisted `SessionData` JSON exceeds Cloudflare’s 2MB string/blob limit.
3. Observe session persistence fail with `SQLITE_TOOBIG`, for example:

```txt
Error: string or blob too big: SQLITE_TOOBIG
    at SqlSessionStore.save
```

title: Extend grep tool with literal matching option and improved descriptions
