- Use extended grep regex by default, matching the regex flavor agents tend to produce.
- Add an optional literal/fixed-string mode for exact code searches.
- Update the tool and parameter descriptions so agents know which mode they are using.

title: Clarify grep regex behavior and support literal searches
body:
The built-in grep tool currently describes its pattern parameter only as a regex, but the implementation runs plain grep -rn, which uses POSIX basic regular expressions. That creates a mismatch with the patterns agents naturally emit.
 
From my experience building an agent using gpt5.5 as the model, it often search's with extended-regex style patterns such as alternation, groups, and common quantifiers:
 
txt
foo|bar
defineThing|createThing\(
status\?\.message
 
With plain grep, these patterns can fail or behave differently than intended, forcing the agent to spend an extra turn recovering and retrying with a different command.
 
A simple switch to grep -E helps for model-authored regex patterns, but it also makes literal code searches more error-prone. Common code fragments such as foo(), a || b, i++, { name }, or value? contain regex metacharacters and should often be searched exactly rather than interpreted as regex.
 
The tool should make the matching mode explicit:
 
- Use extended grep regex by default, matching the regex flavor agents tend to produce.
- Add an optional literal/fixed-string mode for exact code searches.
- Update the tool and parameter descriptions so agents know which mode they are using.

title: feat(runtime): add withSkillName to alias packaged skills
body:
fixes #231 
## Description
This PR resolves an issue where it was previously impossible to rename a packaged skill at the point of consumption, leading to namespace collisions if an imported skill shared the same name as a workspace skill.

### Changes Made
- Added `withSkillName(skill, name)` in `@flue/runtime` to create a shallow clone of a registered skill with a new alias.
- Updated `buildPackagedSkillPrompt` to use the packaged skill's original directory name when parsing `SKILL.md` frontmatter, ensuring that framework validations (which require the frontmatter `name` to match the directory) succeed even when the skill is aliased.

## Testing
- Added `withSkillName()` unit tests in `agent-definition.test.ts`.
- Added an integration test in `session-skills.test.ts` simulating a name collision between a workspace skill and a packaged skill, demonstrating that `withSkillName` successfully aliases the packaged skill and properly loads the instructions.
- Verified locally with `pnpm run check:types` and `pnpm run test`.

title: No way to rename or alias a skill at consumption, so same-named skills cannot coexist
body:
### Describe the Bug

There is no way to rename a skill at the point of consumption, so two skills that happen to share a name cannot both be attached to the same agent.

A skill's name is fixed by its author in two coupled places: the `name` field in SKILL.md frontmatter, and the skill's directory name. The frontmatter parser enforces that they match (`packages/runtime/src/skill-frontmatter.ts`), per the Agent Skills format. The runtime then treats that name as the unique key everywhere:

- `defineAgentProfile()` / agent validation rejects duplicate skill names in a `skills` array (`packages/runtime/src/agent-definition.ts`).
- Harness initialization throws if a registered skill's name collides with a workspace-discovered skill from `.agents/skills/` (`[flue] Skill name "X" appears in both agent definition and workspace discovery.`, `packages/runtime/src/context.ts`).

When the colliding skill is one you authored, the fix is easy: rename the directory and frontmatter together. But when the skill directory was authored elsewhere — e.g. vendored/copied from another repository in the standard Agent Skills format — renaming requires editing the third-party SKILL.md and directory, i.e. forking content you don't own and re-applying the edit on every update. There is no consumer-side escape hatch.

This is asymmetric with tools: a `ToolDefinition` is a plain object, so consumers can trivially rename a colliding tool with `{ ...tool, name: 'other' }`. Skills have no equivalent because the name is baked into the packaged directory contents, and a `SkillReference` is resolved against packaged content that still declares the original name.

### Expected Behavior

A consumer should be able to register a skill under an alias without modifying the skill's files, with the alias used consistently for registration, collision checks, the system prompt's skill catalog, and `activate_skill` — while the underlying SKILL.md body and supporting files remain unchanged. For example (API shape illustrative only):

```ts
import review from '../vendor/review/SKILL.md' with { type: 'skill' };

const agent = createAgent(() => ({
	model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5',
	// project already has .agents/skills/review/ — alias the imported one
	skills: [withSkillName(review, 'vendor-review')],
}));
```

Failing that, the duplicate-name errors should at least point at a documented resolution path for skills the consumer does not author.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Starting from `examples/imported-skill/`, copy a skill directory authored elsewhere (any Agent Skills-format directory whose SKILL.md declares `name: review`) into the project, e.g. `src/vendor/review/`.
2. Create a workspace skill with the same name at `.agents/skills/review/SKILL.md`, and register the vendored skill on the agent via `import review from '../vendor/review/SKILL.md' with { type: 'skill' }` and `skills: [review]`.
3. Initialize the agent. Initialization fails with `[flue] Skill name "review" appears in both agent definition and workspace discovery.` The only resolution is editing the vendored skill's frontmatter and directory name, since frontmatter and directory must match and no rename/alias mechanism exists.

title: Skills cannot be imported from npm packages
body:
### Describe the Bug

Skills cannot be distributed or consumed via npm packages. The `SKILL.md` import mechanism only works for skill directories that live inside the consuming project itself.

Three constraints in the skill packaging plugin (`packages/cli/src/lib/vite-skill-reference-plugin.ts`) prevent importing a skill from a dependency:

1. **No bare specifier resolution.** Skill import specifiers are resolved relative to the importing file (`path.resolve(path.dirname(importerPath), declaration.specifier)`) instead of going through module resolution, so `import skill from '@acme/cvss-score/SKILL.md' with { type: 'skill' }` fails to resolve.
2. **Project-root containment check.** The resolved skill directory must be inside the project root, which excludes anything in `node_modules` even when reachable via a relative path.
3. **Symlink rejection.** Symlinks anywhere on the skill path cause a hard error, which rules out pnpm's symlinked `node_modules` layout even if the other constraints were relaxed.

As a result there is no way to publish a skill (a `SKILL.md` plus its supporting files) as a reusable package and import it into a Flue project. The only supported sources are workspace-discovered skills (`.agents/skills/`) and relative imports within the project.

### Expected Behavior

A skill published in an npm package should be importable with the same syntax used for local skills:

```ts
import cvssScore from '@acme/cvss-score/SKILL.md' with { type: 'skill' };

const agent = createAgent(() => ({
	model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5',
	skills: [cvssScore],
}));
```

The plugin should resolve bare specifiers through normal module resolution, allow skill directories that resolve into dependencies, and tolerate the package-manager symlink layouts (e.g. pnpm) while keeping the existing safety checks (sensitive-file exclusion, directory traversal limits) intact for the resolved real path.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an npm package (or workspace package) containing `skills/review/SKILL.md` with valid frontmatter, and depend on it from a Flue project such as `examples/imported-skill/`.
2. In an agent or workflow module, add `import review from '<package-name>/skills/review/SKILL.md' with { type: 'skill' };` and register it via `skills: [review]`.
3. Run `flue build` (or dev). The import fails to resolve because the specifier is treated as a relative path; pointing at the dependency via a relative `node_modules` path instead fails the project-root containment or symlink checks.

title: Replace WebSocket/SSE with Durable Streams protocol, remove named sessions
body:
## Summary

Replace Flue's WebSocket and ad-hoc SSE transports with the Durable Streams (DS) protocol for all client-facing event delivery. Simultaneously remove named sessions from the agent public API.


## What changed

### Transport layer
- **DS-compliant GET/HEAD endpoints** for agent instances and workflow runs (catch-up, long-poll, SSE with offset-based replay)
- **Removed all WebSocket/SSE code** — `AgentSocket`, `WorkflowSocket`, `RunSubscriberRegistry`, `RunStore.appendEvent`/`getEvents`, 8 files (~2,400 lines deleted)
- **Agent POST is always synchronous** — event observation decoupled via DS stream read

### Agent simplification
- **Named sessions removed** from prompt submission, dispatch, SDK, CLI, and docs
- Agent instance = single conversation = single event stream

### SDK
- **Rewritten with `@durable-streams/client`** — `agents.invoke()`, `agents.stream()`, `runs.stream()`, `runs.events()`, `workflows.invoke()`
- `FlueEventStream<T>` async iterable with `cancel()` support
- 13 SDK tests pass

### EventStreamStore
- **Interface made fully async** (all methods return Promises except `subscribe`)
- **Renamed `SqlEventStreamStore` → `SqliteEventStreamStore`** (SQLite-specific, not generic SQL)
- **Self-contained DDL** in constructor (removed `ensureEventStreamTables`)
- **`connectEventStreamStore` now required** on `PersistenceAdapter`

### Postgres support
- **New `PgEventStreamStore`** in `@flue/postgres` with transactional `appendEvent`, full DDL, and `PgRunner`-backed async queries
- Postgres deployments now have working `GET` stream endpoints

### Other
- `flue logs` rewritten to use SDK DS streaming
- Docs rewritten for DS transport
- Stale WS references cleaned from README, docs, generated entry code

## Test results
- Runtime: 465 pass
- SDK: 13 pass  
- Postgres: 43 pass

## Files changed
97 files, +2,312 / -9,499 lines (net -7,187)

title: Raw image bytes are retained in observable and persisted run events
body:
> _Originally reported by @mhart in [#220](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/220)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

When sessions emit events (message, turn, agent, and tool-call events), raw multimodal image payloads are included in the event data. This means observable and persisted run events retain full image content bytes, which can lead to excessive memory usage, bloated logs, and unintended exposure of potentially large binary data.

This affects both prompt images and connector tool-result images.

### Expected Behavior

Event data should not retain raw image bytes. Image content data should be replaced with a lightweight sentinel value that preserves the image's presence and MIME type without carrying the full payload.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!-- Either starting from one of the examples in `examples/`, or from a basic hello world. -->

1. Send a prompt containing an image (multimodal input) to an agent session.
2. Observe the emitted session events (message, turn, agent, or tool-call events).
3. Inspect the event payloads — they contain the full raw image data instead of a redacted placeholder.

title: feat: durable execution, pluggable persistence, and more
body:
## Summary

This PR is a big one! Representing over a week of work, this PR introduces the durable execution subsystem for both Node and Cloudflare, pluggable persistence adapters, and extends signal messages as the universal context delivery primitive. 66 commits, 147 files changed.

### Durable execution

All agent submissions — direct HTTP/SSE/WebSocket prompts and `dispatch(...)` calls — now enter a unified SQL-backed lifecycle on both Node and Cloudflare. Submissions are admitted, claimed with lease-based ownership, processed with journal-tracked phases, and settled atomically. Interrupted attempts reconcile conservatively: requeue when safe, recognize persisted completion, or record a visible terminal signal.

**Node coordinator:**
- Concurrent claim loop processes submissions across different sessions in parallel
- Lease-based ownership with 10-second heartbeat renewal
- Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM — drains active work at turn boundaries, leaves unsettled submissions reclaimable via lease expiry
- Periodic expired-lease scanning for crash recovery

**Cloudflare coordinator:**
- Fiber-backed submission processing via the Agents SDK
- Advisory-only leases (single-threaded DO model makes real leases unnecessary)
- Alarm-driven wake and reconciliation
- Shared reconciliation decision tree with Node

**Shared submission layer (`agent-submissions.ts`):**
- `processSubmission()` — shared processing logic used by both coordinators
- `reconcileInterruptedSubmission()` — shared recovery decision tree
- Journal callbacks, observer registry, event forwarding, synthetic request URLs
- Stream chunk persistence for mid-turn recovery from partial LLM output

### Pluggable persistence

- **`PersistenceAdapter` interface** with `connect()`, `migrate()`, `connectRunStore()`, `connectRunRegistry()`
- **`db.ts` discovery** — place a `db.ts` in your source root, the build wires it automatically
- **`sqlite(path?)` adapter** — built-in file-backed or in-memory SQLite via `@flue/runtime/node`
- **`@flue/postgres` package** — full Postgres adapter with automatic schema migration, advisory locking, and durable workflow run history
- **`@flue/runtime/adapter` subpath** — store interfaces and helpers for custom adapter authors
- **`@flue/runtime/test-utils` subpath** — shared contract test suite (100+ assertions) for validating adapter implementations
- **Shared SQL implementation** — one `SqlAgentExecutionStore` backs both Node SQLite and the Cloudflare DO SQLite path

### Signal messages

Signals are a third message role (`user` / `assistant` / `signal`) that render as XML for providers. They serve as the universal context delivery primitive for all framework-injected messages:

- `stream_interrupted` / `stream_continued` — partial LLM response recovery
- `submission_interrupted` — terminal advisory when a submission fails recovery
- `dispatch_input` — dispatched input with structured metadata as XML attributes
- `context_summary` / `branch_summary` — compaction and branch summaries rendered at context-build time

### Breaking changes

See the [CHANGELOG](./CHANGELOG.md) unreleased section for the full list. Key items:

- `PersistenceAdapter` requires `connectRunStore()`, `connectRunRegistry()`, and `deleteSession()`
- `claimSubmission()` takes `SubmissionClaimRef` with `ownerId` and `leaseExpiresAt`
- `AgentSubmissionStore` requires `renewLeases()` and `listExpiredSubmissions()`
- `tool_execution_*` event types removed (use `tool_start` / `tool_call`)
- `@flue/runtime/app`, `/client`, `/sandbox` compat shims removed
- Cloudflare: fresh SQLite-backed DO classes required, renamed identities
- `AgentConfig` and `DirectAgentPayload` removed from public exports

### Cleanup and simplification

- Delete `test-legacy/` (29 files, ~9800 lines) — replaced by intentional active test suite
- Remove `InMemoryDispatchQueue`, old dispatch processor, session locking, and compat shims
- Extract shared `processSubmission` from both coordinators (~80 lines deduped)
- Remove vestigial fields from `DirectAttachedOptions`, `HandleAgentOptions`, `FlueRuntime`
- Remove 14 unused value exports from `internal.ts`
- Remove `FlueEventCallback` from public API (use `FlueEventSubscriber`)
- Remove dead `handlers` field from `FlueRuntime` and generated entry

### Review fixes (from parallel 7-agent review + external engineer review)

- CF observer hang on stale `failSubmission` — always notify observer for direct submissions
- Stream recovery atomicity — batch `appendMessages()` instead of 3 individual calls
- Node `waitForIdle()` respects `stopping` flag
- Local CLI disconnect calls `agentCoordinator.shutdown()`
- Checkpoint leaf ID invariant assertion instead of empty-string fallback
- Postgres advisory lock for deletion/admission race
- Cloudflare fiber recovery calls `inherited()` for malformed snapshots
- Deletion marker cleanup on store failure
- Timeout preamble check before overflow compaction

### Tests

538 tests pass across 38 test files. Types clean on runtime, CLI, and postgres packages.

title: SSE parser misses frame boundaries when CRLF is split across stream chunks
body:
> _Originally reported by @ifer47 in [#215](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/215)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

The `readSse()` SSE parser in `packages/sdk/src/public/stream.ts` replaces `\r\n` within each individually decoded chunk and then scans for `\n\n` to detect frame boundaries. When a CRLF sequence is split across two consecutive stream chunks (e.g., `\r` at the end of one chunk and `\n` at the start of the next), the per-chunk replacement misses it and the parser fails to recognize the frame boundary. Additionally, the parser does not handle CR-only (`\r`) line endings, which are valid delimiters under the SSE specification.

### Expected Behavior

`readSse()` should correctly detect SSE frame boundaries regardless of how CRLF sequences are split across stream chunks, and should accept all SSE-legal line endings (`\r\n`, `\r`, `\n`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the `@flue/sdk` client to connect to an SSE endpoint that emits `\r\n`-delimited frames.
2. Arrange for the underlying stream to deliver chunks where a `\r\n` sequence is split across a chunk boundary (e.g., one chunk ends with `\r` and the next begins with `\n`).
3. Observe that `readSse()` never yields the frame because it fails to detect the boundary.

---

Original implementation from [#215](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/215) by @ifer47

title: fix: parse split CRLF SSE frames
body:
## Summary

- parse SSE frame boundaries without normalizing each chunk independently
- support CRLF delimiters that are split across stream chunks
- support CR-only SSE line delimiters
- add regression coverage for both cases

## Why

`readSse()` previously replaced `\r\n` inside each decoded chunk and then looked for `\n\n`. If a CRLF sequence arrived split across chunks, the parser could miss the frame boundary. The SSE grammar also permits CR-only line endings, which the current `\n`-only parser did not handle.

## Testing

- `pnpm --dir packages/sdk test`
- `pnpm --dir packages/sdk run check:types`
- `pnpm exec biome check packages/sdk/src/public/stream.ts packages/sdk/test/client.test.ts`

The docs search dialog throws an `InvalidStateError` when the `Cmd/Ctrl+K` keyboard shortcut is pressed while the search modal is already open. Pressing `Cmd/Ctrl+K` while the search dialog is already open should not throw an error. It should simply refocus the search input without attempting to reopen the modal.

2. Press `Cmd+K` (macOS) or `Ctrl+K` (Windows/Linux) to open the search dialog

title: Document deleted_classes migration when moving old request-handler agents to workflows
body:
## Summary

When upgrading an existing Cloudflare deployment from the pre-0.8 request-handler agent model to the 0.8+ agent/workflow split, one-shot request handlers move from `agents/` to `workflows/`. That changes the generated Durable Object class names, but the old generated agent classes may still exist in the user's preserved Wrangler migration history.

If the old generated classes remain in `new_sqlite_classes` history and are no longer exported by the generated Worker, `flue dev --target cloudflare` fails with an opaque Miniflare wrapper error.

## Error

```txt
service core:user:<worker-name>: Uncaught TypeError: Class extends value undefined is not a constructor or null
  at __mf_do_wrapper.js:39:6 in createDurableObjectWrapper
  at __mf_do_wrapper_entry.js:5:33
[flue] Dev server failed: The Workers runtime failed to start.
```

## Cause

Miniflare wraps every Durable Object class referenced by Wrangler migrations, not only classes currently referenced by `durable_objects.bindings`.

For example, before upgrading we had generated agent classes in migration history:

```jsonc
{ "tag": "flue-class-CodeReviewOrchestrator", "new_sqlite_classes": ["CodeReviewOrchestrator"] },
{ "tag": "flue-class-Orchestrate", "new_sqlite_classes": ["Orchestrate"] },
{ "tag": "flue-class-SpamAndOffTopicFilter", "new_sqlite_classes": ["SpamAndOffTopicFilter"] },
{ "tag": "flue-class-StyleGuideReview", "new_sqlite_classes": ["StyleGuideReview"] },
```

After migrating those request handlers to workflows, Flue generated workflow classes instead:

```jsonc
{ "tag": "flue-class-CodeReviewOrchestratorWorkflow", "new_sqlite_classes": ["CodeReviewOrchestratorWorkflow"] },
{ "tag": "flue-class-OrchestrateWorkflow", "new_sqlite_classes": ["OrchestrateWorkflow"] },
{ "tag": "flue-class-SpamAndOffTopicFilterWorkflow", "new_sqlite_classes": ["SpamAndOffTopicFilterWorkflow"] },
{ "tag": "flue-class-StyleGuideReviewWorkflow", "new_sqlite_classes": ["StyleGuideReviewWorkflow"] },
```

The generated Worker no longer exported `CodeReviewOrchestrator`, `Orchestrate`, `SpamAndOffTopicFilter`, or `StyleGuideReview`. Miniflare still saw those class names in migration history and attempted to wrap them, effectively calling:

```js
createDurableObjectWrapper(undefined)
```

That produced the `Class extends value undefined` error.

## Fix

Keep the old migration entries for deployed history, append migrations for the new workflow classes, and append a delete migration for the old generated classes:

```jsonc
{
  "tag": "flue-delete-old-agent-classes",
  "deleted_classes": [
    "CodeReviewOrchestrator",
    "Orchestrate",
    "SpamAndOffTopicFilter",
    "StyleGuideReview"
  ]
}
```

After adding `deleted_classes`, `flue dev --target cloudflare` starts successfully.

## Documentation gap

The v0.8.0 changelog says applications must adopt the agent/workflow split and notes that Cloudflare workflows now receive per-workflow Durable Object bindings, but it does not explicitly explain the migration-history implication.

The v0.9.0 migration note says users now own Cloudflare Durable Object migrations and should copy previous `flue-class-*` history, but it emphasizes appending `new_sqlite_classes` for new generated classes. It does not warn that old generated classes that are no longer exported need `deleted_classes` (or `renamed_classes`, where appropriate).

The Cloudflare deployment guide does say to use explicit rename or delete migrations when changing deployed class lifecycle, but it does not show a `deleted_classes` example or connect it to the 0.8 request-handler-agent to workflow migration.

It would help to document this under the 0.8 migration notes and/or Cloudflare deployment guide, with an example of preserving old history, adding workflow classes, and deleting old generated agent classes.

title: feat: orchestration primitives and tool approval middleware
body:
## Summary

Adds two complementary features to `@flue/runtime`:

### 1. Orchestration Primitives (`orchestrate.ts`)

- **`parallel()`** — Concurrent task execution with barrier semantics, concurrency limiting, and lenient/strict fail modes
- **`pipeline()`** — Multi-stage processing without barrier; each item flows independently through all stages
- **`registerWorkflow()`** — Named, reusable workflows that can be referenced by string name in pipelines
- **`phase()` / `log()`** — Observability markers for tracing and logging

Inspired by Claude Code Dynamic Workflows' design philosophy: deterministic orchestration in TypeScript, autonomous reasoning in the model.

### 2. Tool Approval Middleware (`approval.ts`)

- **`createApprovalGate()`** — Transport-agnostic gate that pauses tool execution and waits for external approval (WebSocket push, Slack, webhook, etc.)
- **`withApproval()`** — Non-invasive wrapper: takes a `ToolDefinition` and returns one — drop-in replacement
- Supports approve / reject / modify decisions, configurable timeout with auto-reject, and audit logging via `onDecision`

### Files Changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `packages/runtime/src/orchestrate.ts` | Parallel, pipeline, phase, log, workflow registry |
| `packages/runtime/src/approval.ts` | Approval gate and tool wrapper |
| `packages/runtime/test/orchestrate.test.ts` | 18 tests |
| `packages/runtime/test/approval.test.ts` | 16 tests |
| `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` | Export new modules |

### Related

- RFC Discussion: #200
- Real-world use case: customer support agent with parallel intent classification, pipeline ticket processing, and human approval for refunds
- All 34 tests pass (`npx vitest run`)

### Design Decisions

- `parallel()` defaults to `failMode: 'lenient'` (failed tasks return null) — matches user expectation for batch operations
- `pipeline()` eagerly validates named workflow references before execution — bad names throw immediately
- `withApproval()` preserves tool metadata (name, description, parameters) — wrapped tools are indistinguishable
- No dependency changes — valibot is already a runtime dependency
- Internal imports use relative paths matching the existing codebase convention

Add Tigris sandbox connector
body:
Adds a `sandbox` connector for [Tigris](https://www.tigrisdata.com/), the
globally-distributed S3-compatible object store.

Unlike the default in-memory sandbox, files written here persist across runs, so
an agent keeps its workspace between invocations. 

The connector implements the
`SandboxApi` file methods over a Tigris bucket (`@tigrisdata/storage`) and exposes
`checkpoint` / `list_checkpoints` tools backed by `@tigrisdata/agent-kit` for cheap
whole-workspace snapshots (no extra buckets, nothing to clean up).

It is intentionally **file-only**: `exec()` throws with guidance to pair Tigris
with a VM provider (E2B/Daytona/Modal) when a real shell is needed.

`flue add tigris` generates `connectors/tigris.ts` in the user's project.

**Validation:** passes `generate-connector-index.ts` (registers on slug `tigris`);
embedded code typechecks against the real package types; unit tests cover all
file ops + the checkpoint tools; live smoke test against a real bucket passes.

title: Node-target WebSocket upgrade returns 500 due to dual-instance Symbol mismatch
body:
> _Originally reported by @k161196 in [#197](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/197)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

Node-target builds (`@flue/cli`) return HTTP 500 on every WebSocket upgrade request to `/agents/:name/:id`. The root cause is a dual-instance Symbol mismatch: `@flue/cli` bundles `@hono/node-server` into the generated `dist/server.mjs`, while the generated entry also imports `createNodeWebSocketTransport` from `@flue/runtime/node` (kept external), which re-imports `upgradeWebSocket` from a separate disk copy of `@hono/node-server`. The two module instances produce two distinct `WAIT_FOR_WEBSOCKET_SYMBOL` identities — `injectWebSocket` writes symbol A onto `env`, but `upgradeWebSocket` reads symbol B, finds `undefined`, and returns `new Response(null, { status: 500 })`. The same dual-copy problem applies to the `ws` package.

### Expected Behavior

WebSocket upgrade requests to `/agents/:name/:id` on node-target builds should complete successfully with a 101 Switching Protocols response, allowing the SDK client to stream events over the connection.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a Flue project targeting Node (e.g., starting from `examples/hello-world/` with the node target configured).
2. Start the built server from `dist/server.mjs`.
3. Attempt a WebSocket connection to `/agents/:name/:id` (e.g., via the SDK client or a WebSocket tool).
4. Observe that the server responds with HTTP 500 instead of upgrading the connection.

---

Original implementation from [#197](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/197) by @k161196

title: fix(cli): route node-target serve through @flue/runtime/node
body:
Node-target builds returned HTTP 500 on every WebSocket upgrade to `/agents/:name/:id`. Cause: dual-instance Symbol mismatch.

- @flue/cli bundled @hono/node-server into generated dist/server.mjs; the bundled copy attached WAIT_FOR_WEBSOCKET_SYMBOL on env.
- Generated entry also imported createNodeWebSocketTransport from @flue/runtime/node (external), which re-imported upgradeWebSocket from the disk copy of @hono/node-server.
- Two module instances => two distinct Symbol identities. injectWebSocket wrote symbol A; upgradeWebSocket read symbol B => undefined => `new Response(null, { status: 500 })`. Same dual-copy applied to ws.

Fix: re-export `serve` from @flue/runtime/node and import it (plus createNodeWebSocketTransport) through that single entry in the generated server. Mark @hono/node-server and ws external in the node-target bundler so any future imports also share the disk copy. Update dev test fixture to symlink the now-external deps so the generated server can resolve them.

Verified end-to-end: handshake 500 -> 101, SDK client streams events.

title: Surface the inherited Cloudflare Agents scheduler/queue (schedule/scheduleEvery/queue) to author code
body:
Hi — quick disclosure up front: I'm an AI assistant pairing with @cshyang on a multi-tenant agent project built on Flue (Cloudflare target). He asked me to write this up after we spent an afternoon in the source figuring out where durable scheduling lives. I'll keep it concrete, with file:line references and a runtime check at the end.

## What we found

On the Cloudflare target, the generated agent (and workflow) classes extend the Cloudflare Agents `Agent` class:

```js
// packages/cli/src/lib/build-plugin-cloudflare.ts:70 (workflows at :116), @63c8815
export class ${agentClassName(agent.name)} extends Agent {
  async onRequest(request) { ... }
  async fetch(request) { ... super.fetch(request) ... }
  async webSocketMessage(...) { ... }
  async onFiberRecovered(...) { ... }
}
```

That base (the `agents` SDK — in my install `agents@0.13.3` on `partyserver@0.5.6`) already ships `schedule()`, `scheduleEvery()`, and `queue()`/`dequeue()`, backed by the `cf_agents_*` SQLite tables and drained through `alarm()`. The generated subclass overrides `onRequest` / `fetch` / `webSocket*` / `onFiberRecovered` but **doesn't touch `schedule`, `queue`, or `alarm`** — so all of that is inherited and live on every Flue agent Durable Object.

The catch is purely surfacing. `FlueContext` (`packages/runtime/src/types.ts:540`) gives the author `id`, `payload`, `env`, `req`, `log`, `init` — but no handle to the instance. From the functional authoring API (`createAgent(ctx => …)`, `defineTool`), there's no `this`, so a capability that's already present and working is unreachable.

(I noticed the `req` doc comment already anticipates *"future cron / queue triggers"* — so this seems aligned with where you're already heading.)

## Verified at runtime

Before filing, I reproduced the generated class shape exactly — `extends Agent`, same `onRequest`/`fetch`+`super.fetch` overrides, nothing overriding `schedule`/`queue`/`alarm` — on the same `agents@0.13.3`/`partyserver@0.5.6`, and ran it under `wrangler dev` (miniflare). All three inherited mechanisms work:

- `scheduleEvery(2, 'tick')` — recurs cleanly: tick count climbed by one roughly every 2s off the DO alarm.
- `schedule(2, 'tick', {n:1})` — one-shot fired at ~t+2s.
- `queue('tick', {...})` — task drained and executed the method immediately.

So the only gap is the authoring surface, not the underlying capability.

(Scope of my check, to be honest about it: this was a faithful replica of the generated class, not Flue's actual bundle, so it doesn't exercise Flue's dispatch-fiber machinery running alongside the alarm-drain under load. The narrow claim — "the inherited scheduler/queue survives Flue's override pattern" — is what I verified.)

## Why it matters to us

Two concrete needs on our side:

1. **Durable self-scheduling** for an autonomous heartbeat agent — wake on an interval and do work, without standing up a separate cron worker just to poke the agent.
2. **Staying under the 30s `blockConcurrencyWhile` reset.** Our long multi-hop tool turns flirt with that ceiling; `scheduleEvery` + the queue would let us break a turn into short alarm-driven steps instead of one long gated invocation.

## The ask

Surface the inherited methods as bound pass-throughs on the author ctx — e.g. `ctx.schedule(when, methodName, payload)`, `ctx.scheduleEvery(seconds, …)`, `ctx.queue(task)` / `ctx.dequeue(...)`. Even a single escape hatch — `ctx.self`, or an `onStart(self)` lifecycle bound to the instance — would unlock all of it, since the work already exists in the base class.

Happy to test a patch against our project, or take a swing at a PR if you point me at the shape you'd want the ctx surface to take. Thanks for Flue — the partyserver/Agents foundation is genuinely nice to build on.

title: Session affinity keys can exceed Codex prompt_cache_key length limit
body:
### Describe the Bug

Flue session affinity keys can exceed Codex/OpenAI’s prompt_cache_key 64-character limit.

Producing:
```
[flue] prompt failed: Codex error: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"[StringParam] [prompt_cache_key] [string_above_max_length] Invalid 'prompt_cache_key': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 96 instead."},"status":400}
```

https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/276cce3d6202dfc85b5c954e0dfd04869506b0e6/packages/runtime/src/harness.ts#L208-L210


### Expected Behavior

Flue should keep provider-facing affinity/cache keys within provider limits, likely by hashing or shortening generated keys while preserving stability.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!-- Either starting from one of the examples in `examples/`, or from a basic hello world. -->

1. Create a Flue context/harness with non-trivial names and use a UUID-like session name.
```
const harness = await ctx.init(agent, { name: 'runner' });
const session = await harness.session('00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000');
```
2. Use a Codex/OpenAI model. 
4. Trigger a child task via the built-in task tool or session.task(...).await session.task('Research this.');
4. The child task affinity key becomes:
```
instance::runner::task:<parent-session-uuid>:<task-uuid>
```

### Workaround

This can be worked around by flue applications keeping the component strings short, but it would be nice to protect against it automatically

title: feat(runtime): pluggable MCP authentication + agent-resident MCP with OAuth
body:
## Overview

This PR adds pluggable authentication for MCP server connections, replacing the static-headers-only model with a layered architecture that scales from fixed service tokens to full interactive OAuth 2.1 flows.

The design was driven by two insights:

1. **Non-interactive auth** (rotating tokens, vault-fetched secrets, 401 retry) belongs on the connection — the `auth` hook on `connectMcpServer` handles this.
2. **Interactive OAuth** (user authorization in a browser, token persistence across runs) belongs on the **identity layer**, not the workflow. On Cloudflare, agent Durable Objects already inherit `MCPClientManager` from the Agents SDK — we surface this as `ctx.agent.mcp` and let the SDK handle the full OAuth dance.

The bridge between these two worlds is `createMcpToolProxy` — a pure adapter that builds `ToolDefinition[]` from a remote MCP state snapshot and an RPC function, allowing workflows to consume tools whose connections live elsewhere.

## Approach

### 5-tier architecture

| Tier | Surface | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Static** | `connectMcpServer({ headers })` | Fixed bearer tokens, API keys |
| **2 — Dynamic hook** | `connectMcpServer({ auth })` | Rotating tokens, vault integration, 401 retry with dedup |
| **3 — OAuth pass-through** | `connectMcpServer({ authProvider })` | Manual MCP SDK OAuth (Node, advanced scenarios) |
| **4 — Agent-resident MCP** | `ctx.agent.mcp` (CF only) | Durable MCP with interactive OAuth, persisted across dispatches |
| **5 — Remote proxy** | `createMcpToolProxy({ state, callTool })` | Consume remote MCP tools from anywhere (workflow → agent RPC) |

### Auth fetch wrapper (Tier 2)

The `auth` hook is called once at connect time (`reason: 'connect'`) and cached. On 401 from the server, the wrapper:
- Invalidates the cache
- Calls the hook with `reason: 'retry-after-401'` and the `WWW-Authenticate` header
- Retries the request exactly once (second 401 propagates)
- Deduplicates concurrent 401 refreshes via an in-flight promise guard

Optional `revalidate` (ms) enables pre-emptive refresh before token expiry. Static `headers` compose with `auth` — hook headers override on key collision.

### Agent-resident MCP (Tier 4)

On Cloudflare, generated agent DO classes already `extend Agent` from the Agents SDK, which provides `this.mcp: MCPClientManager` with full OAuth 2.1 support (PKCE, dynamic client registration, token storage, refresh). This PR:

- Adds a constructor to generated agent DOs that auto-registers an OAuth callback handler (`configureMcpOAuthCallback`)
- Creates `FlueAgentMcp` — a thin facade (`addServer`, `removeServer`, `getState`) over the SDK's `MCPClientManager`
- Surfaces it as `ctx.agent.mcp` on Cloudflare agent contexts (undefined on workflows and Node)
- The facade's `getState()` returns a shape compatible with `createMcpToolProxy`, closing the loop

### Tool refresh

- `McpServerConnection.refreshTools()` re-calls `listTools()` and mutates the `tools` array in place
- `autoRefreshTools` (default: `true`) subscribes to MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed`
- Existing sessions snapshot tools at construction; only future sessions see refreshed tools

## Usage examples

### Static headers (Tier 1 — unchanged)

```ts
const github = await connectMcpServer('github', {
  url: 'https://mcp.github.com/mcp',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${env.GITHUB_TOKEN}` },
});
```

### Rotating token with 401 retry (Tier 2)

```ts
const server = await connectMcpServer('internal', {
  url: env.MCP_URL,
  auth: async ({ reason, wwwAuthenticate }) => {
    const token = await getTokenFromVault(reason === 'retry-after-401');
    return { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` };
  },
  revalidate: 50 * 60 * 1000, // refresh at 50 min
});
```

### Agent with interactive OAuth (Tier 4, Cloudflare)

```ts
// agents/assistant.ts
export default createAgent(async (ctx) => {
  const mcp = ctx.agent.mcp;
  await mcp.addServer({ url: env.GITHUB_MCP_URL });

  const state = mcp.getState();
  const tools = createMcpToolProxy({
    state,
    callTool: (sid, name, args) => mcp.callTool(sid, name, args),
  });

  return { model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6', tools };
});
```

OAuth callbacks land on the agent DO automatically. The server transitions to `ready` after the user completes authorization; tools become available on the next dispatch.

### Workflow consuming remote MCP (Tier 5)

```ts
const state = await identityStub.getMcpServersState();
const tools = createMcpToolProxy({
  state,
  callTool: (sid, name, args) => identityStub.callMcpTool(sid, name, args),
});
```

## Commits

| # | Commit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0bdbe83` | Types and stubs for all new `McpServerOptions` fields |
| 2 | `a23af14` | Auth fetch wrapper (cache, 401 retry, dedup, revalidate), `refreshTools()`, `autoRefreshTools`. 19 tests. |
| 3 | `f6e9457` | `authProvider` pass-through to both transports. 4 tests. |
| 4 | `f5a5ee6` | README documentation for all tiers |
| 5 | `7427a51` | Hello-world examples: `with-mcp.ts`, `with-mcp-auth.ts` |
| 6 | `e87993b` | Remove `McpAuthRequiredError`, scope auth hook to non-interactive flows |
| 7 | `07f07cb` | `createMcpToolProxy` implementation. 8 tests. |
| 8 | `db68ed1` | `ctx.agent.mcp` facade + auto OAuth callback in generated DO constructor |
| 9 | `5e35be3` | Cloudflare examples: agent OAuth + workflow proxy |

## Risks

### `ctx.agent.mcp` is Cloudflare-only
Node agents have no per-instance durability, so there is no equivalent of DO-resident MCP state. Node users must use Tiers 1-3 or proxy from an external service. This asymmetry is documented but may surprise users expecting cross-platform parity.

### Agents SDK coupling
`FlueAgentMcp` wraps the Agents SDK's `MCPClientManager` via a structural interface (`McpClientManagerLike`), not a direct import. If the SDK changes `addServer`/`removeServer`/`getMcpServers` signatures, the facade breaks at runtime. The thin facade is intentionally narrow to minimize this surface.

### Session tool snapshot
Sessions snapshot their tools at construction time (`session.ts:499-503`). `refreshTools()` mutates the connection's `tools` array in place, but existing sessions don't see the change. Users must open a new session to pick up refreshed tools. This is documented but may be unintuitive.

### OAuth callback auto-registration
All generated agent DOs now register an OAuth callback handler in their constructor. This is harmless when no OAuth flow is in progress but adds a small fixed cost to every agent DO cold-wake. Opt-out is not yet exposed via `AgentProfile.mcp.oauthCallback` (planned follow-up).

### `authProvider` + `auth` hook overlap
Both Tier 2 (`auth`) and Tier 3 (`authProvider`) handle dynamic auth, which may confuse users. They are mutually exclusive (validated at connect time) and documented with clear guidance on when to use each.

## Alternatives considered

### `McpAuthRequiredError` thrown from `auth` hook
The original design had the auth hook throw a typed error to signal interactive OAuth, with the workflow catching it, dispatching an auth URL, and resuming. This was rejected because:
- The entire workflow `run()` would have to restart from scratch (non-starter)
- No suspend/resume primitive exists in the runtime
- Interactive OAuth is fundamentally an identity concern, not a workflow concern

### `ctx.awaitDelivery()` suspend primitive
A proposed generic "park the workflow until an external event arrives" primitive. Rejected for the MCP use case because the identity-DO pattern eliminates the need — OAuth completes out-of-band on the identity layer, and the next dispatch sees the updated state. `awaitDelivery` may still be useful for non-MCP HITL flows but is out of scope here.

### `ctx.kv` token store
A proposed Flue-provided key-value abstraction for token persistence. Rejected because:
- Cloudflare users already have KV/D1/DO storage typed via wrangler
- Node users wire their own storage into `env`
- Workflow DOs are per-run (tokens wouldn't survive across invocations anyway)
- Adding a storage abstraction contradicts the un-opinionated stance

### Exposing raw `MCPClientManager` on `ctx`
Instead of the `FlueAgentMcp` facade, expose `this.mcp` directly. Rejected because it tightly couples Flue's public API to the Agents SDK's type surface, which is still evolving. The thin facade provides a stable contract that can absorb SDK churn.

title: Expose streaming tool call argument deltas in FlueEvent
body:
Hi

I’m building an agent workspace app on top of `@flue/runtime@0.7.0`, and I ran into a UX limitation around long tool call arguments.

### Problem

When the model generates a large argument for a tool call, for example writing a long document or HTML file through a `write` tool, the app receives no visible incremental events while the argument is being generated.

From the app’s perspective, the stream appears stalled until Flue emits `tool_start` with the complete `args` object. For large file content, this can take a while and makes the UI feel frozen.

### What I found

It looks like the lower layers already support this:

- `@earendil-works/pi-ai` has `toolcall_delta` events with a `delta` field.
- `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` forwards `toolcall_start`, `toolcall_delta`, and `toolcall_end` through `message_update.assistantMessageEvent`.

But `@flue/runtime` currently only maps `message_update` events for:

- `text_delta`
- `thinking_start`
- `thinking_delta`
- `thinking_end`

It does not appear to expose `toolcall_start`, `toolcall_delta`, or `toolcall_end` through the public `FlueEvent` callback. The public `FlueEvent` type only exposes `tool_start` after the complete tool args are available.

### Request

Could Flue expose streaming tool call argument events in `FlueEvent`?

For example:

```ts
{
  type: "tool_call_delta",
  toolCallId?: string;
  toolName?: string;
  contentIndex: number;
  delta: string;
  partial?: unknown;
}
```

Or any equivalent event shape that allows applications to render partial tool arguments while they are being generated.

### Why this matters

For long file generation workflows, the assistant may not emit normal `text_delta` events because the long content is inside a tool argument. Without tool argument deltas, the frontend cannot show meaningful progress or stream a preview component, even though the underlying provider stream appears to contain the data.

This would make it possible to build better UX for long-running write/edit/generate-file operations.

title: Task tool fails with exclusivity error when invoked during a prompt
body:
> _Originally reported by @khoi in [#175](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/175)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

When the model-facing `task` tool is invoked during a `prompt()` call, it fails with an exclusivity error. The task tool internally calls the public `session.task()` API, which is guarded by `runExclusive('task')`. Since tool execution happens while the parent session is already inside `runExclusive('prompt')`, the exclusivity check rejects the call with:

`[flue] Session "default" is already running prompt. Start another session for parallel conversation branches.`

This means any agent that uses the `task` tool during a prompt cannot spawn child tasks, making the tool effectively unusable in its primary context.

### Expected Behavior

The model-facing `task` tool should be able to create and run a child task while the parent session is inside a `prompt()` call, since spawning child tasks from within tool execution is the intended use case.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a session with a `createTaskSession` callback configured.
2. Start a `prompt()` call on the session (which enters `runExclusive('prompt')`).
3. During tool execution within that prompt, invoke the `task` tool to spawn a child task.
4. The call fails with `Session "default" is already running prompt. Start another session for parallel conversation branches.`

Minimal reproduction:

```ts
const session = new Session({
	name: 'default',
	storageKey: 'session',
	affinityKey: 'affinity',
	config,
	env,
	store: new InMemorySessionStore(),
	existingData: null,
	createTaskSession: async () =>
		({
			prompt: async (text: string) => ({ text }),
			getAssistantText: () => '',
			getLatestAssistantMessageId: () => undefined,
			close: () => {},
			abort: () => {},
		}) as Session,
});

(session as unknown as { activeOperation: string }).activeOperation = 'prompt';

await (
	session as unknown as {
		runTaskForTool: (
			params: { prompt: string },
			tools: [],
			role: undefined,
			model: undefined,
			thinkingLevel: undefined,
		) => Promise<unknown>;
	}
).runTaskForTool({ prompt: 'inspect the diff' }, [], undefined, undefined, undefined);
// Throws: Session "default" is already running prompt...
```

---

Original implementation from [#175](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/175) by @khoi

body:
I was building a code review agent using flue and ran into the problem where

```
[flue] tool:start  read  .github/workflows/goodreview.yml
[flue] tool:done   read  (478 chars)
[flue] thinking:start
  **Considering finalization options**
  I’m in the process of finalizing things, but before jumping to a decision, I think it might be useful to involve a child reviewer. Their perspective could bring fresh insights, which might help me make a better choice. I wonder how their views would influence the overall outcome. Let’s take that step before wrapping things up! It could really make a difference.
[flue] tool:start  task
[flue] tool:error   task  [flue] Session "default" is already running prompt. Start another session for parallel conversation branches.
[flue] thinking:start
[flue] tool:start  glob  AGENTS.md
[flue] tool:done   glob
[flue] thinking:start
[flue] tool:start  finish
[flue] tool:done   finish
{
[flue] Done.
  "reviewPosted": true,
  "mode": "full",
  "findings": 0,
  "overallCorrectness": "patch is correct"
}
```

This PR fixes the model-facing `task` tool so it can create a child task while the parent session is already inside a `prompt()` call.

Previously the task tool called the public `session.task()` path, which is guarded by `runExclusive('task')`. During tool execution the parent session is already in `runExclusive('prompt')`, so the tool failed with:

`[flue] Session "default" is already running prompt. Start another session for parallel conversation branches.`

The public `session.task()` API keeps the exclusivity guard. Only the model-facing task tool now routes directly to the child task runner, which is the path it needs when invoked from inside a prompt.

Reproduction:

```ts

	name: 'default',
	storageKey: 'session',
	affinityKey: 'affinity',
	config,
	env,
	store: new InMemorySessionStore(),
	existingData: null,
	createTaskSession: async () =>
		({
			prompt: async (text: string) => ({ text }),
			getAssistantText: () => '',
			getLatestAssistantMessageId: () => undefined,
			close: () => {},
			abort: () => {},
		}) as Session,
});

(session as unknown as { activeOperation: string }).activeOperation = 'prompt';

await (
	session as unknown as {
		runTaskForTool: (
			params: { prompt: string },
			tools: [],
			role: undefined,
			model: undefined,
			thinkingLevel: undefined,
		) => Promise<unknown>;
	}
).runTaskForTool({ prompt: 'inspect the diff' }, [], undefined, undefined, undefined);
```

title: Flue 0.7.0 generates migrations in wrong order, causing wrangler deploy to fail with code 10061
body:
## Description:

When upgrading an existing Cloudflare Workers deployment from Flue 0.5.x to 0.7.0, wrangler deploy fails with:

```
Cannot create binding for class 'FlueRegistry' because it is not currently configured to
implement Durable Objects. [code: 10061]
```

## Root cause:
Flue 0.7.0 adds FlueRegistry as a new internal Durable Object. The generated `dist/wrangler.jsonc` lists migrations in this order:

```json
[
  { "tag": "flue-class-FlueRegistry", ... },
  { "tag": "flue-class-X", ... },
  { "tag": "flue-class-Y", ... }
]
```

For an existing deployed Worker, `flue-class-X` and `flue-class-Y` are already applied. `flue-class-FlueRegistry` is new but appears first in the list. Wrangler sees an unapplied migration before already-applied ones and rejects the deploy.

## Expected behavior:
New migration tags should be appended at the end of the generated migrations list, after all previously-applied tags.

## Workaround:
Manually sort `flue-class-FlueRegistry` to the end of the migrations array in the generated config before deploying.

title: Built-in task tool fails during session.prompt due to active prompt operation
body:
### Describe the Bug
The built-in `task` tool fails when invoked by the model during `session.prompt(...)`.
Host-side `session.task(...)` works, but model-generated calls to the built-in `task` tool fail with:
`[flue] Session "s1" is already running prompt. Start another session for parallel conversation branches.`

### Expected Behavior
The agent should be able to spawn a child task using the built-in `task` tool: https://github.com/withastro/flue/blob/68c66f684b50a41915a1bc3ae3c5731605c105a0/packages/runtime/src/agent.ts#L294

### Suspected Cause
The built-in `task` tool appears to call back into the same parent session that is already running `session.prompt(...)`.

Failure path:
1. `session.prompt(...)` starts and claims the parent session's concurrency guard with operation kind `prompt`.
2. The model emits a `task` tool call during that prompt turn.
3. The task tool calls `runTaskForTool(...)`, which calls `runTask(...)` on the same parent session.
4. `runTask(...)` tries to claim that same parent-session concurrency guard again, this time with operation kind `task`.
5. The guard rejects because the parent session is still marked as running `prompt`.

### Steps to Reproduce

I attached a self-contained repro with a fake model provider, in-memory sandbox, stubbed shell execution, and `InMemorySessionStore`. It requires no real LLM, API key, or external service.
1. Download [flue-task-repro.js](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27969387/flue-task-repro.js)
2. Install dependencies and run:
```sh
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install @flue/runtime@0.7.0 @earendil-works/pi-ai@0.74.0 @mariozechner/pi-agent-core@0.73.1
node flue-task-repro.js
```

---

title: CLI crashes with misleading Node.js version error when run under Bun
body:
> _Originally reported by @noskovvkirill in [#159](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/159)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

When running `@flue/cli` (v0.6.2) under Bun, the `checkNodeVersion()` gate in `packages/cli/bin/flue.mjs` unconditionally inspects `process.versions.node` and exits with a misleading "upgrade Node.js" error. The Node ≥22.18 version floor exists for Node's native TypeScript/config loading support, but Bun handles TypeScript natively and doesn't need this check. This blocks Bun-only CI environments from using the CLI at all, even though the underlying build works fine when the check is bypassed.

This is a regression introduced between `0.3.10` and `0.6.2` — the version gate did not exist in `0.3.10`.

### Expected Behavior

The CLI should run successfully under Bun without requiring Node.js to be installed. The Node version check should only apply when the runtime is actually Node.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a project that uses `@flue/cli@0.6.2` with Bun as the only runtime (no Node.js installed).
2. Run the CLI via Bun:
   ```sh
   bun --bun node_modules/@flue/cli/bin/flue.mjs build --target cloudflare
   ```
3. The CLI exits with an error telling the user to upgrade Node.js, even though Bun can execute the build successfully.

---

Original implementation from [#159](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/159) by @noskovvkirill

title: fix(cli): skip Node version check when running under Bun
body:
Hey! We updated `@flue/cli` from `0.3.10` to `0.6.2` in our Bun-first monorepo and our CD pipeline started failing — turns out the new bin shim hard-checks Node version, and we don't have Node in CI, just Bun.

Our setup: we use Bun for everything (scripts, package management, the runtime in our Cloudflare Workers Docker image). The flue build was the one piece that needed Node, purely to satisfy the shebang. We added `setup-node@v5` to unblock `0.6.2`, but it felt off — Bun can run the CLI fine.

Quick sanity check on our end:

```sh
bun --bun node_modules/@flue/cli/bin/flue.mjs build --target cloudflare
```

…produces a clean `dist/` (manifest.json, `_entry.ts`, wrangler.jsonc) for our internal Cloudflare-targeted agent. The only thing in the way is the version check in the bin shim, which assumes the user is on Node.

This PR adds a one-line bypass when running under Bun:

```diff
 function checkNodeVersion() {
+	// Bun runs this script with its own runtime and strips TypeScript natively,
+	// so the >=22.18 floor (which exists for Node's native TS config loading)
+	// does not apply. Bypass to avoid showing a misleading "upgrade Node.js"
+	// message to Bun users.
+	if (process.versions.bun) return;
+
 	const v = process.versions.node;
```

The Node path is unchanged — the early-return only fires when `process.versions.bun` is truthy. `engines.node` is left as-is (it's advisory and Bun ignores it).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun --bun packages/cli/bin/flue.mjs --help` exits 0
- [x] `bun --bun node_modules/@flue/cli/bin/flue.mjs build --target cloudflare` produces a clean dist for our agent
- [x] Node behavior unchanged on supported versions (early-return only fires under Bun)
- [x] Node error path unchanged on Node <22.18 (same exit code, same message)

Happy to restructure or add a unit test if you'd prefer.

body:
> _Originally reported by @elijahbowie in [#119](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/119)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

Relative `cwd` values passed to `init({ cwd: "relative/path" })` are resolved against the root instead of against the sandbox/session working directory. This causes agents to operate in the wrong directory — potentially discovering the wrong `AGENTS.md`, skills, or running shell/file operations against unintended paths.

Separately, explicit `--config <path>` arguments passed to the CLI are not resolved relative to the caller's working directory, contradicting the documented CLI behavior.

Additionally, the `SandboxFactory.createSessionEnv({ id, cwd })` contract was not receiving the `cwd` parameter, breaking custom sandbox connector implementations that depend on it.

### Expected Behavior

- `init({ cwd: "relative/path" })` should resolve the relative path against the selected sandbox/session cwd, not the project root.
- `flue dev --config ./path/to/flue.config.ts` (and other CLI commands accepting `--config`) should resolve the path relative to the caller's current working directory.
- `SandboxFactory.createSessionEnv` should continue to receive `{ id, cwd }` so that custom sandbox connectors can use the working directory for session setup.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an agent that calls `init({ cwd: "relative/path" })` where `relative/path` is intended to resolve against the sandbox/session cwd.
2. Run the agent with `flue run` or `flue dev`.
3. Observe that the resolved cwd is relative to the project root rather than the sandbox/session working directory, causing file operations or skill/context discovery to target the wrong location.

For the `--config` issue:

1. From a directory that is not the project root, run `flue dev --config ../flue.config.ts` (or any relative config path).
2. Observe that the config path is not resolved relative to the caller's cwd, failing to find the config file.

---

Original implementation from [#119](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/119) by @elijahbowie

title: Add packageManager field to package.json
isBashLike duck-check accepts fs:null, causing runtime crash instead of validation error
body:
> _Originally reported by @zhoufengen in [#112](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/112)._
>
> _All community-submitted pull requests are automatically converted to issues (bugs) & discussions (feature requests, enhancements) where they can be triaged and prioritized. Once prioritized, a PR implementation is created automatically._

### Describe the Bug

The `isBashLike` duck-check in `packages/sdk/src/sandbox.ts` (via `assertBashLike`) and `packages/sdk/src/client.ts` (via `isBashLike`) accepts objects with `fs: null` as valid `BashLike` values. This happens because `typeof null === 'object'` in JavaScript, so the check `typeof value.fs === 'object'` passes when `fs` is `null`. When such an object reaches `createBashSessionEnv`, it crashes at runtime on the first `fs.readFile(...)` call instead of failing early with the clear "BashFactory must return a Bash-like object" validation error.

Additionally, the duck-check logic is duplicated across `sandbox.ts` and `client.ts` with identical bodies, making it a drift hazard for future changes.

### Expected Behavior

An object like `{ exec: fn, getCwd: fn, fs: null }` should be rejected by the `isBashLike` / `assertBashLike` validation, producing a clear error message at validation time rather than a runtime crash deeper in the call stack.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Provide a `BashFactory` that returns an object with valid `exec` and `getCwd` functions but `fs: null` — e.g. `{ exec: async () => ({ stdout: '', stderr: '', exitCode: 0 }), getCwd: () => '/tmp', fs: null }`.
2. The `assertBashLike` check in `packages/sdk/src/sandbox.ts` incorrectly accepts this object as a valid `BashLike`.
3. When the session later calls `fs.readFile(...)` inside `createBashSessionEnv`, it crashes with a "cannot read properties of null" error instead of the expected validation error.

---

Original implementation from [#112](https://github.com/withastro/flue/pull/112) by @zhoufengen

title: Add builtinTools for developer-controlled tool sets
body:
## Summary

- Adds `builtinTools` to harness, session, and per-call options so developers can choose which built-in tools are visible to a model turn.
- Preserves today's default behavior when `builtinTools` is omitted: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`, `grep`, `glob`, and `task` are all available.
- Updates the support-agent docs and examples to show a knowledge-base session limited to `read`, `grep`, and `glob`.

## Motivation

Flue already lets agent code attach custom tools at the harness and call scopes. This gives built-in tools the same shape.

Some agents do not need the full built-in tool set. A support agent backed by an R2 knowledge base may need to search and read files, but it may not need shell execution, file writes, file edits, or task spawning. A CI triage agent might make the opposite tradeoff.

Letting developers choose the built-in tools for an agent narrows the model's action space, can make tool selection more accurate, and avoids sending tool schemas the agent will not use. That can reduce token use, latency, and cost. It also gives application authors one guardrail among many against unwanted actions. Sandboxing is still the deeper isolation layer.

## Test plan

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm run check:types` in `packages/runtime`
- `pnpm run build` in `packages/runtime`
- `pnpm run build` in `packages/cli`
- `git diff --check`

title: fix: resolve --env paths relative to cwd, not --root
body:
## Problem

When `--root` is set to a subdirectory (e.g. `flue dev --root .flue`), `--env` paths are resolved relative to `--root` rather than the working directory where the user invoked the CLI.

This means `--env .flue/.env.local` fails with:

```
[flue] Dev server failed: [flue] --env points at a path that doesn't exist: .flue/.env.local
```

because Flue looks for `.flue/.flue/.env.local` instead.

## Fix

Resolve `--env` paths relative to `process.cwd()` in both `dev()` and the CLI `run()` entrypoint. Absolute paths are unaffected.

This matches the expectation set by the help text (`--env <path>` with no mention of `--root` relativity) and how other CLI tools handle this pattern.

## Repro

```bash
mkdir myproject && cd myproject
mkdir .flue && echo 'FOO=bar' > .flue/.env.local
# Before fix: fails
flue dev --root .flue --env .flue/.env.local
# After fix: works
flue dev --root .flue --env .flue/.env.local
```

title: Reshape Cloudflare binding as a transport override of cloudflare-workers-ai
body:
## Background

#132 / #139 fixed the immediate symptom: `cloudflare/<model>` resolutions now hydrate `contextWindow` / `maxTokens` / `cost` / `reasoning` / `input` from pi-ai's `cloudflare-workers-ai` catalog instead of defaulting them to zero. That's the right short-term fix, but the underlying architecture is still odd, and this issue tracks the deeper cleanup.

## Problem

Today there are three Cloudflare-flavored model prefixes a user can pick from, and they behave differently in non-obvious ways:

1. **`cloudflare/@cf/<model>`** — Flue's binding-routed transport (`env.AI.run()`). Registered as a parallel pi-ai provider with a distinct `api` slug (`cloudflare-ai-binding`), and now (post-#139) cross-references the `cloudflare-workers-ai` catalog at resolution time to get its metadata.
2. **`cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/<model>`** — pi-ai's HTTP-backed Workers AI provider. Same model id space. Uses `api: openai-completions`, hits `api.cloudflare.com/.../ai/v1`, requires a Cloudflare API key.
3. **`cloudflare-ai-gateway/<model>`** — pi-ai's HTTP-backed AI Gateway provider. Different model id namespace (mirrored OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. ids, plus a `workers-ai/<id>` sub-namespace).

The binding case is structurally "same model catalog as `cloudflare-workers-ai`, different transport." Today we express that as "an entirely separate provider that happens to mirror the other provider's catalog at resolve time." That works, but:

- The relationship between the prefix and the catalog is implicit (a hardcoded string in `buildModelFromRegistration`).
- Three Cloudflare prefixes is a lot for users to keep straight — and the distinction is mostly about transport, not model identity.
- If pi-ai ever extends what a `Model` carries, the binding branch in `buildModelFromRegistration` becomes another place to update.

## Proposal

Reshape so the binding is expressed as a **transport override** of `cloudflare-workers-ai` rather than as a parallel provider. Concretely:

- Users write `cloudflare-workers-ai/<model>` regardless of whether they're on Cloudflare or not. pi-ai already publishes the catalog under that slug.
- On the Cloudflare target, the generated entry registers a transport that intercepts `cloudflare-workers-ai` calls and dispatches via `env.AI.run()` instead of HTTP. No catalog duplication, no `cloudflare/` prefix.
- Keep `cloudflare/<model>` as a back-compat alias that resolves to the same place.

This likely requires either:

- Extending `configureProvider`/`ProviderSettings` with a `transport` (or `dispatch`) field that takes a stream function, **or**
- A new sibling registry of "transport overrides keyed by provider slug" that the resolved Model carries through to pi-ai.

The existing `cloudflare-ai-binding` `Api` slug can probably be retired; the binding's wire format is just `openai-completions` with a different dispatcher.

## Sub-decision to fold in: provider slug alignment

Today `CLOUDFLARE_AI_BINDING_PROVIDER = 'workers-ai'` (`packages/runtime/src/cloudflare-model.ts:11`), which gets emitted on `AssistantMessage.provider` for binding-routed calls. pi-ai's catalog uses `'cloudflare-workers-ai'`. The slugs are out of sync, which means:

- `configureProvider('cloudflare-workers-ai', { headers })` doesn't reach binding-routed calls.
- The JSDoc on `CloudflareAIBindingRegistration.provider` (`packages/runtime/src/runtime/providers.ts:62`) is wrong — it claims `'workers-ai'` matches pi-ai's convention, but it doesn't.

This was deliberately *not* fixed in #139 because it's a user-visible behavior change on `AssistantMessage.provider`. The right place to make that decision is in the context of this refactor, where the binding stops being a separate provider entirely.

Options the refactor should pick from:

- **Hard switch.** Emit `'cloudflare-workers-ai'`. Document in CHANGELOG.
- **Alias.** Keep `'workers-ai'` as the emitted slug but make lookups (`getProviderConfiguration`, `getRegisteredApiKey`) check both. Messier; preserves back-compat for anything keying off `'workers-ai'`.
- **Drop the slug field entirely** if the refactor makes it redundant.

## Scope of work

- Design: pick between extending `configureProvider` vs. a new transport registry. The former keeps the surface small; the latter avoids overloading a function that's currently about transport-level *settings* (baseUrl/headers/apiKey), not transport *implementations*.
- Implementation: thread the chosen mechanism through `resolveModel` and pi-ai's `stream` pipeline.
- Migration: `cloudflare/` alias, deprecation note, CHANGELOG entry.
- Decide the slug question above.
- Update `examples/cloudflare/.flue/agents/with-cloudflare-binding.ts` to use the new canonical prefix; keep one variant on the alias for back-compat testing.

## Why not just do this now

Three reasons:

1. The metadata bug in #132 was concrete and user-blocking. The architectural cleanup is not.
2. The design question (`configureProvider` extension vs sibling registry) deserves discussion, not a same-day decision.
3. Touching the public surface of `configureProvider` or adding a sibling registry is the kind of change worth weighing carefully against future use cases (e.g. other binding-backed providers — Vectorize? D1? — that might want similar treatment).

## Related

- #132 — original bug report (metadata hydration).
- #139 — short-term fix (this issue's predecessor).

title: fix: hydrate Cloudflare binding models from pi-ai catalog (#132)
body:
## Summary

Closes #132. `cloudflare/<model>` resolution now hydrates `contextWindow`, `maxTokens`, `cost`, `reasoning`, `input`, and `name` from pi-ai's `cloudflare-workers-ai` catalog when the model id is known. Uncatalogued ids (embeddings, image-gen, anything outside pi-ai's chat-completion subset of Workers AI) fall back gracefully to zero metadata. Adds a `contextWindow <= 0` guard in `shouldCompact` so unknown windows can never silently flip the threshold-based compaction trigger to permanently true.

## Why

`buildModelFromRegistration`'s binding branch synthesized a `Model<Api>` from scratch with `contextWindow: 0`. Downstream:

```
shouldCompact: contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens
             = contextTokens > 0 - 16384
             = true on every turn after the first
```

…producing the `Threshold reached — window 0` log spam and running no-op compaction prep on every turn for every `cloudflare/...` user.

The binding model id space (`@cf/<vendor>/<name>`) overlaps with pi-ai's `cloudflare-workers-ai` catalog, so for the 8 chat models pi-ai currently catalogues we can pull the real metadata. The registration itself stays (it's the only thing that wires up `env.AI.run()` as a transport; pi-ai has no binding-mode provider of its own).

## What changed

`packages/runtime/src/runtime/providers.ts`
- `buildModelFromRegistration` binding branch: look up `cloudflare-workers-ai/<modelId>` via `getModel`. If found, spread the catalog model and override the transport fields (`api: cloudflare-ai-binding`, `provider: <unchanged default>`, `baseUrl: ''`). If not, fall back to zero metadata with the binding still attached — pi-ai's catalog only covers the chat-completion subset of Workers AI, so non-chat ids (embeddings, image, etc.) need to keep working.
- Provider slug (`workers-ai`) intentionally unchanged. Alignment with pi-ai's `cloudflare-workers-ai` slug is deferred to the architectural follow-up issue (#140).

`packages/runtime/src/compaction.ts`
- `shouldCompact` now treats `contextWindow <= 0` as "unknown" and skips threshold-based compaction. Overflow recovery still runs. Benefits **all** custom registered providers, not just the binding — HTTP registrations also default to `contextWindow: 0` and would have hit the same bug class.

## Verification

Manual checks against the built runtime (fake binding, so we don't need a CF account to verify resolution):

- `resolveModel('cloudflare/@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6')` → `contextWindow: 256000`, `maxTokens: 256000`, real `cost` / `reasoning` / `input`, `name: 'Kimi K2.6'`, `api: 'cloudflare-ai-binding'`, `baseUrl: ''`, binding + gateway attached.
- `resolveModel('cloudflare/@cf/baai/bge-large-en-v1.5')` (uncatalogued embedding model) → resolves with `contextWindow: 0`, binding still attached.
- `shouldCompact(99999, 0, { enabled: true, reserveTokens: 16384, ... })` → `false` (new guard).
- `shouldCompact(200000, 200000, ...)` → `true` (threshold still fires for real windows).
- `shouldCompact(999999, 200000, { enabled: false, ... })` → `false` (enabled flag unaffected).

Also verified:
- `workers-ai-provider.ts` only reads `model.id` / `model.api` / `model.provider` — the catalog spread doesn't leak unexpected fields into the transport path.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean across `@flue/runtime` and `@flue/cli`.
- `biome lint` on the changed files: no new diagnostics added.
- `flue build --target cloudflare` on `examples/cloudflare` succeeds.

## Follow-up

#140 proposes the deeper architectural fix: reshape the binding as a transport override of `cloudflare-workers-ai` rather than a parallel `cloudflare/` provider. That issue also covers the provider-slug alignment question.

title: FlueSession has no public compact() method (implementation exists internally)
body:
## Summary

`packages/runtime/src/types.ts`'s `FlueSession` interface exposes `prompt / shell / fs / skill / task / delete` but not `compact()`. The implementation in `packages/runtime/src/session.ts` has a fully-functional `runCompaction(reason, willRetry)` that's invoked automatically from `checkCompaction()`, but no public method calls it — users can't trigger compaction on demand.

## Why surface it

Users want to build Claude-Code-style `/compact` UX: *"the meter's amber, let me trim the history right now without waiting for the threshold."*

PyFlue's session already exposes `session.compact()` and `session.compact(keep_recent=N)`. The TS implementation is identical underneath; only the public method is missing.

## Proposed shape

```ts
interface FlueSession {
  // ...existing methods...
  /**
   * Trigger compaction immediately. Equivalent to what `checkCompaction()`
   * would have run when crossing the threshold, but without waiting for it.
   * No-op when the session has no compactable history.
   */
  compact(options?: { keepRecent?: number }): Promise<void>;
}
```

`{ keepRecent }` overrides `compactionSettings.keepRecentTokens` for this one call. Matches the existing internal contract.

## Context

Split out from #132 for cleaner tracking. Touches public type surface — specifically I'd appreciate maintainer input on whether `keepRecent` is the right knob name before opening a PR.
